BURHAN:v1p100/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p100/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p100/r6.claim: The ending إلى بني إسرائيل in Aal Imran is counted by analogy with similar endings in al-A'raf, al-Shu'ara, and al-Sajda.
BURHAN:v1p100/r6.anchor: ومنها ﴿ إلى بني إسرائيل ﴾ بآل عمران حملا على ما فى الأعراف والشعراء والسجد

TABATABAI:12:36-38/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:36-38/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:36-38/r1.claim: If the pronoun in ‘its interpretation’ refers to the food, Joseph offers to disclose its nature and outcome before it arrives, a prophetic sign like Jesus’ foretelling what people eat and store; some Imami reports support this reading.
TABATABAI:12:36-38/r1.anchor: ويؤيد هذا المعنى بعض الروايات الواردة من طرق أهل البيت عليهم السلام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r1.claim: Color adjectives usually follow أفعل, with verbs on فعل يفعل and verbal nouns most often on فعلة; some dialects vary.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r1.anchor: أما الألوان فإنها تبنى على أفعل ويكون الفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r2.claim: Color terms also show alternatives such as صدئ يصدأ and غبس/أغبس; غبسة follows the pattern of الحمرة.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r3.claim: Colors often form verbs and verbal nouns on إفْعال; frequent forms like احمر and اخضر shorten, while the underlying pattern remains.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r3.anchor: واعلم أنهم يبنون الفعل منه على افعال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r4.claim: Sībawayh relates الصهوبة to أرعن/رعونة and explains البياض and السواد as color terms paired like morning and evening.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r4.anchor: وقالوا البياض والسواد كما قالوا الصباح والمساء لأنهما لونان بمنزلتهما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r5.claim: Some colors use forms such as جون and ورد; their verbal nouns can follow أفعل, while خصيف/أخصف shows another pattern and means blackish green.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r5.anchor: وقد جاء شيء منه على فعيل وذلك خصيف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r6.claim: Afʿal adjectives also describe diseases and defects, with verbs on فعل يفعل and verbal nouns on فعل; the verse's al-akmah and al-abraṣ fit this class.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r6.anchor: وقد يبنى على أفعل ويكون الفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r7.claim: The feminine of an أفعل adjective is فعلاء; Sībawayh lists disease and defect pairs such as أعور/عوراء and آدر.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r7.anchor: واعلم أن مؤنث كل أفعل صفة فعلاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r8.claim: أميل is irregular beside مال يميل; the expected verbal noun is ميل, by analogy with الأصيد and صيد يصيد صيدا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r8.anchor: وقالوا مال يميل وهو مائل وأميل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r9.claim: Forms such as أشيب/أشمط and أشعر/أجرد express related meanings with different adjective and verb patterns; أزب is also used for hairy.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r9.anchor: وقالوا شاب يشيب كما قالوا شاخ يشيخ

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r10.claim: هوج يهوج and ثول يثول form adjectives and verbal nouns for madness, following the same adjective-building pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايبنىعلىأفعل)#673/r10.anchor: وقالوا هوج يهوج هوجا وهو أهوج

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r1.claim: رسول may be an adjective meaning “sent,” on the فعول pattern like صبور and شكور.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r1.anchor: صفة بمعنى مرسل فهو صفة على فعول كالصبور والشكور

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r2.claim: رسول may also be a verbal noun meaning “message”; the anonymous cited poem uses برسول in this sense.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r2.anchor: بسر ولا أرسلتهم برسول أي: برسالة، وقال آخر:

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r3.claim: A second anonymous poem likewise uses رسولا for a message delivered to Abu Salma.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r4.claim: On one interpretation, the Qur’anic رسول means bearer of a message from the Lord of the worlds.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r4.anchor: على أحد التأولين، أي: إنا ذوا رسالة رب العالمين

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r5.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r5.claim: If رسول is an adjective, it may coordinate with يعلمه, itself read as a circumstantial phrase coordinated with وجيها.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r6.claim: The Sheikh calls that parse weak because it depends on the already weak coordination of ويعلمه with وجيها across a long separation.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهو مبني على إعراب " ويعلمه " ، وقد بينا ضعف إعراب

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows رسول to coordinate with كهلا, the circumstantial phrase attached to يكلم.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r7.anchor: جوز ذلك ابن عطية. واستبعده الشيخ

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r8.claim: The Sheikh considers coordination with كهلا remote because of the long distance between the coordinated terms.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r8.anchor: استبعده الشيخ لطول الفصل بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r9.claim: The author rejects this parse on meaning: it would make Jesus speak to people as their messenger before he became a messenger, years later.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r9.anchor: وهو إنما صار رسولا بعد ذلك بأزمنة

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r10.claim: A future circumstantial state can be allowed when unambiguous, as in the falcon example and 39:73; the default circumstantial state is simultaneous.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r10.anchor: الأصل في الحال أن تكون مقارنة، ولا تكون مقدرة إلا حيث لا لبس

SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r11.claim: Another parse supplies the suitable verb ونجعله because رسول cannot coordinate directly with the preceding teaching objects; examples elide verbs before faith, spear, water, and eyes.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49/r11.anchor: تقديره: ونجعله رسولا، لما رأوه لا يصح عطفه

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r1.claim: The omitted-verb examples continue with implied “believe” before faith, “carry” before spear, “water” before cold water, and “apply kohl to” before eyes.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r1.anchor: أي: واعتقدوا الإيمان، ومعتقلا رمحا، وسقيتها ماء باردا، وكحلن العيون

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r2.claim: A fourth parse supplies a verb derived from رسول, itself governed by an omitted speech verb attributed to Jesus.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r2.anchor: منصوبا بإضمار فعل من لفظ " رسول " ، ويكون ذلك الفعل معمولا لقول مضمر

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari proposes supplying أرسلت under implicit speech: Jesus says he was sent as a messenger who came with the message and affirms earlier scripture.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r3.anchor: ما قاله الزمخشري، قاله رحمه الله

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r4.claim: Alternatively رسول and مصدقا imply speech, yielding “uttering that I have come to you” and affirming what came before.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r4.anchor: فيهما معنى النطق، فكأنه قيل: وناطقا بأني قد جئتكم

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r5.claim: The elisions reconcile the prior third-person pronouns with first-person pronouns in these phrases and make the syntax and meaning consistent.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r5.anchor: من المنصوبات لا يصح عطفه عليه في الظاهر

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r6.claim: The Sheikh rejects the two-elision proposal as weak and redundant: an omitted saying and أرسلت are unnecessary when رسول already means messenger.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا الوجه ضعيف؛ إذ فيه إضمار شيئين: القول ومعموله

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r7.claim: The Sheikh prefers the third parse because it requires only one omitted verb and lets أني قد جئتكم complement رسول as speech on the majority reading.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r7.anchor: واختار الشيخ الوجه الثالث قال: " إذ ليس فيه إلا إضمار فعل يدل عليه المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r8.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash makes رسول a circumstantial phrase from the object of ويعلمه, assuming و is redundant.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r8.anchor: قاله الأخفش، وهذا على أصل مذهبه

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r9.claim: The author calls redundant و a weak position in keeping with al-Akhfash’s grammatical doctrine.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#2/r9.anchor: وهذا على أصل مذهبه من تجويزه زيادة الواو، وهو مذهب مرجوح

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r1.claim: If رسول is a verbal noun, it may be a direct object coordinated with the second object of يعلمه, meaning Jesus is taught the message too.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r1.anchor: عطفا على المفعول الثاني ليعلمه أي: ويعلمه الكتاب ورسالة

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r2.claim: If رسول is a verbal noun, it may instead function as a circumstantial verbal noun, with the familiar interpretation of رجل عدل.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r2.anchor: أنه مصدر في موضع الحال، وفيه التأويلات المشهورة في: رجل عدل

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r3.speaker: اليزيدي
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r3.claim: Al-Yazidi reads رسول in the genitive, and al-Zamakhshari links it to بكلمة as two objects of glad tidings; the author finds the long separation awkward but sees no clearer parse.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r3.anchor: قرأ اليزيدي: " ورسول " بالجر، وخرجها الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r4.claim: إلى بني إسرائيل may be governed by رسول, whose verb takes إلى, or may be an omitted adjective modifying رسول.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r4.anchor: يتعدى بإلى، والثاني: أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه صفة لرسولا

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r5.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r5.claim: The majority opens the hamza of أني; a genitive parse deletes ب, making the phrase dependent on رسول, as al-Khalil and al-Kisaʾi hold.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r6.speaker: سيبويه والفراء
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r6.claim: For the open-hamza reading, Sibawayh and al-Farraʾ parse أني accusative after deleting the preposition ب.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r7.claim: Another accusative parse supplies يذكر, with the phrase left as its complement after its modifying phrase for رسول is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r7.anchor: فيذكر صفة لرسولا، حذفت الصفة وبقي معمولها

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ allows أني as an accusative substitute for رسول when رسول is a verbal noun direct object; the author finds this semantically remote.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r8.anchor: جوزه أبو البقاء وهو بعيد في المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r9.claim: A third parse gives the open-hamza phrase nominative as predicate of an omitted subject: هو أني قد جئتكم.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r10.speaker: بعض القراء
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r10.claim: Some reciters break the hamza; one parse supplies omitted قول with a circumstantial قائلا, retaining its complement.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r10.anchor: قرأ بعض القراء بكسر هذه الهمزة وفيها تأويلان

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r11.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r11.claim: The Kufans explain the broken hamza by taking رسول as “speaker,” embedding the meaning and syntax of saying.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#3/r11.anchor: أعطي حكم القول، وهذا مذهب الكوفيين

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r1.claim: بآية may be an omitted-predicate circumstantial phrase describing Jesus as coming accompanied by a sign, or attach directly to the coming.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r1.anchor: جئتكم ملتبسا بآية. والثاني: أنها متعلقة بنفس المجيء

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r2.claim: من ربكم may modify آية through an omitted عند, with من marking figurative origin, or may attach directly to the coming.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ estimates the circumstantial meaning as “advancing with a sign”; the author accepts this semantically but not as formal syntax.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r3.anchor: بقوله: محتجا بآية، إن عنى من جهة المعنى صح

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r4.claim: For grammatical ellipsis, the author says only an absolute existential verb is supplied, not the specific verb محتجا.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r4.anchor: لم يضمر في هذه الأماكن إلا الأكوان المطلقة

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r5.claim: The majority reads آية in the singular in both occurrences; Ibn Masʿud reads آيات in the plural both times.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r5.anchor: قرأ الجمهور: " بآية " بالإفراد في الموضعين، وابن مسعود

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r6.speaker: نافع
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r6.claim: Nafiʿ breaks the hamza of أني أخلق; the other readers open it.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r6.anchor: قرأ نافع بكسر الهمزة، والباقون بفتحها

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r7.claim: With Nafiʿ’s reading, the phrase may follow an omitted saying, resume independently, or explain what the sign is; explanatory usage remains linked to آية, unlike pure resumption.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r7.anchor: على إضمار القول أي: فقلت: إني أخلق

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r8.claim: The explanatory reading is illustrated by 3:59, where خلقه من تراب explains the likeness, and 5:9, where لهم مغفرة explains the promise.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r9.claim: With the majority’s open hamza, the phrase may substitute for أني قد جئتكم or for آية as a statement that is itself a sign.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r10.claim: Alternatively it may be predicate of an omitted subject هي, answering the implied question, “What is the sign?”
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r10.anchor: الثالث: أنها خبر مبتدأ مضمر تقديره: هي أني أخلق

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r11.claim: A final parse supplies أعني as its governing verb, likewise answering the implied question about the sign.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#4/r11.anchor: منصوبة بإضمار فعل، وهو أيضا جواب لذلك السؤال

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r1.claim: لكم attaches to أخلق; the lām expresses purpose: securing the audience’s faith and ending denial, since people themselves are not ends but their actions are.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r1.anchor: واللام للعلة، أي: لأجلكم بمعنى: لتحصيل إيمانكم

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r2.claim: من الطين attaches to أخلق and marks starting material; calling من explanatory is lax because no prior phrase needs clarification.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r3.claim: The preferred parse makes the comparison an adjective of an omitted object: Jesus creates an object whose form resembles a bird’s form.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r3.anchor: أحدها: أنها نعت لمفعول محذوف تقديره: أني أخلق لكم هيئة مثل هيئة الطير

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r4.claim: هيئة can be a verbal noun transferred to its result, like خلق for created thing, or a noun for a thing’s state; verbal nouns include التهيؤ and التهيئة.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r4.anchor: وإما اسم لحال الشيء، وليست مصدرا

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r5.claim: The root هاء الشيء يهيء describes something arranged and settled in a particular state; the Qur’an uses يهيئ لكم in 18:16.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r5.anchor: هاء الشيء يهيء هيئا وهيئة إذا ترتب واستقر

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r6.claim: طانه الله على كذا and variant طامه mean God fashioned him that way, with ن replaced by م; blowing is familiar usage.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r6.anchor: طانه الله على كذا وطامه بإبدال النون ميما

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r7.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash treats kaf itself as the direct object because he regards it as a noun wherever it occurs; other grammarians allow this only under necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r7.anchor: وهذا رأي الأخفش، يجعل الكاف اسما حيث وقعت

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r8.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi, transmitting from Abu ʿAli, parses kaf as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, “a creating like a bird’s form.”
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r8.anchor: قاله الواحدي نقلا عن أبي علي بعد كلام طويل

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r9.claim: The author objects that the challenge concerns the created result, not creating itself, unless the verbal noun means its object, returning to the first parse.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r9.anchor: لأن التحدي إنما يقع في أثر الخلق، وهو ما ينشأ عنه

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari paraphrases أخلق as أقدر, clarifying that human “creation” here means measuring or shaping.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#5/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " إني أقدر لكم شيئا مثل هيئة الطير "

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r1.claim: The anonymous poetic line uses يخلق for estimating or fashioning, not origination, which is exclusive to God.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r1.anchor: إذ ليس المراد الاختراع فإنه مختص بالباري تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r2.speaker: الزهري
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri reads كهية by moving the hamza’s vowel to yāʾ, a form the author calls eloquent.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r2.anchor: وقرأ الزهري: " كهية " بنقل حركة الهمزة

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r3.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads كهيئة الطائر in place of كهيئة الطير.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r4.claim: The pronoun فيه has six proposed antecedents: kaf; هيئة understood as a shaped thing; an omitted object; the created thing implied by أخلق; the comparison sense of kaf; or clay.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r4.anchor: في هذا الضمير ستة أوجه، أحدها: أنه عائد على الكاف

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r5.claim: On the هيئة parse, the pronoun is masculine by sense (“thing shaped”), despite the feminine word; 4:8 similarly returns منه to القسمة meaning the divided property.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r6.claim: Other parses return فيه to the omitted object, the created result implied by أخلق, or the comparison sense of kaf.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r6.anchor: أنه عائد على ذلك المفعول المحذوف أي: فأنفخ في ذلك الشيء

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r7.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r7.claim: Abu ʿAli returns the pronoun to the comparison sense of kaf, with kaf describing an omitted verbal noun: creating a creation like a bird’s form.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r7.anchor: قاله الفارسي وقد تقدم الكلام معه في ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ returns فيه to الطين; al-Wahidi objects that the blowing is into fashioned clay, not the general clay mentioned earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r8.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء. وهذا الوجه قد أفسده الواحدي

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r9.claim: The author counters that من may partitivize the clay, allowing the pronoun to refer to that portion; al-Wahidi instead takes من as marking origin, which the author calls more apparent.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r9.anchor: بل المراد بعضه، ولذلك أدخل عليه

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r10.claim: The Sheikh mentions a rare فأنفخها reading; feminine agreement refers to an omitted هيئة or to kaf by its feminine sense, as in 5:110.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#6/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وقد قرأ بعض القراء: " فأنفخها " أعاد الضمير

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r1.claim: The feminine reading omits في: an unnamed poet’s نائحة did not rise for someone, and al-Nabigha’s line means “blows into the coal.”
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r1.anchor: ما شق جيب ولا قامتك نائحة ولا بكتك جياد عند إسلاب

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r2.claim: Al-Nabigha’s phrase ينفخ الفحما omits في, meaning “blows into the coal,” just as the feminine reading omits its preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r2.anchor: يريد: ولا قامت عليك، وينفخ في الفحم

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ transmits فأنفخها as rare; al-Kashshaf attributes it to ʿAbd Allah, a detail the author says al-Farraʾ omitted.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r4.claim: يكون may be complete, with طيرا circumstantial, or incomplete with طيرا as predicate; the author prefers incomplete syntax because a bare species noun is awkward as a circumstantial.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ says يكون means يصير and permits complete or incomplete syntax; with طائرا the first has a circumstantial and the second a predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r5.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " فيكون " أي: يصير، فيجوز

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r6.claim: The author says complete كان needs no “become” sense: grammarians mean حدث or وجد; صار meaning “become” is defective.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r6.anchor: النحويون إنما يقدرون التامة بمعنى حدث ووجد وحصل

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r7.speaker: نافع ويعقوب
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r7.claim: Nafiʿ and Yaʿqub read فيكون طائرا here and in 5:110; the remaining readers have طيرا in both places.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r8.claim: The singular can mean each thing Jesus breathes into becomes a bird; omission of alif in the codex is permissible, as 6:38 writes طير for recited طائر.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#7/r8.anchor: الرسم الكريم إنما هو " طير " دون ألف

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r1.claim: One explanation of Nafiʿ’s singular is that Jesus created only one kind of bird, the bat; another says each form he breathes into becomes a bird, like the distributive “eighty lashes” in 24:4.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r2.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r2.claim: For the majority’s طيرا, al-Akhfash regards طير as a plural form like ركب, صحب, and تجر; Sibawayh calls these collective nouns rather than explicit plurals.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r2.anchor: جمع راكب وصاحب وتاجر وهو الأخفش

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#8/r3.claim: The majority reading may mean the bird species, one bird, or many; the author favors it for matching من الطير and the written form and sense.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r1.claim: On Nafiʿ’s طائرا reading, بإذن الله may modify طائرا; with collective طيرا it is an adjective of the bird phrase through an omitted relation, meaning enabled by God.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r1.anchor: وهذا على قراءة نافع، وأما على قراءة غيره فلا يتعلق به

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ attaches the phrase to يكون; this appears only if كان is complete, while attachment to a defective verb is disputed.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r3.claim: وأبرئ coordinates with أخلق, so it remains within the scope of أني.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r4.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿi assigns برئت من المرض to Tamim and برأت to the Hijaz; al-Raghib infers both vowels apply to illness, while debt and sin take fatḥa only.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r4.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: " برئت من المرض لغة تميم وبرأت لغة الحجاز "

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r5.claim: The forms include أبرأت someone from illness or debt, برأتك from debt with doubled rāʾ, and برئت من المرض for recovery; البراءة means escaping a disliked thing, as do التبري and البرء.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r5.anchor: أبرأت زيدا من العاهة ومن الدين

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r6.claim: الأكمه can mean one born blind, from كمه يكمه; the author cites Ruʾba’s line using the word.

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r7.speaker: الزمخشري والراغب
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and al-Raghib define الأكمه as one born with eyes extinguished; al-Zamakhshari says Qatada was the only such person in this community.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري والراغب وغيرهما: " الأكمه من ولد مطموس العين "

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r8.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r8.claim: Al-Raghib also allows الأكمه for someone whose eyes were lost, citing Suwayd’s line كمهت عيناه.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r8.anchor: وقال الراغب: " وقد يقال لمن ذهبت عينه

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r9.claim: البرص is the familiar disease of white patches, also called الوضح; Arabs particularly recoiled from it, and the author gives its root verb.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r9.anchor: والبرص داء معروف وهو بياض يعتري الإنسان، ولم تكن العرب تنفر من شيء

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r10.claim: The report وكان بها وضح illustrates الوضح; an Arab king was called الوضاح because people avoided calling him الأبرص, and the moon is also called أبرص for whiteness.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r10.anchor: والوضاح من ملوك العرب هابوا أن يقولوا له الأبرص

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r11.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r11.claim: Al-Raghib attributes the moon’s name أبرص to its spot, but the author objects that the spot is black.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r11.anchor: وقال الراغب: " للنكتة التي عليه " وليس بظاهر، فإن النكتة التي عليه سوداء

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r12.claim: The lizard is called سام أبرص because of its whiteness; تبريص describes a gleam resembling the shine of leprosy.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#9/r12.anchor: والوزغ: سام أبرص لبياضه، والتبريص: الذي يلمع لمعان البرص

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r1.claim: ما in both clauses may be a relative noun, verbal-noun particle, or indefinite noun with adjective; only the noun options need a resumptive pronoun, unlike the particle for most grammarians.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r1.anchor: أن تكون موصولة اسمية أو حرفية أو نكرة موصوفة

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r2.claim: The four miraculous acts use imperfect verbs to signal that Jesus performed them repeatedly whenever asked.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r2.anchor: وأتى بهذه الخوارق الأربع بلفظ المضارع دلالة على تجدد ذلك كل وقت طلب منه

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r3.claim: The creation miracle is explicitly restricted to God’s permission because it is extraordinary and could suggest divinity; the healing clause omits the phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r3.anchor: لأنه خارق عظيم، فأتى به دفعا لتوهم الإلهية

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r4.claim: The resurrection miracle is also restricted to God’s permission; the unqualified knowledge report signals its predecessor’s greatness and dispels mistaken divine attribution, which the author prefers over ellipsis of the qualifier.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r4.anchor: منبهة على عظم ما قبله ودفعا لوهم من يتوهم فيه الإلهية

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r5.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r5.claim: The general reading is تدخرون, from تذتخرون, an iftiʿāl form of ذخر meaning to hide or store; an anonymous poem uses ذخر for something stored, like الأكل for what is eaten.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r5.anchor: وأصله تذتخرون تفتعلون من الذخر وهو التخبئة

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r6.claim: In the poem, ذخر is an action noun meaning the thing stored; some grammarians misread it as ووخز, and الثعالي and أرانيها mean foxes and rabbits.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r6.anchor: الذخر: فعل بمعنى المذخور نحو: الأكل بمعنى المأكول

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r7.claim: The sound change from تذتخرون to تدخرون changes the form’s ت to د beside ذ, then assimilates ذ into د.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r7.anchor: أبدلت تاء الافتعال دالا مهملة فالتقى بذلك متقاربان: الذال والدال

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r8.speaker: السوسي
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r8.claim: Al-Susi, in a transmission from Abu ʿAmr, reads تذدخرون, changing ت to د without assimilation; it is permissible though assimilation is more eloquent.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r8.anchor: قرأ السوسي في رواية عن أبي عمرو

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r9.speaker: الزهري ومجاهد وأبو السمال وأيوب السختياني
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r9.claim: Al-Zuhri, Mujahid, Abu al-Sammal, and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani read تذخرون, using the simple verb ذخرته, “I stored it”; Arabic also has ادخر with emphatic ذال.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#10/r9.anchor: وقرأ الزهري ومجاهد وأبو السمال وأيوب السختياني " تذخرون " بسكون الذال

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ gives an alternate derivation: تذتخرون changed ت to د to approach ذ, then ذ changed to د and assimilated; في بيوتكم attaches to تدخرون.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r1.anchor: والأصل في تدخرون: تذتخرون، إلا أن الذال مهجورة والتاء مهموسة

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r3.claim: ذلك points to all the preceding miracles, using a singular demonstrative for a plural sense understood as everything mentioned; ʿAbd Allah’s reading has plural لآيات.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r3.anchor: وأشير إليها بلفظ الأفراد وإن كانت جمعا في المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r4.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r4.claim: The ʿAbd Allah codex and reading have لآيات in the plural, reflecting the plural sense of the miracles.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r4.anchor: في مصحف عبد الله وقراءته: " لآيات " بالجمع مراعاة لما ذكرته

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r5.claim: The closing sentence may be spoken either by Jesus or by God.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r5.anchor: تحتمل أن تكون من كلام عيسى وأن تكون من كلام الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r6.claim: The conditional apodosis is omitted: if they believe, they benefit from the sign and reflect on it.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r6.anchor: جوابه محذوف أي: إن كنتم مؤمنين انتفعتم بهذه الآية وتدبرتموها

SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r7.claim: The Sheikh proposes an omitted adjective, “beneficial,” for آية so the condition links to it; the author says no adjective is needed for that link.
SAMIN-DURR:3:49#11/r7.anchor: قال الشيخ: " حتى يتجه التعلق بهذا الشرط "

ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r5.claim: One possible accusative analysis supplies an omitted verb: and He makes him a messenger to the Children of Israel.
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما ويجعله رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل

ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r6.claim: Zajjāj prefers coordinating rasūlan with speaking: Jesus speaks as a messenger, as confirmed by his announcement that he brought a sign from God.
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r6.anchor: والاختيار عندي - والله أعلم - ويكلم الناس رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل والدليل على ذلك أنه قال: (أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم).

ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r7.claim: Reading innī with kasra is also sound as a direct statement that he came with a sign proving his messengership.
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r7.anchor: ولو قرئت إني قد جئتكم - بالكسر - كان صوابا، المعنى إني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم - أي بعلامة تثبت رسالتي.

ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r8.claim: The clause may be genitive as an apposition to āya: he came with the sign that he creates from clay.
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r8.anchor: يصلح أن يكون خفضا ورفعا، - فالخفض على البدل من (آية) المعنى جئتكم بأني أخلق لكم من الطين

ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, the clause explains what the sign is: Jesus tells them that he creates a bird-like form from clay.
ZAJJAJ:v1p412#2/r9.anchor: وجائز أن يكون "إني أخلق لكم من الطين" يخبرهم بهذه الآية ما هي أي أقول لكم أني أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير.

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r1.claim: In fīhi, the masculine pronoun follows al-ṭīn; in 21:91 the feminine fīhā follows al-hayʾa, the form.
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r1.anchor: فيه للفظ الطين، وقال في موضع آخر (فتنفخ فيها فتكون طيرا بإذني) للفظ الهيئة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r2.claim: Al-akmah is someone born blind; an anonymous rajaz line is cited with the word al-akmah.
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r2.anchor: (الأكمه) الذي يولد أعمى. قال الراجز هرجت فارتد ارتداد الأكمه

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r3.claim: Mā may be a relative pronoun for what you eat and store, or form verbal nouns for your eating and storing; the relative-pronoun analysis is better.
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r3.anchor: فجائز أن تكون (ما) ههنا في موضع الذي. والمعنى أنبئكم بالذي تأكلونه وتدخرونه، ويجوز أن يكون " ما " وما وقع بعدها بمنزلة المصدر. المعنى أنبئكم بأكلكم وادخاركم والأول أجود.

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r4.claim: Exegetical reports gloss what they store as the food they keep from the morning meal.
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r4.anchor: ومعنى تدخرون: جاء في التفسير: ما تأكلون في غدوكم.

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r5.claim: The form is reported with either dāl or dhāl: taddakhirūn or tadhakhirūn.

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r6.speaker: بعض النحويين
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r6.claim: Some grammarians prefer dāl because tāʾ assimilates into dhāl in forms like tadhakkarūn; dāl is an intermediate voiced consonant.
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r6.anchor: وقال بعض النحوين إنما اختير تدخرون لأن التاء تدغم في الذال نحو تذكرون، فكرهوا تذخرون لأنه لا يشبه ذلك، فطلبوا حرفا بين التاء والذال فكان ذلك الحرف الدال.

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r7.speaker: الخليل
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r7.claim: Al-Khalīl defines voiced consonants as firmly articulated so breath cannot flow, and voiceless consonants as weaker articulation with airflow.
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r7.anchor: وهي فيما زعم الخليل ضربان: فالمهجورة حرف أشبع الاعتماد عليه في موضعه، ومنع النفس أن يجري معه، والمهموس حرف أضعف الاعتماد عليه في موضعه وجرى معه النفس.

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r8.claim: Taddakhirūn derives from tadhakhirūn; since dhāl is voiced and tāʾ voiceless, tāʾ changes to voiced dāl, then the first dhāl assimilates into dāl.
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r8.anchor: وإنما قيل (تدخرون) وأصله تذخرون: أي يفتعلون من الذخر، لأن الذال حرف مجهور لا يمكن النفس أن يجري معه لشدة اعتماده في مكانه والتاء مهموسة، فأبدل من مخرج التاء حرف مجهور يشبه الذال في جهرها وهو الدال.

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r9.claim: The cluster tadhdakhirūn undergoes ordinary assimilation of the first consonant into the second; unreplaced tadhkharūn is also permissible.
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r9.anchor: فصار تذدخرون. ثم أدغمت الذال في الدال، وهذا أصل الإدغام أن تدغم الأول في الثاني، وتذخرون جائز

ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r10.claim: Zajjāj rejects the objection that tadhkharūn would be confused with another form; it is not ambiguous.
ZAJJAJ:v1p413/r10.anchor: فأما ما قال في الملبس فليس تذخرون ملبسا بشيء.

ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r1.claim: One reading treats the following passage through 3:51 as part of the angel’s announcement to Mary, implying Jesus would say these words in the future.
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r1.anchor: as part of the announcement made to Mary (implying that he would thus speak in the future)

ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r2.claim: Asad prefers reading it as what Jesus later said to the children of Israel, since the narrative from 3:52 onward supports that reading.
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r2.anchor: as a statement of what, at a later time, he actually did say to the children of Israel

ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r3.claim: Asad’s reason for preferring the later speech reading is the narrative form adopted from verse 52 onward.
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n36/r3.anchor: In view of the narrative form adopted in verses 52 ff., the second of these two alternatives seems preferable.

ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r1.claim: Tayr can be a plural of ta’ir, “flying creature” or “bird,” or an infinitive meaning “flying” from tara, “he flew.”
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r1.anchor: The noun tayr is a plural of ta'ir ("flying creature" or "bird"), or an infinitive noun ("flying")

ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r2.claim: In pre-Islamic usage and the Qur’an, ta’ir and tayr often mean fortune or destiny, good or evil; Asad cites 7:131, 27:47, 36:19, and 17:13 and dictionaries including Lane.
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r2.anchor: words ta'ir and tayr often denote "fortune" or "destiny", whether good or evil

ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r3.claim: Asad reads Jesus’ parable as fashioning a soaring vision of destiny from the humble clay of people’s lives, made real through God-given inspiration, God’s leave, and faith.
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n37/r3.anchor: out of the humble clay of their lives he would fashion for them the vision of a soaring destiny

ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n38/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n38/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n38/r1.claim: Asad considers it probable that Jesus’ raising the dead metaphorically means giving new life to people spiritually dead, as in 6:122.
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n38/r1.anchor: giving new life to people who were spiritually dead

ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n38/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n38/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n38/r2.claim: If the raising of the dead is metaphorical, healing the blind and lepers similarly means inner regeneration of people spiritually diseased and blind to truth.
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n38/r2.anchor: the "healing of the blind and the leper" has a similar significance: namely, an inner regeneration

ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n39/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n39/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n39/r1.claim: The things people eat are good things enjoyed in this life, while what they store up means good deeds laid up for the life to come.
ASAD-NOTES:3:47#n39/r1.anchor: what good things you may partake of in the life of this world, and what good deeds you should lay up as a treasure for the life to come

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p237/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p237/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p237/r1.claim: Bint al-Shati endorses linguists who deny true synonyms within one language: different forms reflect distinct nuances in speakers' minds, though identical meanings can occur across dialects.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p237/r1.anchor: فأما أن يجئ في لغة واحدة فمحال أن يختلف اللفظان والمعنى الواحد، كما ظن كثير من النحويين واللغويين

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p237/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p237/r2.speaker: ابن جني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p237/r2.claim: Ibn Jinni says equally frequent forms in one speaker may reflect tribal convention or an acquired dialect; if one is rarer, it is more likely borrowed, and multiple synonyms usually come from other tribes.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p237/r2.anchor: فقال فيه "ابن جنى" في (باب الفصيح تجتمع في كلامه لغتان فصاعداً)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p4/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p4/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p4/r5.claim: One Qurʾanic pattern of shortening a verb is to signal that the action is partial or truncated; the passage lists several verb pairs as examples.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p4/r5.anchor: يحذف من الفعل إما للدلالة على الإقتطاع من الفعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p829/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p829/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p829/r1.claim: He pairs the easier verb يفعل with ordinary conception from two parents, and the harder يخلق with Jesus’s birth from a mother without a father.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p829/r1.anchor: جعل تعالى الفعل الأيسر (يفعل) مع الأمر الأيسر وهو الإيجاد من أبوين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p455/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p455/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p455/r5.claim: He gives a general rule for verb reduction: deleting part of a verb can indicate that only part of the action is meant.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p455/r5.anchor: يحذف من الفعل إما للدلالة على الاقتطاع من الفعل

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p43/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p43/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p43/r3.claim: All except Nāfiʿ open annī; al-Fārisī parses it as apposition to āya.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p43/r3.anchor: قال: كلهم قرأ: أني أخلق لكم

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p43/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p43/r4.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p43/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ reads innī with kasra; it may start a new sentence or explain the sign, like the explanatory clause after a promise.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p109/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p109/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p109/r1.claim: Kasra on in either implies a verb of saying after messenger or begins a fresh sentence without ellipsis.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p109/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن كسر أنه أضمر القول يريد ورسولا يقول إني أو يبتدئها مستأنفا من غير إضمار

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p109/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p109/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p109/r2.claim: Fatḥa makes the clause an appositive to the earlier statement that Jesus came with a sign.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p109/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن فتح أنه جعلها بدلا من قوله ﴿ أني قد جئتكم ﴾

NASHR:v1p399/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p399/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p399/r2.claim: Al-Ḥanbalī from Hibat Allāh, via Ibn Wardān, alone facilitates the hamza after alif in these two places; the other Abū Jaʿfar transmitters verify it.
NASHR:v1p399/r2.anchor: بتسهيل الهمزة بعد الألف من (كهية الطاير، فيكون طايرا)

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:5#1/r1.claim: A hamza variant changes how the glottal stop is treated in the name Isrāʾīl.
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:5#1/r1.anchor: Hamza variant — different treatment of the glottal stop in the name

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#1/r1.claim: The inna reading is an independent assertion, Indeed I, rather than subordination, shifting the syntax into direct speech.

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#2/r1.claim: A variant vocalization of the pronoun suffix is dialectal and does not alter meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#2/r1.anchor: Variant vocalization of the pronoun suffix — no semantic change, dialectal variant

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#3/r1.claim: The segment records the base canonical anni reading with the standard pronoun suffix.
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:13#3/r1.anchor: Base canonical reading with standard pronoun suffix

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:19#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:19#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:19#1/r1.claim: Assimilating hamza changes hayʾa to hayya, a phonological variant without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:19#1/r1.anchor: Assimilation of hamza: hayʾa → hayya — phonological variant, no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:20#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:20#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:20#1/r1.claim: The active participle al-ṭāʾir means the flying one, shifting from a collective species noun to a singular agent.
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:20#1/r1.anchor: shifts from collective noun (species) to singular agent

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:26#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:26#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:26#1/r1.claim: The base ṭayran reading is an indefinite singular or collective form.

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:26#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:26#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:26#2/r1.claim: The active participle ṭāʾiran emphasizes flying as an act rather than the category of bird.
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:26#2/r1.anchor: emphasizes the act of flying over the species-category

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#1/r1.claim: The base canonical reading has ḍamma on the bāʾ of buyūtikum.
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#1/r1.anchor: Base canonical reading with ḍamma on bāʾ

QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#2/r1.claim: The biyūtikum variant has kasra on the bāʾ and is a dialectal vowel variant without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:3:49:50#2/r1.anchor: Kasra on bāʾ — dialectal vowel variant, no semantic change

IBNHISHAM:v1p581/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p581/r2.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p581/r2.claim: Jesus’ signs confirm his prophethood: he forms a bird from clay and heals the congenitally blind and lepers, all by God’s permission, affirming that God is his and their Lord.
IBNHISHAM:v1p581/r2.anchor: ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم 3: 49، أي يحقق بها نبوتي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r1.claim: Qatada says al-akmah means the blind person.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وأبرئ الأكمه والأبرص ﴾ قال الأكمه الأعمى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r2.claim: Qatada says Jesus foretold what people ate from the table and what they stored from it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ﴿ وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم ﴾ قال أنبئكم بما تأكلون من المائدة وما تدخرون منها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r3.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r3.claim: A report traced to ʿAmmar b. Yasir says the table’s followers were commanded to eat without storing food; when they stored it and betrayed the command, they became swine, as in 5:115.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#3/r3.anchor: قال معمر ذكره قتادة عن خلاس بن عمرو عن عمار بن ياسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r1.speaker: رُوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r1.claim: A report says Galen lived in Jesus’ time and traveled from Rome to Syria to meet him, but died on the way.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r1.anchor: روي أن جالينوس كان في زمان عيسى، وأنه رحل إليه من رومية إلى الشام ليلقاه، فمات في طريقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r2.speaker: أئمة التفسير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r2.claim: Leading exegetes report four resurrections: Jesus’ friend Lazarus after three days, who lived until fathering a child; an old woman’s son, who rose from his bier and carried it; a tax collector’s daughter, who lived to have her child; and Sam son of Noah, raised to speak about the Ark, asking if Judgment had begun and saying its terror had turned half his hair gray despite being five hundred years old.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r2.anchor: نقل أئمة التفسير أنه أحيا أربعة: عاذر، وكان صديقا له، بعد ثلاثة أيام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r3.speaker: رُوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r3.claim: Another report says Jesus struck a corpse, grave, or skull with his staff, whereupon the person revived, spoke with him, and lived.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r3.anchor: وروي أنه في إحيائه الموتى كان يضرب بعصاه الميت، أو القبر، أو الجمجمة، فيحيي الإنسان ويكلمه ويعيش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r4.claim: An unnamed report says the revived person would die soon.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r5.speaker: الزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r5.claim: Al-Zuhrī says he heard that Jesus and his disciples reached al-Andalus, where Jesus revived a dead man who proved to be from the people of ʿĀd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r5.anchor: وروي عن الزهري أنه قال: بلغني أن عيسى خرج هو ومن معه من حوارييه حتى بلغ الأندلس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r6.claim: Many further stories describe people revived by Jesus and prayers he used; the author says God knows whether they are sound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r6.anchor: ووردت قصص في إحياء خلق كثير على يد عيسى، وذكروا أشياء مما كان يدعو بها إذا أحيا، الله أعلم بصحتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r7.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r7.claim: Al-Suddī, Ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, and Ibn Isḥāq say Jesus foretold, from childhood in school until his commission, what the children’s fathers did and what food they ate or stored, telling questioners what they had eaten the previous day and saved.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r7.anchor: قال السدي، وابن جبير، ومجاهد، وعطاء، وابن إسحاق: كان عيسى من لدن طفوليته، وهو في الكتاب يخبر الصبيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r8.claim: Another view places the disclosure after Jesus’ prophethood: after he raised the dead, people requested another sign and asked him to reveal what they ate and stored for the next day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r8.anchor: وقيل: كان ذلك بعد النبوة لما أحيا لهم الموتى، طلبوا منه آية أخرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r9.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r9.claim: Qatāda places the disclosure at the descent of the Table: Jesus had told them to eat and not hide or store its food, but after they disobeyed he exposed what they ate and kept at home as punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان ذلك في نزول المائدة، عهد إليهم أن يأكلوا منها ولا يخبأوا ولا يدخروا، فخالفوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r10.claim: The four extraordinary acts use imperfect verbs to convey renewed or continuing action; Jesus begins with creating, the greatest miracle, then healing, raising the dead, and foretelling hidden matters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r10.anchor: وأتى بهذه الخوارق الأربع مصدرة بالمضارع الدال على التجدد، والحالة الدائمة: وبدأ بالخلق إذ هو أعظم في الإعجاز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r11.claim: Jesus’ raising the dead is a miracle others also shared by God’s leave; the repeated permission clause guards against attributing divinity to him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r11.anchor: وأتى ثالثا بإحياء الموتى، وهو خارق شاركه فيه غيره بإذن الله تعالى، وكرر: بإذن الله، دفعا لمن يتوهم فيه الألوهية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r12.claim: The permission clause follows creating and resurrection, the two greatest miracles; healing and foretelling need no repetition because each is coordinated with a permission-qualified greater miracle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p165/r12.anchor: فكل واحد من الخارقين الأعظمين قيد بقوله: بإذن الله، ولم يحتج إلى ذلك فيما عطف عليهما اكتفاء بالأول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r1.claim: Mā in mā taʾkulūna wa-mā taddakhirūna is most clearly a relative pronoun, though it may be a verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r1.anchor: و: ما، في: ما تأكلون وما تدخرون، موصولة اسمية، وهو الظاهر. وقيل: مصدرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r2.claim: The majority read taddakhirūna with a doubled dāl: its form begins idtakhara, the tāʾ changes to dāl, then dhāl assimilates into dāl, like iddakar(a).
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تدخرون، بدال مشددة، وأصله: اذتخر، من الذخر، أبدلت التاء دالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r3.claim: Mujāhid, al-Zuhrī, Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, and Abū al-Sammāl read tadhkharūna, with silent dhāl and open khāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r3.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد، والزهري، وأيوب السختياني، وأبو السمال: تذخرون، بذال ساكنة وخاء مفتوحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r4.speaker: أبو شعيب السوسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r4.claim: In one report, Abū Shuʿayb al-Sūsī reads tadhdakhirūna with silent dhāl and unassimilated dāl, a permissible unreduced form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو شعيب السوسي، في رواية عنه: وما تذدخرون، بذال ساكنة ودال مفتوحة من غير إدغام، وهذا الفك جائز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r5.claim: The majority’s assimilated reading is better; one may also change dāl to dhāl and assimilate it, producing doubled dhāl in idhkhara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r5.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور بالإدغام أجود، ويجوز جعل الدال ذالا، والإدغام فتقول: اذخر، بالذال المعجمة المشددة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r6.claim: The clause is apparently part of Jesus’ speech because it is enclosed by his words, though another view makes it God’s independent statement, phrased as information but intended as rebuke.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r6.anchor: ظاهر هذه الجملة أنها من كلام عيسى لاحتفافها بكلامه من قبلها ومن بعدها، حكاه الله عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r7.claim: A second view takes the sentence as God’s own independent speech, in the form of a report but with the force of blame and reproach.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو من كلام الله تعالى، استئناف صيغته صيغة الخبر، ومعناه التوبيخ والتقريع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r8.claim: Dhālika refers to the preceding acts: forming clay into a bird, healing, reviving the dead, and foretelling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r8.anchor: وأشير بذلك إلى ما تقدم من جعل الطين طائرا، والإبراء والإحياء والإنباء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s codex has the plural āyāt; the singular reading means the generic category and can cover few or many, while the plural follows the original plurality of the signs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r9.anchor: وتقدم أن في مصحف ابن مسعود: آيات، على الجمع، فمن أفرد أراد الجنس وهو صالح للقليل والكثير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r10.claim: A deleted qualifier may mean a beneficial, guiding sign if the addressees believe, addressing future believers; if believers are addressed, the conditional wording instead steadies and encourages them, like telling a son to obey if he is truly one’s son.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p166/r10.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون ثم صفة محذوفة حتى يتجه التعليق بهذا الشرط، أي: لآية نافعة هادئة لكم إن آمنتم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān’s preferred parsing supplies an omitted “make him” and coordinates “a messenger” with “teach him.”

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r2.claim: Another analysis supplies an omitted verb of saying and coordinates Jesus’s “I was sent” with “teach him”; this works if the coordination is with an independent “teach” clause.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r3.speaker: التفتازاني
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r3.claim: Al-Taftāzānī objects when the saying is coordinated with “gives you glad tidings” or “creates,” since that joins clauses without a proper link.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r3.anchor: فقد طعن فيه العلامة التفتازاني بأنه يكون التقدير إن الله يبشرك أو إن الله يخلق ما يشاء ويقول عيسى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r4.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r4.claim: Al-Baḥr calls the saying analysis weak in all forms because it requires ellipsing both the saying and its complement when the accusative circumstantial noun suffices.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r4.anchor: وفي البحر : إن هذا الوجه مطلقا ضعيف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r5.claim: Some instead coordinate the word with the preceding circumstantial descriptions, understanding it as “a messenger speaking thus”; the person shift is then harmless.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r5.anchor: واختار بعضهم عطفه على الاحوال المتقدمة مضمنا معنى النطق فلا يضر كونها في حكم الغيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r6.claim: On the main analyses, “messenger” is an adjective like “grateful” or “patient”; the faʿūl pattern here has the sense of mufʿil.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r6.anchor: والرسول على سائر التقادير صفة كشكور وصبور وفعول هنا بمعنى مفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r7.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows “messenger” as a verbal noun, cites a poetic line using the word, and would coordinate it with “the Book” as a thing taught.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r7.anchor: كما قال أبو البقاء مثله في قوله الشاعر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the verbal-noun analysis: the adjectival sense is more immediate, and “teaching a message” is not found in Arabic usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r8.anchor: بعيد لفظا ومعنى أما الأول فلأن المتبادر الوصفية لا المصدرية وأما ثانيا فلأن تعليم الرسالة مما لا يكاد يوجد في كلامهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r9.claim: The phrase may modify “messenger” directly or describe him through an omitted phrase, meaning a messenger sent to all the Children of Israel.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r9.anchor: والظرف إما متعلق برسولا أو بمحذوف وقع صفة له أي رسولا كائنا إلى بني إسرائيل أي كلهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r10.claim: A reported explanation says Israel is singled out to indicate Jesus’s particular commission or to answer a Jewish claim that he was sent to others.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p166#3/r10.anchor: قيل : وتخصيصهم بالذكر للإيذان بخصوص بعثته

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī doubts that Jews made the claim that Jesus was sent to non-Jews; it is absent from the well-known books he has seen.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r1.anchor: ولي في نسبة هذا الزعم لبعض اليهود تردد وليس ذلك في الكتب المشهورة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r2.speaker: أكثر اليهود
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī says most Jews accuse Jesus and his mother of the gravest things.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r2.anchor: فرقة ترميه وحاشاه بأفظع ما رمت به أمه نبيها وهم أكثر اليهود

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r3.speaker: العنانية
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r3.claim: The Ananites, followers of Anan ben David, accept Jesus’s teachings and signs, say he upheld and preached the Torah as an Israelite worshipper, but deny that he was a prophet or messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r3.anchor: العنانية أصحاب عنان بن داود رأس الجالوت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r4.speaker: العنانية
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r4.claim: The Ananites say other Jews wronged Jesus by first disbelieving without understanding his claim and then killing him without understanding his purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r4.anchor: العنانية أصحاب عنان بن داود رأس الجالوت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r5.speaker: العيسوية
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r5.claim: The Isawiyya, followers of Abū ʿĪsā Isḥāq ibn Yaʿqūb al-Iṣfahānī, say a post-Mosaic messenger called the Messiah has not yet come; five messengers precede him, and their leader is one.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r5.anchor: العيسوية أصحاب أبي عيسى إسحاق بن يعقوب الاصفهاني

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī says these Jewish positions are far from the alleged claim, while allowing that its proponent may have found evidence unknown to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r6.anchor: وكل الأقوال بعيد عما ادعاه صاحب القيل بمراحل ولعله وجد ما يوافق دعواه ومن حفظ حجة على من لم يحفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r7.claim: One account says Jesus received his mission in childhood, at three years old.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r7.anchor: فقيل : في الصبا وهو ابن ثلاث سنين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r8.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r8.claim: Al-Baḥr says revelation came after Jesus reached adulthood, at age thirty, and that his prophethood lasted three years.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r9.claim: Another reported chronology gives three months and three days before Jesus was raised to heaven; the source calls the age-thirty account famous.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r9.anchor: قيل : ثلاثة أشهر وثلاثة أيام ثم رفع إلى السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r10.claim: The source reports disagreement over whether Joseph or Moses was the first prophet of the Children of Israel, and identifies Jesus as the last.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r10.anchor: وفيه أن أول أنبياء بني إسرائيل يوسف وقيل : موسى وآخرهم عيسى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r11.speaker: اليزيدي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r11.claim: Al-Yazīdī reads “messenger” in the genitive, coordinating it with “a word.”
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r11.anchor: وقرأ اليزيدي ورسولا بالجر على أنه معطوف على كلمة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r12.claim: The clause “that I have come to you” is governed by “messenger,” which carries the sense of speaking.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r12.anchor: معمول لرسولا لما فيه معنى النطق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r13.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r13.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows the clause to modify “messenger,” to stand in apposition if messenger is a verbal noun, or to predicate an omitted noun phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r13.anchor: أبو البقاء كونه معمولا لمحذوف وقع صفة لرسول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r14.claim: “With a sign” may be a circumstantial phrase meaning Jesus came bearing proof, or may attach to “I have come”; the bāʾ can mark accompaniment or transitivity.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r14.anchor: في موضع الحال أي محتجا أو متلبسا بآية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r15.claim: The indefinite ending on “a sign” magnifies the sign rather than specifying that there was only one.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r15.anchor: والتنوين للتفخيم دون الوحدة لظهور ما ينافيها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r16.claim: “From your Lord” may modify “sign” or “I have come”; in either case min marks figurative origination.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r17.claim: The address “your Lord” reinforces the duty to obey the coming commands and suits God’s role in sending Jesus to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167/r17.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة إلى ضمير المخاطبين لتأكيد إيجاب الامتثال لما سيأتي من الأوامر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r1.claim: The clause may be an appositive to أَنِّى قَدْ جِئْتُكُم or آيَةٍ, an object of an omitted أعني, or a predicate of omitted هي.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r1.anchor: أني أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير بدل من قوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r2.speaker: نافع
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r2.claim: Nafi reads إني with initial hamza kasra, treating it as a new sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع ( إني ) بكسر الهمزة على الاستئناف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r3.claim: Here creating means shaping and bringing something forth to a measured form, not originating it from nothing; the verse names its material and shape.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالخلق التصويلا والإبراز على مقدار معين لا اليجاد من العدم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r4.claim: One view takes هيئة as a verbal noun meaning what is prepared, as خلق can mean the created thing.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r4.anchor: والهيئة مصدر بمعنى المهيأ كالخلق بمعنى المخلوق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r5.claim: Another view makes هيئة a noun for a state or thing rather than a verbal noun; the verbal nouns are الهئ and التهيؤ, and هيئة is substance on one analysis, an accident on the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : إنها اسم الحال الشئ وليست مصدرا وإنما المصدر الهئ والتهيؤ

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r6.claim: هيئة is explained as a quality formed when one or more boundaries surround a body.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r6.anchor: من إحاطة الحد الواحد أو الحدود بالجسم والمعنى أني أقدر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r7.claim: Isa forms from clay, to win belief and repel denial, something prepared like a bird or a form resembling one.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r7.anchor: أني أقدر لاجل تحصيل إيمانكم ودفع تكذيبكم إياي من الطين شيئا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Hasan treats the kaf as a noun, either an object of أخلق or an adjective of an omitted object.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r8.anchor: والكاف إنا اسم كما ذهب اليه أبو الحسن في موضع نصب على المفعولية لأخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r9.claim: The majority treat the kaf as a particle attached to an omitted phrase that itself modifies the omitted object.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r9.anchor: وإما حرف كما ذهب اليه الجمهور فتتعلق بمحذوف وقع نعتا ايضا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r10.speaker: يزيد وحمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r10.claim: Yazid and Hamza read كهيئة with a doubled ya.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ يزيد وحمزة كهيئة بتشديد الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r11.speaker: ابن القاسم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Qasim relays Khalaf's report that Hamza drops the hamza and gives the ya its vowel.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r11.anchor: وكان ابن القاسم يقول : بلغني أن خلفا يقول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r12.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r12.claim: The people of Medina and Yaqub read الطائر; al-Alusi notes the same reading in al-Maida.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب الطائر ومثله في المائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r13.claim: The pronoun in فيه returns to the implied هيئة in the sense of the prepared thing, since an abstract quality cannot receive a breath.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r13.anchor: الضمير للهيئة المقدرة في نظم الكلام لكن بمعنى الشئ المهيأ

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r14.claim: The pronoun is masculine here by reference to the thing's meaning, while al-Maida uses feminine agreement with the word هيئة; the shift is clear of ambiguity.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r15.claim: Some take the pronoun to refer to the kaf as a noun, which in reality means the thing it describes.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r15.anchor: وقع في كلام غير واحد كون الضمير للكاف بناءا على أنها اسم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r16.speaker: ابن هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r16.claim: Ibn Hisham objects that treating the pronoun as referring to the kaf noun would predict an unattested expression like مررت بكالأسد.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r16.anchor: واعترضه ابن هشام بأنه لو كان كما زعموا لسمع في الكلام مررت بكالاسد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r17.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r17.claim: Others object that referring a pronoun back to the kaf is unfamiliar.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r17.anchor: وبعضهم بأن عود الضمير إليها غير معهود

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r18.claim: The result is a living, flying bird like other birds.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r18.anchor: فيكون طيرا ( حيا طيارا كسائر الطيور

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r19.speaker: المفضل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r19.claim: Al-Mufaddal reads the verb with feminine agreement, فتكون.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r20.speaker: يعقوب وأبو جعفر ونافع
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r20.claim: Yaqub, Abu Jaafar, and Nafi read طائرا instead of طيرا.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r21.claim: The phrase may modify يكون or طيرا and means by God's command; life-giving is God's act, with the breath as its occasion, not a special property of Isa or Gabriel's spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r21.anchor: والمراد بأمر الله واشار بذلك إلى أن إحياءه من الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r22.claim: God could bring life through anyone's breath if He willed, without resistance or failure.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r22.anchor: بل لو شاء الله تعالى الإحياء بنفخ أي شخص كان لكان من غير تخلف ولا استعصاء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r23.claim: The bird miracle suits Isa's own creation without a father.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r23.anchor: وفي هذه المعجزة مناسبة لخلقه من غير أب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r24.speaker: المعظم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r24.claim: The majority say the Israelites demanded the miracle obstinately, asking Isa to make a bat; after he did so, they called him a magician.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r25.claim: They singled out the bat as a highly complete sign of divine power: it has teeth, bears young, flies without feathers, has ears and milk-producing breasts, laughs, and sees only at twilight.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r25.anchor: لانه أكمل الطير خلقا وأبلغ دلالة على القدرة لأن له نابا واسنانا ويحيض ويلد ويطير بغير ريش

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r26.claim: The commonly held view is that Isa made no bird other than a bat.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r26.anchor: والمشهور أنه لم يخلق غير الخفاش

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r27.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r27.claim: Abu al-Shaykh transmits from Ibn Abbas the report that Isa's bird was a bat.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r27.anchor: وأخرجه أبو الشيخ عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r28.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r28.claim: Wahb says the bird flew while people watched and fell dead once out of sight, distinguishing it from God's unmediated creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r28.anchor: قال وهب : كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون اليه فإذا غاب عن أعينهم سقط ميتا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r29.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p167#2/r29.claim: Another view says Isa made several kinds of birds.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r1.claim: Some hold the miracle was not requested; Ibn Ishaq's report has Isa offer to make a bird to schoolboys, who doubt he can, then he shapes and breathes into clay and it flies from his hands.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r1.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى الثاني فقد أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن إسحق ان عيسى عليع السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r2.speaker: ابن إسحق
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r2.claim: In Ibn Ishaq's account, the boys carry news of the flying bird to their teacher and spread the story among people.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r3.claim: وأبرئ is coordinated with أخلق and falls under the scope of أني.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r3.anchor: الأكمة ( عطف على ( أخلق ) فهو داخل في حيز ( أني )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak's transmission from Ibn Abbas defines al-akmah as one born blind.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p168/r4.anchor: هو الذي ولد اعمى أخرجه ابن جرير من طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r1.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas describes al-akmah as one whose eye was wiped flat, whose sight did not open, and who was created without an eyeball.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r1.anchor: أنه الممسوح العين الذي لم يشق بصره ولم يخلق له حدقة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r2.claim: A report says the only person in the early Muslim community with al-akmah in this sense was Qatada ibn Diama al-Sadusi.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r2.anchor: قيل : ولم يكن في صدر هذه الأمة أكمة بهذا المعنى غير قتادة بن دعامة السدوسي

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r3.claim: Mujahid defines al-akmah as someone who sees by day but not by night.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r3.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنه الذي يبصر بالنهار ولا يبصر بالليل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r4.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r4.claim: Ikrima interprets al-akmah as a person with weak or dim eyesight.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r5.claim: The verb means that Isa cures blindness, removing al-akmah from its condition.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r6.speaker: author
