ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r6.claim: Al-abras is someone with the familiar skin disease al-wadah.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r6.anchor: والأبرص ( وهو الذي به الوضح المعروف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r7.claim: These two ailments are singled out because they were difficult cases that defeated even the numerous, highly skilled physicians of Isa's time.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r7.anchor: وتخصيص هذين الأمرين لأنهما أمران معضلان أعجزا الاطباء وكانوا في غاية الحذاقة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r8.claim: God matched each people with a miracle in the field where their expertise lay: medicine for Isa's people, magic for Moses' people, and eloquence for the Arabs.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r8.anchor: ولهذا أراهم الله تعالى المعجزة من جنس الطب كما أرى قوم موسى عليه السلام المعجزة بالعصا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r9.claim: Mentioning these cures does not rule out Isa curing other conditions; reports describe additional healings.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r9.anchor: والاقتصار على هذين الأمرين لا يدل على نفي ما عداهما لقد روى أنه عليه السلام أبرأ أيضا غيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r10.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r10.claim: Wahb says as many as fifty thousand sick people might gather for Isa; those able to reach him came, and he went to those unable to do so, treating them through prayer to God on condition of faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r10.anchor: وروى عن وهب أنه ربما اجتمع على عيسى عليه السلام من المرضى خمسون ألفا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r11.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r11.claim: Wahb says Isa's prayer addressed God as lord, mighty one, and king of heaven and earth, affirming His power and asking by His noble name and luminous face.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r11.anchor: وكان دعاؤه الذي يدعو به للمرضى والزمنى والعميان والمجانين وغيرهم اللهم أنت إله من في السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r12.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r12.claim: Wahb says reciting the prayer over a frightened or mentally ill person, or writing it and giving it to drink, can benefit them, God willing.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r12.anchor: ومن خواص هذا الدعاء كما قال وهب أنه إذا قرئ على الفزع والمجنون وكتب له وسقى منه نفع

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r13.claim: The phrase is coordinated with the predicate of أني.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r14.claim: The permission qualifier marks this extraordinary act as God's work and guards against supposing its agent divine, since reviving the dead is unlike ordinary human acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r14.anchor: وقيد الإحياء بالإذن كما فعل في الأول لأنه عظيم يكاد يتوهم منه ألوهية فاعله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r15.claim: A report says Isa revived the dead through the prayer يا حي يا قيوم.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r15.anchor: وكان إحياؤه بالدعاء وكان دعاؤه يا حي ياقيوم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r16.claim: Another report says he prayed two units, reciting al-Mulk and al-Sajda, praised God, then invoked seven names before reviving the dead.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r16.anchor: كان إذا أراد أن يحي الموتى صلى ركعتين يقرأ في الأول تبارك الذي بيده الملك وفي الثانية تنزيل السجدة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r17.speaker: البيهقي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r17.claim: Al-Bayhaqi judges the report about the two prayers and seven names not strong.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r18.claim: One report says Isa struck the dead person, grave, or skull with his staff; the person revived by God's permission, spoke, then soon died again.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r18.anchor: وقيل : إنه كان إذا أراد أن يحي ميتا ضرب بعصاه الميت أو القبر أو الجمجمة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r19.claim: Muhyi al-Sunna transmits from Ibn Abbas that Isa revived four people: Azar, a widow's son, a tax collector's daughter, and Sam son of Noah.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r19.anchor: وأخرج محي السنة عن ابن عباس أنه قال : قد أحيا عليه السلام أربعة أنفس

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r20.claim: Azar was Isa's friend; his sister sent word after he had been dead three days, and Isa prayed at his grave, whereupon he rose, lived for some time, and had a child.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169/r20.anchor: فوجدوه قد مات منذ ثلاثة أيام فقال لاخته : انطلقي بنا إلى قبره

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r1.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account, Isa revived a widow's son during his funeral procession; he sat up, came down from the bearers, carried the bier home, then lived and had a child.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r1.anchor: فمر به ميتا على عيسى عليه السلام على سرير يحمل فدعا الله تعالى عيسى فجلس على سريره

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r2.claim: The tax collector's daughter had died the previous day; Isa prayed for her, she revived, lived for some time, and had a child.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r2.anchor: ماتت له بنت بالأمس فدعا الله تعالى واحياها وبقيت زمانا وولد لها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r3.claim: Sam son of Noah emerged from his grave after Isa invoked God's greatest name; half his hair had turned gray from fear of the Hour, and he asked whether it had come.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r3.anchor: فخرج من قبره وقد شاب نصف رأسه خوفا من قيام الساعة ولم يكونوا يشيبون في ذلك الزمان

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r4.claim: When Isa told Sam the Hour had not come, Sam agreed to die only if God protected him from death's agonies; Isa prayed and this was granted.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r4.anchor: قال : بشرط أن يعيذني الله تعالى من سكرات الموت فدعا الله تعالى له ففعل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r5.claim: Some reports say the Jews had argued Isa revived only the recently dead, perhaps merely unconscious people, so he revived Sam, dead for over four thousand years; Sam called him a prophet, some believed, and others called it magic and demanded a sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r5.anchor: إنك تحي من كان قريب العهد من الموت ولعلهم لم يموتوا بل أصابتهم سكتة فأحي لنا سام بن نوح

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r6.claim: Other reports say Isa revived a king's son to succeed him and also revived a fawn, sheep, and cow.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r6.anchor: وقد ورد أيضا أنه عليه السلام أحيا ابن ملك ليستخلفه في قصة طويلة وأحيا خشفا وشاة وبقرة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p169#2/r7.claim: The word الموتى encompasses all of these reported cases.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r1.claim: ما in both clauses is either a relative pronoun or an indefinite noun described by a clause, with its pronoun omitted; the house phrase modifies its verb, with no تنازع.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r1.anchor: ( ما ) في الموضعين موصولة أو نكرة موصوفة والعائد محذوف أي تأكلونه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r2.claim: ادخار means hiding or storing something away.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r3.claim: The underlying form is تذتخرون; its ta changes to dhal, then dhal to dal and assimilates, with some Arabs instead changing ta to dal and assimilating.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r3.anchor: ( وأصل ) تدخرون تذتخرون بذال معجمة فتاء فأبدلت التاء ذالا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r4.claim: Some reports place Isa's foretelling after his prophethood and reviving the dead.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r4.anchor: وقد كان هذا الإخبار بعد النبوة وإحيائه الموتى عليه السلام على ما في بعض الأخبار

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r5.speaker: عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r5.claim: Ibn Asakir transmits from Abdullah ibn Amr that as a boy Isa told playmates what their mothers had hidden for them; when the boys checked, their mothers asked who had informed them, and they named Isa.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r5.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن عساكر عن عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص أنه قال : كان عيسى عليه السلام وهو غلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r6.speaker: عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r6.claim: In the same account, people feared Isa would influence the boys, shut them in a house, and answered his inquiry by saying they were monkeys and pigs; he prayed that they become so, and they did.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r6.anchor: فجمعوهم في بيت وأغلقوه عليهم فخرج عيسى يلتمسهم فلم يجدهم حتى سمع ضوضاهم في بيت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r7.claim: Another view places the foretelling after the descent of the table.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r7.anchor: وذهب بعضهم أن ذلك كان بعد نزول المائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r8.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r8.claim: Abd al-Razzaq and others transmit Ammar ibn Yasir's explanation that the foretelling concerned food from the table; people were told to eat and not store any, but some stored food and betrayed the condition, becoming apes and pigs.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r8.anchor: وأيد بما أخرجه عبدالرزاق وغيره عن عمار بن ياسر رضي الله تعالى عنه في الآية أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r9.claim: Al-Alusi allows that both accounts could have occurred; in any case, the apparent sense is that Isa foretold these two particular matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r9.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال : إن كل ذلك قد وقع

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r10.claim: Another view takes the examples as representative of all unseen matters; specifying familiar personal facts leaves the hearers no room to doubt.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r10.anchor: وقيل : المراد الاخبار بالمغيبات إلا أنه قد اقتصر على ذكر أمرين منها ولعل وجه تخصيص الإخبار

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r11.claim: Food and stored provisions are singled out because people devote much effort to obtaining nourishment and feel reassured by having reserves.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170/r11.anchor: والسر في ذكر هذين الامرين بخصوصهما أن غالب سعى الانسان وصرف ذهنه لتحصيل الأكل الذي به قوامه والادخار

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r1.claim: A variant reads تدخرون with dhal and without gemination.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r2.claim: ذلك refers to the four extraordinary signs just mentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r2.anchor: أي المذكور من الخوارق الأربعة العظيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r3.claim: The statement may be Isa's speech as reported by God, or God's own words spoken as rebuke.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r3.anchor: وهذا من كلام عيسى عليه السلام حكاه الله تعالى عنه وقيل : هو من كلام الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r4.claim: The singular آية may denote a genus; another reading has the plural لآيات.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r4.anchor: لآية ( أي جنسها وقرئ لآيات لكم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r5.claim: The signs clearly establish the messenger's truth because they occur without instruments or ordinary causes used by physicians and astrologers.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r5.anchor: دالة على صحة الرسالة دلالة واضحة حيث لم يكن ذلك بتخلل آلات وتوسط أسباب عادية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r6.claim: Jafr, astrology, and similar disciplined arts are not knowledge of the unseen: they depend on known principles and cosmic means; some say they yield only strong probability, far from certain unseen knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r6.anchor: ومن هنا يعلم أن علم الجفر وعلم الفلك ونحوهما لما كانت مقرونة بأصول وضوابط

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r7.claim: Revelatory knowledge is not acquired but granted by God; inspiration likewise has no material basis, only divine bestowal.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r7.anchor: وليس ذلك كالعلم بالوحي لأنه غير مكتسب بل الله تعالى يختص به من يشاء وكذا العلم بالإلهام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r8.claim: The conditional may mean if you are enabled to believe, or if you believe; in either case the omitted result is that you benefit from the sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p170#2/r8.anchor: فيه مجاز المشارقة أي إن كنتم موفقين للايمان ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى إن كنتم مصدقين وجواب الشرط على التقديرين محذوف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r5.claim: رسولاً is understood as And We make him a messenger.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r6.claim: One view says Jesus was a messenger while still a child.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r6.anchor: قيل: كان رسولا في حال الصبا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r7.claim: Another view says Jesus became a messenger only after reaching adulthood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: إنما كان رسولا بعد البلوغ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r8.claim: Joseph was the first prophet among the Children of Israel and Jesus the last.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r8.anchor: وكان أول أنبياء بني إسرائيل يوسف وآخرهم عيسى عليهما السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r9.speaker: الكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī explains the fatḥa on أني as making Jesus the object of the sending, while another explanation gives the sense by my coming with.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r9.anchor: قال الكسائي: إنما فتح لأنه أوقع الرسالة عليه، وقيل: معناه بأني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r10.claim: The sign is singular though Jesus brought several signs because they all establish one thing: the truth of his messengership.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r10.anchor: وإنما قال: بآية وقد أتى بآيات لأن الكل دل على شيء واحد وهو صدقه في الرسالة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r11.speaker: نافع والباقون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r11.claim: Nāfiʿ reads أني with a kasra as a new statement; the others read it with fatḥa, meaning by my doing so.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r11.anchor: قرأ نافع بكسر الألف على الاستئناف، وقرأ الباقون بالفتح على معنى بإني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r12.claim: Here أخلق means I shape and form, and determine the figure.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r12.anchor: {أخلق} أي أصور وأقدر {لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r13.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads كهيئة الطائر in this verse and in al-Māʾida.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r13.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر كهيئة الطائر هاهنا وفي المائدة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r14.claim: الهيئة means the formed figure, from the verb for preparing, shaping, and setting something right.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r14.anchor: والهيئة الصورة المهيأة من قولهم: هيأت الشيء إذا قدرته وأصلحته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r15.speaker: الأكثرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r15.claim: Most readers use the plural طيراً because Jesus created many birds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r15.anchor: قراءة الأكثرين بالجمع لأنه خلق طيرا كثيرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r16.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r16.claim: Medinan readers and Yaʿqūb use the singular طائراً here; in al-Māʾida they chose one bird kind because Jesus made only the bat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r16.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب فيكون طائرا على الواحد هاهنا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r17.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r17.claim: The bat was singled out as the most fully formed bird, with breasts, teeth, and menstruation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r17.anchor: لأنه لم يخلق غير الخفاش وإنما خص الخفاش، لأنه أكمل الطير خلقا لأن لها ثديا وأسنانا وهي تحيض.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r18.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r18.claim: Wahb says the bird flew while watched but fell dead from sight, distinguishing Jesus's created act from the Creator's and showing perfection belongs to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r18.anchor: قال وهب: كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون إليه فإذا غاب عن أعينهم سقط ميتا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r19.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r19.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda say الأكمه is someone born blind.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r19.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة: هو الذي ولد أعمى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r20.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r20.speaker: الحسن والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r20.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī say الأكمه means a blind person.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r21.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r21.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r21.claim: ʿIkrima says الأكمه is someone with weak or dim sight.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r22.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r22.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r22.claim: Mujāhid says الأكمه can see by day but not by night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r22.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو الذي يبصر بالنهار ولا يبصر بالليل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r23.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r23.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r23.claim: الأبرص is a person with white skin patches.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r24.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r24.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r24.claim: Jesus healed these two incurable diseases as a miracle matching the prominence of medicine in his time.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r24.anchor: وإنما خص هذين لأنهما داءان عياءان، وكان الغالب في زمن عيسى عليه السلام الطب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r25.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r25.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r25.claim: Wahb says as many as fifty thousand patients gathered in a day; Jesus went to those unable to reach him and treated them by prayer on condition of faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p39#2/r25.anchor: قال وهب: ربما اجتمع عند عيسى عليه السلام من المرضى في اليوم الواحد خمسون ألفا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r2.claim: Jesus tells them what they eat without having witnessed it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r3.claim: تدخرون means what they set aside to eat later.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r4.claim: One view says Jesus told each person what he ate the previous night, what he would eat that day, and what he had stored for supper.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: كان يخبر 58/ب الرجل بما أكل البارحة وبما يأكل اليوم وبما ادخره للعشاء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r5.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī recounts that Jesus told schoolboys what their parents did; after the parents called him a sorcerer and hid the boys, Jesus declared them pigs, and Mary fled with him to Egypt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: كان عيسى عليه السلام في الكتاب يحدث الغلمان بما يصنع آباؤهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r6.claim: Qatāda places this in the table episode: people were forbidden to cheat or save food for tomorrow, but did so; Jesus told them what they had eaten and stored, and God transformed them into pigs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p40#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: إنما هذا في المائدة وكان خوانا ينزل عليهم أينما كانوا كالمن والسلوى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p41/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p41/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p41/r1.claim: That is, what Jesus has just described is a sign for them if they believe.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p41/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى {إن في ذلك} الذي ذكرت {لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين}

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r4.claim: The accusative “messenger” may depend on an omitted “I send him as a messenger, saying…,” or coordinate with earlier predicates while implying speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r4.anchor: منصوب بمضمر على إرادة القول تقديره: ويقول أرسلت رسولا

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r5.claim: Jesus is specified as a messenger to the Children of Israel either because his mission was limited to them or to refute claims that he was sent more broadly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r5.anchor: وتخصيص بني إسرائيل لخصوص بعثته إليهم أو للرد على من زعم

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r6.claim: The phrase may be an appositive to “I came to you with a sign,” genitive as an appositive to “sign,” or nominative with “it is that I create.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r6.anchor: نصب بدل من أني قد جئتكم، أو جر بدل من آية،

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r7.claim: Akhluqu means to measure, form, and fashion something from clay in a shape like a bird.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r7.anchor: أقدر لكم وأصور شيئا مثل صورة الطير

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r9.claim: The pronoun in “into it” refers to the likeness, the shaped object, rather than the clay itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r9.anchor: الضمير للكاف أي في ذلك الشيء المماثل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r10.claim: The shaped likeness becomes a living, flying bird by God’s command, showing that Jesus does not bring it to life independently.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r10.anchor: فيصير حيا طيارا بأمر الله، نبه به على أن إحياءه

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r11.speaker: نافع
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r11.claim: Nāfiʿ reads ṭāʾiran, with alif and hamza, here and in al-Māʾida.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r11.anchor: وقرأ نافع هنا وفي المائدة «طائرا» بالألف والهمزة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r12.claim: Al-akmah may mean someone born blind or someone whose eyes have been effaced.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r12.anchor: الأكمه الذي ولد أعمى أو الممسوح العين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r13.claim: A report says thousands of sick people gathered around Jesus; he went to those unable to come and treated them only by prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r13.anchor: روي: أنه ربما كان يجتمع عليه ألوف من المرضى

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r14.claim: Repeating “by God’s permission” blocks any inference of divinity, since reviving the dead is not a human kind of act.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r14.anchor: كرر بإذن الله دفعا لتوهم الألوهية، فإن الإحياء ليس من جنس الأفعال البشرية

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r15.claim: Jesus tells them unseen circumstances about themselves that they cannot doubt.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r15.anchor: بالمغيبات من أحوالكم التي لا تشكون فيها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r16.claim: The sign benefits those enabled to believe, or those who accept truth without obstinacy; others do not benefit from miracles.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:48-49/r16.anchor: موفقين للإيمان فإن غيرهم لا ينتفع بالمعجزات

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r1.claim: “A messenger” coordinates with an implied “reciting,” or is accusative through an implied “he makes him”; Jesus is sent to the Children of Israel with the Gospel.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r2.claim: The particle of expectation introduces the sign because a messenger addresses his recipients directly and they expect a proof; “your Lord” recalls God's longstanding beneficence toward them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r2.anchor: وكان من شأن الرسول مخاطبة المرسل إليهم وإقباله بجميع رسالته عليهم اتبعه ببيان الرسالة مقرونا بحرف التوقع

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r3.claim: Al-Harali defines clay as water and earth matured to receive an imprint, and the bird's form as the arrangement of limbs perceived by sight, prepared for its intended function.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r3.anchor: هو متخمر الماء والتراب حيث يصير متهيئا لقبول وقع الصورة فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r4.claim: Al-Harali glosses blowing as forcefully sending air from its source; the mention of the process prevents anyone supposing Jesus is truly the creator.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r4.anchor: قال الحرالي : من النفخ , وهو إرسال الهواء من منبعثه بقوة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r5.claim: Nafi reads “طائرا,” describing the result as actually flying; the author notes that this makes the bird's realized motion explicit.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r5.anchor: طائرا بالفعل - كما في قراءة نافع

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r6.claim: The repeated permission removes doubt and attributes the miracle to God; the living bird recalls Adam created from dust and is even more astonishing, so Jesus's unusual birth must not lead to deification.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r6.anchor: أي بتمكين الملك الأعظم الذي له جميع صفات الكمال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r7.claim: Al-Harali says “I heal” means complete release from disease, which weakens faculties and changes their ordinary natural actions; he explains akmah as loss of sight and leprosy as a disordered bodily complexion.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r7.anchor: قال الحرالي : من الإبراء وهو تمام التخلص من الداء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r8.claim: Al-Harali connects leprosy to an abnormal temperament and corrupted phlegm that weakens the body's power to transform it into its normal color.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r8.anchor: وقال الحرالي : البرص عبارة عن سور مزاج يحصل بسببه تكرج

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r9.claim: Raising the dead restores souls to bodies; Jesus actually raised some, and his granted power over some proves the One who enabled him can raise all.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r9.anchor: لأن الذي أقدرني على البعض قادر على ذلك في الكل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
BIQAI-FULL:v2p90#2/r10.claim: Al-Hasan, as reported by al-Quda'i, relates that the Prophet called a man's dead daughter from a valley by God's permission; she emerged and chose God after her parents embraced Islam. No grading is stated.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r1.claim: He points to the story at 2:260, a report that the Prophet restored Qatada ibn Diama's eye after an arrow dislodged it, and the account that God cured Uways al-Qarni's leprosy for his kindness to his mother; no grading is given.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r1.anchor: وقصة قتادة ابن دعامة في رده صلى الله عليه وسلم عينه بعد أن أصابها سهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r2.claim: Because reviving the dead is a divine prerogative, Jesus explicitly disclaims independent divinity and attributes the deed to God's enabling; he then adds another disclosure from the unseen.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r2.anchor: ولما كان ذلك من أمر الإحياء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r3.claim: Jesus reports unseen information about what people eat and store, although he did not witness it; the home is the most private and concealing dwelling.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r3.anchor: أي من الأخبار الجليلة من عالم الغيب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r4.claim: Al-Harali derives iddikhar from dakhira, retaining something for later need; he distinguishes private saving for oneself from ihtikar, storing goods to profit in trade.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r4.anchor: قال الحرالي : من الادخار : افتعال من الدخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r5.claim: The signs show Jesus is God's servant and chosen one, not divine: he attributes them to God and acts dependently, even through supplication; they benefit those who submit to God's power and can truly believe.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r5.anchor: أي أيها المشاهدون على أني عبد الله ومصطفاه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r6.claim: He explains the address shifting between singular and plural as forestalling two objections: that only a collective could see the sign, or that it benefits just one person rather than all recipients.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p92/r6.anchor: وكذا جمع ثانيا قطعا لتعنت من قد يقول

BURSEVI:v2p30/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r1.claim: Jesus is a messenger who speaks to the Children of Israel.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r1.anchor: يجعله {ورسولا إلى بنى إسراءيل} أي : يكلمهم

BURSEVI:v2p30/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r2.speaker: بعض اليهود
BURSEVI:v2p30/r2.claim: Some Jews said Jesus was sent to a particular people; Joseph was the first Israelite prophet and Jesus the last.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r2.anchor: وقال بعض اليهود إنه كان مبعوثا إلى قوم مخصوصين وكان أول أنبياء بني إسرائيل يوسف وآخرهم عيسى عليهما السلام

BURSEVI:v2p30/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r3.claim: The clause I have come to you is governed by messenger, which carries the sense of speaking, and means Jesus came declaring it.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r3.anchor: معمول لرسول لما فيه من معنى النطق أي : رسولا ناطقا بأني قد جئتكم ملتبسا

BURSEVI:v2p30/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r4.claim: The sign is a great miracle, namely the creation of the bird and the other wonders listed next.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r4.anchor: وهي ما ذكر بعده من خلق الطير وغيره

BURSEVI:v2p30/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r5.claim: Here create means to estimate and shape, since a servant cannot create in the sense of originating and bringing things into existence.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r5.anchor: بدل من أني قد جئتكم أي : أقدر وأشكل لأنه قد ثبت أن العبد لا يكون خالقا بمعنى التكوين والإبداع

BURSEVI:v2p30/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r6.claim: For you means for your benefit: to bring you to faith and end your denial of Jesus.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r6.anchor: أي : لأجلكم بمعنى التحصيل لإيمانكم ورفع تكذيبكم إياي

BURSEVI:v2p30/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r7.claim: The pronoun in I breathe into it refers to the shaped object resembling a bird; it then becomes a living, flying bird.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r7.anchor: الضمير للكاف أي : في ذلك الشيء للكاف أي : في ذلك الشيء المماثل لهيئة الطير

BURSEVI:v2p30/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r8.claim: The qualification by God’s permission shows that God, not Jesus, creates life in the body by His power when Jesus breathes, as a miracle.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r8.anchor: أشار بذلك إلى أن إحياءه من الله تعالى لا منه لأن الله هو الذي خلق الموت والحياة فهو يخلق الحياة في ذلك الجسم

BURSEVI:v2p30/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r9.claim: When Jesus claimed prophethood and showed miracles, people demanded a bat; he shaped it from clay and breathed into it, and it flew between heaven and earth.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r9.anchor: روي أن عيسى عليه السلام لما ادعى النبوة وأظهر المعجزات طالبوه بخلق خفاش فأخذ طينا وصورة ثم نفخ فيه

BURSEVI:v2p30/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r10.speaker: وهب
BURSEVI:v2p30/r10.claim: Wahb says the bat flew while people watched and fell dead when out of sight, distinguishing created agency from God’s act.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r10.anchor: قال وهب : كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون إليه فإذا غاب عن أعينهم سقط ميتا ليتميز فعل الخلق من فعل الله

BURSEVI:v2p30/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r11.claim: The bat was requested as an especially wondrous creature: it has flesh and blood, flies without feathers, bears live young, nurses them, and has other unusual traits.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r11.anchor: قيل : إنما طلبوا خلق الخفاش لأنه أعجب من سائر الخلق ومن عجائبه أنه لحم ودم يطير بغير ريش

BURSEVI:v2p30/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30/r12.claim: Because the Quran says Jesus was born through Gabriel’s breath into Mary and Gabriel is pure spirit, Jesus’s breath became a cause of life and spirit.
BURSEVI:v2p30/r12.anchor: ولما دل القرآن على أن عيسى عليه السلام إنما تولد من نفخ جبريل في مريم وجبريل روح محض وروحاني محض فلا جرم كانت نفخة عيسى سببا للحياة والروح

BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the only person born blind in this community was Qatada ibn Diama al-Sadusi, the Quran commentator.
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري : لم يوجد في هذه الأمة أكمه غير قتادة بن دعامة السدوسي صاحب التفسير

BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r2.claim: Al-abras is a person with vitiligo, a white skin condition; when severe it cannot be cured, and Arabs especially recoiled from it.
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r2.anchor: وهو الذي به برص أي : بياض في الجلد يتطير به وإذا استحكم فلا برء له ولا يزول بالعلاج

BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r3.claim: Jesus singled out these two afflictions because physicians could not treat them, despite their great expertise in his time.
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r3.anchor: وإنما خصهما بالذكر للشفاء لأنهما مما أعيى الأطباء في تداويهما وكانوا في غاية الحذاقة في زمن عيسى عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r4.speaker: جالينوس وأصحابه
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r4.claim: Galen and his colleagues said congenital blindness was incurable, as was advanced leprosy from which a needle drew no blood.
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r4.anchor: فقال جالينوس وأصحابه إذا ولد أعمى لا يبرأ بالعلاج وكذا الأبرص إذا كان بحال لو غرزت الإبرة فيه لا يخرج منه الدم

BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r5.claim: Jesus prayed and touched the blind and the leper; the blind man saw and the leper recovered, so some believed and others dismissed it as magic.
BURSEVI:v2p30#2/r5.anchor: فرجعوا إلى عيسى وجاءوا بالأكمه والأبرص فمسح يده بعد الدعاء عليهما فأبصر الأعمى وبرىء الأبرص فآمن به البعض وجحد البعض وقالوا هذا سحر

BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r1.claim: A report says Jesus cured fifty thousand sick people in one day, treating those who came and visiting those unable to come; he healed by prayer on the condition of faith.
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r1.anchor: روي أنه أبرأ في يوم واحد خمسين ألفا من المرضى من أطاق منهم أتاه ومن لم يطق أتاه عيسى عليه السلام وكان يداويهم بالدعاء وحده على شرط الإيمان

BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r2.claim: Jesus raised his friend Lazarus, dead for three days; after Jesus prayed at his sealed rock tomb, Lazarus emerged, lived, and had a child.
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r2.anchor: أحيى العازر وكان صديقا له فأرسل أخته إلى عيسى أن أخاك العازر يموت فائته فكان بينه وبينه مسيرة ثلاثة أيام

BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r3.claim: Jesus revived a widow’s son being carried on a bier; he sat up, dressed, carried the bier home, then lived and had a child.
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r3.anchor: وأحيى ابن عجوز مر به ميتا على عيسى على سرير يحمل فدعا الله عيسى فجلس على سريره ونزل عن أعناق الرجال ولبس ثيابه

BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r4.claim: At their request Jesus revived the daughter of a tax collector who had died the previous day; she lived and bore a child.
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r4.anchor: وأحيى ابنة العاشر الذي يأخذ العشور قيل له أحيها وقد ماتت أمس فدعا الله تعالى فعاشت وبقيت وولد لها

BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r5.claim: When they argued the recent dead might only have fainted, Jesus raised Sam son of Noah; Sam said he had been dead over four thousand years and that fear of the Resurrection had turned his hair gray.
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r5.anchor: فأحيي لنا سام بن نوح فقال عيسى دلوني على قبره فخرج والقوم معه حتى انتهى إلى قبره فدعا الله تعالى بالاسم الأعظم فخرج من قبره

BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r6.claim: Sam testified that Jesus was a prophet; when asked to die again, he agreed only if God spared him death’s agony, and Jesus’s prayer secured this.
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r6.anchor: فقال للقوم صدقوه فإنه نبي فآمن به بعضهم وكذبه آخرون

BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r7.claim: Jesus told people what they had eaten and stored, including schoolchildren what their families were preparing and hiding for them.
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r7.anchor: فكان يخبر الرجل بما أكل قبل وبما يأكل بعد ويخبر الصبيان وهو في المكتب بما يصنع أهلهم وبما يأكلون ويخبأون لهم

BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r8.claim: Parents gathered the children in a house and said they were pigs; Jesus said that was what they would become, and they were transformed into pigs.
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r8.anchor: خنازير فقال عليه السلام : كذلك يكونون فإذا هم خنازير

BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r9.claim: These extraordinary signs clearly prove Jesus’s message; they benefit those who believe.
BURSEVI:v2p30#3/r9.anchor: ما ذكر من الخوارق والأمور العظام

DURR-FULL:v2p214/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts that Jesus shaped a clay bird among schoolboys, breathed into it at his Lord's permission, and it flew; the boys spread the story to their teacher and others.
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحق أن عيسى جلس يوما مع غلمان من الكتاب فأخذ طينا ثم قال: أجعل لكم من هذا الطين طائرا

DURR-FULL:v2p214/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Jesus asked which bird was hardest to create and was told the bat, described as merely flesh, so he made one.
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج أن عيسى قال: أي الطير أشد خلقا قال: الخفاش إنما هو لحم

DURR-FULL:v2p214/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the only bird Jesus created was the bat.
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إنما خلق عيسى طيرا واحدا وهو الخفاش

DURR-FULL:v2p214/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, defines al-akmah as someone born blind.
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r5.anchor: من طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس {الأكمه} الذي يولد وهو أعمى

DURR-FULL:v2p214/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r6.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas calls al-akmah a blind person whose eye has been effaced.
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r6.anchor: من طريق عطاء عن ابن عباس قال {الأكمه} الأعمى الممسوح العين

DURR-FULL:v2p214/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r7.claim: Mujahid says al-akmah sees during the day but not at night.
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد قال {الأكمه} الذي يبصر بالنهار ولا يبصر بالليل

DURR-FULL:v2p214/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r8.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r8.claim: Ikrima interprets al-akmah as someone with dim eyesight.

DURR-FULL:v2p214/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r9.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r9.claim: Wahb gives a prayer Jesus used for the ill, infirm, blind, and insane; for fear or insanity it may be recited, written, and its water given to drink.
DURR-FULL:v2p214/r9.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه قال: كان دعاء عيسى الذي يدعو به للمرضى والزمنى والعميان والمجانين وغيرهم

DURR-FULL:v2p220/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r1.claim: An unattributed continuation tells of three men plotting over money: the returning man is killed, the other two eat poisoned food, and all die, leaving the money behind.
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r1.anchor: فبعثوا أحدهم فقال الذي بعث: لأي شيء أقاسم هؤلاء المال ولكن أضع في الطعام سما

DURR-FULL:v2p220/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r2.speaker: خالد الحذاء
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r2.claim: Khalid al-Hadha says Jesus instructed messengers who went to raise the dead what to say and to pray when they felt a shiver and saw tears.
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r2.anchor: عن خالد الحذاء قال: كان عيسى بن مريم إذا سرح رسله يحيون الموتى يقول لهم

DURR-FULL:v2p220/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r3.speaker: ثابت
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r3.claim: Thabit recounts that Jesus called his dead friend's brother from the grave; the man emerged gray-haired and said he mistook Jesus's voice for the trumpet blast.
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r3.anchor: عن ثابت قال: انطلق عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام يزور أخا له فاستقبله إنسان

DURR-FULL:v2p220/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r4.claim: Mujahid explains the phrases as what people have eaten and what they have put away.
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون} قال: بما أكلتم الراحة من طعام وما خبأتم منه

DURR-FULL:v2p220/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r5.claim: Ibn Jubayr says Jesus told a boy at school what his family had hidden for him.
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: كان عيسى يقول للغلام في الكتاب: إن أهلك قد خبأوا لك كذا وكذا

DURR-FULL:v2p220/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r6.claim: Ibn Amr says that as a boy Jesus told other children what their mothers hid for them; alarmed families confined the children, and Jesus searched for them.
DURR-FULL:v2p220/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال: كان عيسى بن مريم وهو غلام يلعب مع الصبيان فكان يقول لأحدهم: تريد أن أخبرك

DURR-FULL:v2p221/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p221/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p221/r1.claim: The continuation says the children were said to be apes and pigs; Jesus prayed that they become so, and they did.
DURR-FULL:v2p221/r1.anchor: إنما هؤلاء قردة وخنازير قال: اللهم اجعلهم قردة وخنازير فكانوا كذلك

DURR-FULL:v2p221/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p221/r2.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
DURR-FULL:v2p221/r2.claim: Ammar says what the children ate and stored was from the heavenly table; they had been required to eat without saving, and their fear led to their becoming apes and pigs.
DURR-FULL:v2p221/r2.anchor: عن عمار بن ياسر قال {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون} من المائدة {وما تدخرون} منها

DURR-FULL:v2p221/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p221/r3.speaker: عاصم بن أبي النجود
DURR-FULL:v2p221/r3.claim: Asim ibn Abi al-Najud read taddakhiruna with a geminated consonant through assimilation.
DURR-FULL:v2p221/r3.anchor: عن عاصم بن أبي النجود {وما تدخرون} مثقلة بالإدغام

IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains that Jesus was a messenger from God to the Children of Israel.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r1.anchor: قال محمد ة بن اسحاق و رسولا إلى بني اسرائيل اي رسول منه اليكم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the sign Jesus brought was proof of his prophethood.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r2.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق اي يحق بها نبوتي

IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that they asked Jesus to make the bird that was hardest to create.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله : اني اخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير قالوا : اي طير اشد خلقا ليخلق عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says God made signs through Jesus’ hands to demonstrate His power to resurrect whom He wills and create whatever He wills, visible or unseen; Jesus’ bird-making was by God’s permission.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p654/r4.anchor: ثنا محمد بن اسحاق قال : ثم جعل الله على يديه يعني : عيسى امورا تدل به على قدرته في بعثه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r1.claim: Mujahid says Jesus told them what they had eaten the previous night; Said ibn Jubayr gives the same explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ، عن مجاهد 1 قوله : وانبئكم بما تاكلون بما اكلتم البارحة من الطعام

IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r2.claim: Qatada says Jesus foretold what they would eat from the table, transmitting this report from Khallas ibn Amr through Ammar ibn Yasir.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r2.anchor: عن قتادة وانبئكم بما تاكلون قال : انبئكم بما تاكلون من المائدة .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r3.claim: Qatada says Jesus disclosed what they stored from the table. They had been forbidden to store its food; those who did so betrayed the covenant and became pigs, as in the warning in 5:115.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r3.anchor: وبه عن قتادة وما تدخرون في بيوتكم قال : وما تدخرون منها يعني : من المائدة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r4.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase as what they had hidden from the table; Said ibn Jubayr gives the same explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r4.anchor: عن مجاهدوما تدخرون في بيوتكم قال : ما خباتم منه ، عيسى يقوله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r5.claim: Said ibn Jubayr relates that Jesus told a boy at school what food his family had hidden for him, then asked the boy to share it.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير : ان عيسى كان يقول للغلام في الكتاب : ان اهلك قد خباوا لك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r6.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r6.claim: Abu Malik specifies that the initial hamza in “inna” is read with kasra; the report also says “if not,” without further explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r6.anchor: عن اسباط عن السدى ، عن أبي مالك قوله : ان بكسر الالف فلم يكن

IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r7.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r7.anchor: وبه عن أبي مالك قوله : ذلك يعني : هذا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r8.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the sign as proof that Jesus was a messenger from God to them.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p656/r8.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق ان في ذلك لاية لكم اي رسول من الله اليكم ان كنتم مؤمنين

IBNABIHATIM:v2p657/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p657/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p657/r1.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains “believers” as those who affirm the truth.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p657/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ان كنتم مؤمنين يعني : مصدقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r3.claim: Rasulan coordinates with yaʿlamuhu, a clause functioning as a single circumstantial expression; kalima is the circumstantial subject, continuing angelic speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r3.anchor: عطف على جملة ( يعلمه ) لأن جملة الحال ، لكونها ذات محل من الإعراب ، هي في قوة المفرد فنصب رسولا على الحال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r4.claim: Anni has an open hamza because ba is understood after rasulan, meaning messenger with this declaration; Jesus begins speaking after the angels finish.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r4.anchor: وفتح همزة أن في قوله : { أني قد جئتكم } لتقدير باء الجر بعد رسولا ، أي رسولا بهذا المقال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r5.claim: Jiʾtukum means Jesus was sent from God to the Israelites, as in the parallel wording at 43:63.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p249/r5.anchor: ومعنى { جئتكم } أرسلت إليكم من جانب الله ونظيرة قوله تعالى : { ولما جاء عيسى بالبينات قال قد جئتكم بالحكمة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r1.claim: Bi-ayatin is circumstantial to jiʾtukum: the point is Jesus's status as messenger, not merely arrival bearing a sign.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r1.anchor: وقوله : { بآية } حال من ضمير { جئتكم } لأن المقصود الإخبار بأنه رسول لا بأنه جاء بآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r2.claim: The ba means accompaniment: Jesus came with signs proving his mission; the phrase may attach to jiʾtukum or stand as a stable circumstantial phrase.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r2.anchor: والباء في قوله { بآية } للملابسة أى مقارنا للآيات الدالة على صدقي في هذه الرسالة المعبر عنها بفعل المجيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r3.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r3.claim: Nafi and Abu Jaʿfar read anni with kasra as a fresh sentence explaining the sign; others read fatha as apposition to the prior declaration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r3.anchor: وقوله : { إني أخلق بكسر الهمزة استئناف لبيان آية وهي قراءة نافع ، وأبي جعفر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r4.claim: The literal root sense of khalq is measuring or proportioning, as with preparing hide before cutting; Zuhayr's verse contrasts estimating with cutting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r4.anchor: والخلق : حقيقته تقدير شيء بقدر ، ومنه خلق الأديم تقديره بحسب ما يراد من قطعه قبل قطع القطعة منه قال زهير :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r5.claim: Khalq also means originating with or without a model; here Jesus shapes clay like a bird, not creating an animal, as the blowing shows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r5.anchor: ويستعمل مجازا مشهورا أو مشتركا في الإنشاء ، والإبداع على غير مثال ولا احتذاء ، وفي الإنشاء على مثال يبدع ويقدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r6.claim: The kaf means likeness and describes an omitted object inferred from akhluqu: something proportioned like a bird's form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r6.anchor: والكاف في قوله : كهيئة الطير } بمعنى مثل ، وهي صفة لموصوف محذوف دل عليه أخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر والجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r7.claim: Most readers have al-tayr, generally collective but sometimes singular; Abu Jaʿfar reads singular al-taʾir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ( الطير ) وهو اسم يقع على الجمع غالبا وقد يقع على الواحد . وقرأه أبو جعفر ( الطائر )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r8.claim: The pronoun in fihi refers to the omitted object indicated by the kaf: the shaped thing resembling a bird.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r8.anchor: والضمير المجرور بفي من قوله : { فأنفخ فيه } عائد إلى ذلك الموصوف المحذوف الذي دلت عليه الكاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r9.speaker: نافع والجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r9.claim: Nafi reads singular taʾiran to match the singular pronoun; others read collective tayran by sense. Jesus shapes the form, while God brings it to life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p250/r9.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده فيكون طائرا بالإفراد وقرأ الباقون فيكون طيرا بصيغة اسم الجمع فقراءة نافع على مراعاة انفراد الضمير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r1.claim: Hayʾa means shape or configuration: Jesus forms a clay image in the shape of a bird.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r1.anchor: والهيئة : الصورة والكيفية أي أصور من الطين صورة كصورة الطير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r2.speaker: جميع القراء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r2.claim: All readers pronounce hayʾa with a silent yāʾ followed by an open hamza.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجميع كهيئة بتحتية ساكنة بعدها همزة مفتوحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r3.claim: Adding bi-idhnillah displays Jesus's servitude and excludes any suggestion he shares in creating beings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r3.anchor: وزاد قوله : { بإذن الله } لإظهار العبودية ، ونفي توهم المشاركة في خلق الكائنات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r4.claim: Al-akmah means a blind person generally, or specifically someone born blind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r4.anchor: والأكمه : الأعمى ، أو الذي ولد أعمى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur describes leprosy as variable skin disease with pale patches, of unknown cause, hereditary and noncontagious; ancient peoples associated it with leprosy and feared it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r5.anchor: والأبرص : المصاب بداء البرص وهو داء جلدي له مظاهر متنوعة منها الخفيف ومنها القوي وأعراضه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r6.claim: Arabs and Hebrews stigmatized the disease; Arab kings used a screen, while Torah rules isolated sufferers, making Jesus's cure especially valuable to Jews.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r6.anchor: فأما العرب فكان ملوكهم لا يكلمون الأبرص إلا من وراء حجاب ، كما وقع في قصة الحارث بن حلزة الشاعر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r7.claim: Muslim jurists treated leprosy as a spousal defect permitting annulment in some forms, but described the conditions imprecisely.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r7.anchor: وقد ذكر فقهاء الإسلام البرص في عيوب الزوجين الموجبة للخيار وفصلوا بين أنواعه التي توجب الخيار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r8.claim: Raising the dead, like animating the clay bird, was another miracle; Jesus briefly revived a dead person, and the Gospels recount his raising a girl just after death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r8.anchor: وإحياء الموتى معجزة للمسيح أيضا ، كنفخ الروح في الطير المصور من الطين ، فكان إذا أحيا ميتا كلمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r9.claim: Ibn Ashur cites Matthew 17: Jesus ascended a mountain with Peter, James, and John, where Moses and Elijah appeared speaking with them; all was by God's permission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p251/r9.anchor: ووقع في إنجيل متى في الإصحاح 17 أن عيسى صعد الجبل ومعه بطرس ويعقوب ويوحنا أخوه وأظهر لهم موسى وإيلياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r1.claim: Jesus’ promise to inform them concerns hidden household facts—what they ate and stored—so the coordinated acts are miracles, since informing concerns concealed matters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r1.anchor: لتكون هاته المتعاطفات كلها من قبيل المعجزات بقرينة قوله أنبئكم لأن الإنباء يكون في الأمور الخفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r2.claim: The miracles are signs inviting belief if the Israelites wish to believe; the address confronts people who met Jesus’ call with denial and insults.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r2.anchor: جعل هذه الأشياء كلها آيات تدعو إلى الإيمان به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r3.claim: The Qur’an indirectly rebuts Christians who infer Jesus’ divinity from acts beyond human power; that argument is sophistical, and the wording attributes the acts to God’s permission.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r4.speaker: أهل السير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r4.claim: Historians report that the Christians of Najran used these miracles as an argument before the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p252/r4.anchor: وقد روى أهل السير أن نصارى نجران استدلوا بهذه الأعمال لدى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r1.claim: “As a messenger” may be a circumstantial clause coordinated with “he teaches him,” or imply “He makes him a messenger”; semantically the whole description connects to “held in honor” at 3:45.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r1.anchor: وقوله: ورسولا حال معطوفة على ويعلمه إذ التقدير، ومعلما الكتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r2.claim: Jesus was sent to the Israelites to explain Torah law, call them to follow it, and make lawful some things it had forbidden, including certain foods, camel meat, and some fish and birds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r2.anchor: وكانت رسالة عيسى عليه السلام إلى بني إسرائيل، مبينا حكم التوراة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r3.claim: The speech to Mary runs through “Israel”; the words “I have come to you” through “straight path” are most naturally what Jesus will say to Israel, with an understood “then Jesus came and said” afterward. An alternative places that omitted transition before the speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r3.anchor: والأول أظهر، وقرأ جمهور الناس «أني قد جئتكم» بفتح الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r4.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r4.claim: Most readers open the hamza of annī, understood as bi-annī (“that I have come”); an irregular reading uses innī with kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r4.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «أني قد جئتكم» بفتح الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r5.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r5.claim: Most readers have the singular “a sign”; Ibn Masʿūd’s codex has the plural “signs,” also in the later phrase “I have come to you with signs from your Lord.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r5.anchor: وجمهور الناس قرؤوا بآية على الإفراد وفي مصحف ابن مسعود «بآيات»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r6.speaker: نافع وجماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r6.claim: Nāfiʿ and a group read innī with kasra, either as a new independent statement or as an explanation of the sign, like the Adam example.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r6.anchor: فقرأ نافع وجماعة من العلماء، «إني» بكسر الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r7.speaker: باقي السبعة وجماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r7.claim: The remaining canonical readers and other scholars open the hamza: “that I shape,” as an apposition to “a sign” or to the first annī; these parses are close in meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r7.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة وجماعة من العلماء، «أني» بفتح الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r8.claim: Here akhluqu means to shape, measure, or prepare by hand, as in Zuhayr’s line contrasting shaping something with successfully completing it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438/r8.anchor: وأخلق معناه، أقدر وأهيئ بيدي، ومن ذلك قول الشاعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r1.claim: “For you” qualifies the shaping and shows that Jesus does not claim creation from nothing; the clause “by God’s permission” makes this explicit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r1.anchor: وقوله لكم تقييد لقوله، أخلق لأنه يدل دلالة ما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r2.claim: Creation properly concerns physical bodies but is also used figuratively, as at 29:17 for inventing falsehood and in a cited poem for making up speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r2.anchor: وحقيقة الخلق في الأجرام، ويستعمل في المعاني، ومنه قوله تعالى: وتخلقون إفكا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r3.claim: Jesus shapes the clay and breathes to show his involvement in the sign; God alone brings the form into existence from nothing and creates life in it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r3.anchor: وأما الإيجاد من العدم وخلق الحياة في ذلك الطين فمن الله تعالى وحده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r4.claim: Most readers use hayʾa, on the faʿla pattern, from a verb meaning to settle or take an ordered state, and it is made transitive as hayyaʾa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r4.anchor: وجمهور الناس قرأ «كهيئة» على وزن فعلة بفتح الفاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r5.speaker: الزهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r5.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads hayʾati with kasra on hāʾ and a geminated, opened yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الزهري «كهيئة الطير» ، بكسر الهاء وياء مفتوحة مشددة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن القعقاع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar b. al-Qaʿqāʿ reads “bird” as singular in both places: the first is a collective genus and the second means one bird among birds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بن القعقاع، «كهيئة الطائر فأنفخ فيه فيكون طائرا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r7.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ alone uses singular ṭāʾiran in the final position; the other readers use plural ṭayran in both places, likewise in Sūrat al-Māʾida.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده، «كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طائرا» بالإفراد في الأخير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r8.speaker: أبو علي عن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r8.claim: Ṭayr is a collective noun, not a standard plural form; the regular plural of ṭāʾir is aṭyār, and the plural of that is ṭuyūr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r8.anchor: والطير اسم جمع وليس من أبنية الجموع، وإنما البناء في جمع طائر أطيار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r9.claim: The masculine pronoun in “I breathe into it” can refer to the prepared clay or to the previously mentioned object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r9.anchor: وقوله فأنفخ فيه ذكر الضمير هنا لأنه يحتمل أن يعود على الطين المهيأ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r11.claim: Permission means God’s knowledge that the act will occur and His enabling it; accompanying speech makes the permission more explicit and can approach a command, though it remains within permission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r11.anchor: وقوله بإذن الله، معناه بعلم منه تعالى أني أفعل ذلك وتمكين منه لي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya links the phrase to “they defeated them by God’s permission” at 2:251 and cites the Prophetic dictum that a woman’s silence is her permission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p438#2/r12.anchor: وتأمل قوله تعالى: فهزموهم بإذن الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r1.claim: Abraʾu means to remove illness: a patient may be described as healed, and one person may heal another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: أبرئ، معناه أزيل المرض يقال برأ المريض وأبرأه غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r2.claim: Mujāhid defines an akmah as someone who sees in daylight but not at night.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r2.anchor: فقال مجاهد: الأكمه هو الذي يبصر بالنهار ولا يبصر بالليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and al-Suddī define akmah as absolutely blind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن والسدي: الأكمه الأعمى على الإطلاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says an akmah is someone with weak or dim eyesight.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r5.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r5.claim: Al-Naqqāsh reports a view that akmah means mute and unable to understand, “dead of heart.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r5.anchor: وحكى النقاش قولا: أن الأكمه هو الأبكم الذي لا يفهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda also define akmah as someone born blind, with closed eyes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وقتادة: الأكمه الذي يولد أعمى مضموم العين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r7.claim: Jesus healed every illness by prayer and touch, but a prophetic proof must concern ailments beyond physicians; the born-blind definition best fits, since akmah linguistically means blind. Without that linguistic constraint, al-Naqqāsh’s sense would make a good proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r7.anchor: قال القاضي: وقد كان عيسى عليه السلام يبرىء بدعائه ومسح يده كل علة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r8.claim: Leprosy is a familiar disease and, once established, does not heal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r8.anchor: والأبرص معروف، وهو داء لا يبرأ منه إذا تمكن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r9.claim: Reports say Jesus struck a dead person, grave, or skull with his staff, reviving a person who then spoke; no specific authority is given.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r9.anchor: وروي في إحيائه الموتى، أنه كان يضرب بعصاه الميت أو القبر أو الجمجمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r10.claim: One report says Jesus raised Sam, son of Noah; other accounts disagree over whether the revived person remained alive or soon died again.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r10.anchor: وروي أنه أحيى سام بن نوح عليه السلام، وروي أن الذي كان يحييه كانت تدوم حياته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says there are many resurrection stories, but their reports cannot be established as authentic.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r11.anchor: وفي قصص الإحياء أحاديث كثيرة لا يوقف على صحتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r12.claim: Raising the dead is Jesus’s miraculous sign exposed to challenge in substance, even though the verse does not explicitly state the challenge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r12.anchor: وإحياء الموتى هي آيته المعجزة المعرضة للتحدي، وهي بالمعنى متحدى بها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r13.claim: Jesus’s signs addressed the age’s preoccupation with medicine: healing and raising the dead exceeded humoral theory and medical practice, revealing divine power, just as Moses challenged magicians and Muḥammad challenged masters of eloquence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r13.anchor: وآيات عيسى عليه السلام إنما تجري فيما يعارض الطب لأن علم الطب كان شرف الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r14.claim: A story says Jesus asked which bird was hardest to form; the Israelites chose the featherless bat, so he shaped clay bats and breathed life into them before witnesses, who called him a magician. No authority or grading is given.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p439/r14.anchor: فيقولون: الخفاش، لأنه طائر لا ريش له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r1.claim: Translated medical histories say Galen lived in Jesus' time, traveled from Rome to Syria to meet him, and died on the way.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r2.speaker: السدي وسعيد بن جبير وابن إسحاق ومجاهد وعطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r2.claim: They say Jesus foretold from childhood what boys' parents did at home and what they ate and stored; after his commission he answered such questions, prompting parents to call him a sorcerer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r2.anchor: فقال السدي وسعيد بن جبير وابن إسحاق ومجاهد وعطاء: كان عيسى من لدن طفولته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq adds that Jesus' teacher would begin teaching him something, but Jesus anticipated it, astonishing the teacher, who told people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r3.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وكان معلمه يريد أن يعلمه الشيء فيسبقه إليه عيسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r4.claim: Qatada places the foreknowledge at the table's descent: Jesus had required people not to hide its food, but they secretly kept some at home, so he told each person what he had eaten and stored and they were punished.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة، معنى الآية إنما هو في نزول المائدة عليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r5.claim: The two occurrences of ما can each be relative or infinitival.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r5.anchor: وما في قوله بما تأكلون يحتمل أن تكون بمعنى الذي وتحتمل المصدرية وكذلك وما تدخرون،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r6.claim: The majority read تدخرون with doubled dāl and kasra on khāʾ, from تفتعلون of ذخر; original تذخرون was eased by changing tāʾ to dāl and assimilating ذ into it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور، «تدخرون» بدال مشددة وخاء مكسورة، وهو تفتعلون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r7.speaker: الزهري ومجاهد وأيوب السختياني وأبو السمال
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r7.claim: These readers pronounce تدخرون with a vowelless dāl and fatḥa on khāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r7.anchor: وقرأ الزهري ومجاهد وأيوب السختياني وأبو السمال «تدخرون» - بدال ساكنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r8.speaker: زهير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r8.claim: Zuhayr's form فيطلم, pronounced with ṭāʾ, is cited as a parallel for the sound change discussed in the majority reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r8.anchor: نحو قول الشاعر: [زهير] [البسيط] إن الكريم الذي يعطيك نائله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r9.claim: That points to the signs just mentioned: reviving the dead, healing, and foretelling what people eat and store.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r9.anchor: وقوله: إن في ذلك إشارة إلى ما ذكر من الإحياء والإبراء والإنباء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r10.claim: Ibn Masud's codex has plural لآيات instead of the canonical singular.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r10.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود «لآيات» على الجمع،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r11.claim: If the addressees are still unbelieving Israelites, the condition challenges them: the signs guide believers, though they remain signs whether people believe or disbelieve.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r11.anchor: هذا كله على أن المخاطبة لمن لم يؤمن- بعد- وهو ظاهر حاله مع بني إسرائيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r12.claim: If addressed to people who already believe in Moses, the conditional exhorts them to act, like telling someone he must do a thing if he is truly a man.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p440/r12.anchor: وإن كان خطابه لمؤمنين، أو كما كانوا مؤمنين بموسى، فمعنى الآية التشبيت وهز النفس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows two accusative parses for “a messenger,” but prefers attaching it to “he speaks to people,” as a messenger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج ينتصب على وجهين أحدهما ونجعله رسولا والاختيار عندي ويكلم الناس رسولا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r2.claim: Most reciters read annī with fatḥa and take it as apposition to “a sign”; Nāfiʿ reads innī with kasra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r2.anchor: قرأ الأكثرون أني بالفتح فجعلوها بدلا من آية فكأنه قال قد جئتكم بأني أخلق لكم وقرأ نافع بالكسر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r3.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī says Nāfiʿ's kasra can begin a new sentence or explain the sign; “create” here means to shape and form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي يحتمل وجهين أحدهما أن يكون مستأنفا والثاني أنه فسر الآية بقوله إني أخلق أي أصور وأقدر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jesus took clay, fashioned a bat, and breathed into it until it flew; some say he made no bird other than a bat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس أخذ طينا وصنع منه خفاشا ونفخ فيه فإذا هو يطير ويقال لم يصنع غير الخفاش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r5.claim: It is said the Israelites requested a bat because its creation is wondrous: it flies without feathers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r5.anchor: ويقال إن بني إسرائيل نعتوه بذلك لأن الخفاش عجيب الخلق وروي عن أبي سعيد الخدري أنه قال لهم ماذا تريدون قالوا الخفاش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r6.speaker: وهب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r6.claim: Wahb says the fashioned creature flew while people watched, then fell dead when they looked away, distinguishing the creature's act from the Creator's.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r6.anchor: وقال وهب كان الذي صنعه يطير ما دام الناس ينظرونه فإذا غاب عن أعينهم سقط ميتا ليميز فعل الخلق من فعل الخالق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r7.claim: Most reciters read ṭayran, while Nāfiʿ reads ṭāʾiran here and in al-Māʾida.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع هاهنا وفي المائدة طائرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r8.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r8.claim: Abū ʿAlī supports the majority reading from the wording “like the form of a bird”; Nāfiʿ's reading means what is breathed into or made becomes a flying creature.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r8.anchor: ووجهة قراءة نافع أنه أراد يكون ما أنفخ فيه أو ما اخلقه طائرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r9.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس، سعيد عن قتادة، اليزيدي، ابن قتيبة، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r9.claim: One definition of al-akmah is someone born blind.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r9.anchor: أحدها أنه الذي يولد أعمى رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس وسعيد عن قتادة وبه قال اليزيدي و ابن قتيبة و الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r10.speaker: ابن جريج عن ابن عباس، معمر عن قتادة، الحسن، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r10.claim: A second definition is a blind person; al-Khalīl's reported gloss includes both one born blind and one who becomes blind after sight.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r10.anchor: والثاني أنه الأعمى ذكره ابن جريج عن ابن عباس ومعمر عن قتادة وبه قال الحسن والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r12.speaker: مجاهد، الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r12.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say al-akmah sees by day but not by night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r12.anchor: ولا يبصر بالليل قاله مجاهد و الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r13.claim: Al-abraṣ is a person marked by white patches.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r14.claim: Medicine was the dominant skill of Jesus's age, so his healing matched its field while curing congenital blindness and leprosy exceeded medicine and demonstrated his truth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r14.anchor: وكان الغالب على زمان عيسى عليه السلام علم الطب فأراهم المعجزة من جنس ذلك إلا أنه ليس في الطب إبراء الأكمه والأبرص وكان ذلك دليلا على صدقه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r15.speaker: وهب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r15.claim: Wahb says as many as fifty thousand sick people might gather around Jesus in one day, and he treated them through prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r15.anchor: قال وهب ربما اجتمع على عيسى من المرضى في اليوم الواحد خمسون ألفا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r16.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r16.claim: The exegetes say Jesus raised four people from the dead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r16.anchor: وذكر المفسرون أنه أحيا أربعة أنفس من الموت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says all four lived long enough to have children, except Sām son of Noah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p391#3/r17.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن الأربعة كلهم بقي حتى ولد له إلا سام بن نوح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
