IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r1.claim: Unspecified exegetes variously define al-akmah as one who sees by day but not night, the reverse, a squint-eyed person, a weak-sighted person, or one born blind; Ibn Kathir prefers the last as the greater miracle and challenge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r1.anchor: قيل: هو الذي يبصر نهارا ولا يبصر ليلا. وقيل بالعكس. وقيل: هو الأعشى. وقيل: الأعمش.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r2.claim: Al-abras refers to the familiar condition of leprosy.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r3.speaker: كثير من العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r3.claim: Many scholars say each prophet received miracles suited to his era: Moses came amid sorcery, and his sign confounded the magicians, who then submitted and became righteous.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r3.anchor: قال كثير من العلماء: بعث الله كل نبي من الأنبياء بمعجزة تناسب أهل زمانه، فكان الغالب على زمان موسى، عليه السلام، السحر وتعظيم السحرة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r4.speaker: كثير من العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r4.claim: Jesus was sent among doctors and natural scientists with signs beyond human capacity: reviving inanimate things, curing the blind and leper, and raising the dead, all by God's support.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r4.anchor: وأما عيسى، عليه السلام، فبعث في زمن الأطباء وأصحاب علم الطبيعة، فجاءهم من الآيات بما لا سبيل لأحد إليه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r5.speaker: كثير من العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r5.claim: Muhammad came among eloquent rhetoricians and master poets with the inimitable Qur'an, which humans and jinn could not match even with collective help, because God's speech is unlike created speech.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p44#2/r5.anchor: وكذلك محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بعثه [الله] (1) في زمن الفصحاء والبلغاء ونحارير الشعراء، فأتاهم بكتاب من الله، عز وجل،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p45/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p45/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p45/r1.claim: Jesus tells them what each person has just eaten and what he has stored at home for the next day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p45/r1.anchor: أي: أخبركم بما أكل أحدكم الآن، وما هو مدخر [له] (2) في بيته لغده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p45/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p45/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p45/r2.claim: All these signs demonstrate that Jesus is truthful in what he brings, for those who believe.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p45/r2.anchor: إن في ذلك} أي: في ذلك كله {لآية لكم} أي: على صدقي فيما جئتكم به. {إن كنتم مؤمنين}

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r5.speaker: نافع
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r5.claim: Nāfiʿ reads innī with kasra; the other readers use fatḥa.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع إني أخلق بكسر الألف من (إن) والباقون بالفتح

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r6.claim: The fatḥa reading attaches to messengerhood or supplies an omitted preposition, bi-annī or li-annī; kasra begins an independent clause.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r6.anchor: فمن فتح فلوقوع الرسالة عليه، وقيل: بنزع حرف الصفة أي بأني أو لأني

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r7.claim: The kasra reading treats the statement as a fresh independent sentence.

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the word with a doubled yāʾ; other readers use hamza.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر كهية بتشديد الياء والآخرون بالهمز

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r9.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, and Yaʿqūb read ṭāʾiran in the singular; the rest read ṭayran collectively, likewise in 5:110.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع ويعقوب فيكون طائرا بالألف على الواحد

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r10.speaker: العامة
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r10.claim: The general reading has the second-person tāʾ in taddakhirūn.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r10.anchor: وقراءة العامة: وما تدخرون بالتاء، وعن مجاهد بالياء

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r11.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r11.claim: Mujāhid is reported to read the verb with yāʾ rather than tāʾ.

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r12.claim: Ṭīn means clay; ṭayyanat al-kitāb means clay was placed on the document.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r12.anchor: الطين معروف، يقال: طينت الكتاب جعلت عليه طينا

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r13.claim: Hayʾa is the visible state or appearance; the verb hāʾa describes a fine appearance.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r13.anchor: والهيئة: الحال الظاهرة هاء فلان يهاء هيئة

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r14.claim: Nafkh is air that comes out of the mouth.

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r15.claim: Ṭayr is a collective plural whose singular is ṭāʾir, like zūr from zāʾir and safar from sāfir.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r15.anchor: والطير جمع، واحده: طائر نحو: زائر وزور، وسافر وسفر

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r16.claim: Barʾ means healing, and akmah means blind.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r16.anchor: والبرء: الشفاء. والأكمه في اللغة الأعمى يقال: كمه يكمه كمها

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r17.claim: Baras is the familiar disease, which Arabs regarded as ill-omened and which has no cure once firmly established.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r17.anchor: والبرص: الداء المعروف، وكان يتطير منه العرب، وإذا استحكم فلا برء له

JISHUMI:v2p1171/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r18.claim: Iddikhar derives from d-kh-r and means hiding something for a future need; its morphology changes the tāʾ and assimilates the adjacent dhāl into dāl.
JISHUMI:v2p1171/r18.anchor: والادخار: افتعال من الدخر، دخرت أدخر دخرا، وادخرت ادخارا

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r1.claim: Teaching Jesus the Book is interpreted as teaching him writing by hand.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r1.anchor: ويعلمه الكتاب قيل: الكتابة بيده، عن ابن جريج

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r2.claim: Another report says God divided writing into ten parts, giving humanity one and Jesus nine.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r2.anchor: وقيل: إنه تعالى قسم الخط عشرة أجزاء فجعل للخلق جزءا

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r3.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r3.claim: Abu Ali says the Book is another scripture besides Torah and Gospel, such as Psalms; the author finds this likelier to the wording and more fitting to prophethood and wisdom.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r3.anchor: وقيل: كتابا آخر سوى التوراة والإنجيل نحو الزبور أو غيره، عن أبي علي، وهو أليق بالظاهر،

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r4.claim: Wisdom is interpreted either as knowledge or soundness in speech and action.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r4.anchor: وأشبه بالنبوة والحكمة قيل: العلم، وقيل: الإصابة من القول والعمل

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r5.claim: The account breaks off Mary's birth story, told in Surat Maryam, and begins the story of Jesus.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r5.anchor: ورسولا قطع ههنا قصة ولادة مريم، وقصه في سورة مريم، وابتدأ بقصة عيسى

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r6.claim: God would make Jesus a messenger to the Children of Israel.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r6.anchor: ورسولا أي ويجعله رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r7.claim: A report from the Prophet identifies Moses as the first and Jesus as the last prophet of the Children of Israel.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r7.anchor: وكان أول أنبياء بني إسرائيل موسى، وآخرهم عيسى (عليه السلام) عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r8.claim: The kasra on inni begins a new sentence; the fatha makes it dependent on the preceding statement.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r8.anchor: إني بالكسر على الاستئناف، وبالفتح أي بأني أخلق

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r9.claim: The sign is a proof and marker demonstrating Jesus's prophethood.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r9.anchor: (قد جئتكم بآية) أي حجة وعلامة دالة على نبوتي

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r10.claim: Akhluqu here means I fashion or determine a form from clay.

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r11.claim: The blowing is breath or air blown into the fashioned bird.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r11.anchor: (فأنفخ فيه) أي في الطير الريح (فيكون طيرا) حيا يطير

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r12.claim: A report describes Jesus fashioning a bat, said to be the strangest bird because it menstruates, does not lay eggs, and flies; it flew before the onlookers then fell dead after leaving sight.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r12.anchor: روي أنه قيل: أي الطير أعجب؟ قالوا: الخفاش يحيض ولا يبيض ويطير، مع عجيب خلقته،

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r13.claim: God alone can give life and the faculties of flight; Jesus shapes and blows, God gives life and the means of flight, and the bird itself flies.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r13.anchor: لأن الحياة وآلات الطيران لا يقدر عليها غير الله تعالى، وإنما أحياه عند نفخ عيسى (عليه السلام) معجزة له،

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r14.claim: By God's permission marks the life-giving act as God's, not Jesus's.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r14.anchor: وأما الطيران فمن فعل الطير، وإنما قال: بإذن الله ليعلم أنه فعله، وليس بفعل لعيسى (عليه السلام)

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r15.claim: Al-akmah can mean someone born blind, according to Ibn Abbas and Qatadah.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r15.anchor: والأكمه: قيل: الذي ولد أعمى، عن ابن عباس وقتادة،

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r16.speaker: الحسن والسدي
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r16.claim: Hasan and al-Suddi interpret al-akmah as a blind person.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r16.anchor: وقيل: هو الأعمى، عن الحسن والسدي،

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r17.speaker: عكرمة
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r17.claim: Ikrima interprets al-akmah as someone with weak eyesight.

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r18.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r18.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak say al-akmah sees by day but not at night.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r18.anchor: وقيل: الذي يبصر بالنهار دون الليل، عن مجاهد والضحاك

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r19.claim: Al-abras is a person afflicted with baras, a skin disease.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r19.anchor: والأبرص الذي به برص وأحيي الموتى

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r20.claim: Healing and reviving are God's acts; Jesus prayed for healing or revival and God healed or raised the dead.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r20.anchor: وكل ذلك توسع ومجاز؛ لأن الإبراء والإحياء فعل الله تعالى، وحقيقة الكلام أدعو الله بإحياء الموتى

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r21.claim: One account says Jesus revived four people: Azar after three days in the grave, Sam son of Noah, the son of the old woman, and another described as the tenth's son.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r21.anchor: وقيل: إنه أحيا أربعة أنفس: عازر بعد ما مات وقبر بثلاثة أيام، وسام بن نوح، وابن العجوز، وابنه العاشر،

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r22.claim: Jesus's healing matched his era's strength in medicine; Moses confronted an era of magic, while Muhammad's sign matched mastery of eloquence.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r22.anchor: وإنما خص عيسى (عليه السلام) بهذه الأشياء؛ لأن الغالب على الناس في زمانه كان الطب والمعالجات، فأراهم المعجزة من جنس ذلك

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r23.claim: A miracle is most conclusive when it resembles what people excel at and nevertheless defeats them; an unfamiliar feat could seem an ordinary skill.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r23.anchor: ومثل هذا يكون غاية الإعجاز: أن يأتي بمثل ما هم عليه ثم يعجزون؛ إذ لو أتاهم بشيء لا يعرفونه

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r24.speaker: وهب
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r24.claim: Wahb reports that fifty thousand sick people might gather around Jesus in a day; he treated them if they believed.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r24.anchor: وقيل: كانوا ربما يجتمع على عيسى في يوم واحد من المرضى خمسون ألفا، ويداويهم بالدواء على شرط الإيمان [1]، عن وهب،

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r25.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r25.claim: One report says Jesus invoked God as Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum when raising the dead.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r25.anchor: وقيل: كان يدعو عند إحياء الميت ب (ياحي يا قيوم)

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r26.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r26.claim: Jesus says he will tell people what they eat at lunch and supper and what they store at home.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r26.anchor: وأنبئكم أخبركم بما تأكلون من غدائكم وعشائكم، وما تدخرون في بيوتكم

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r27.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r27.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r27.claim: One account says after Jesus healed and raised the dead, people called it magic and challenged him to disclose their household stores.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r27.anchor: قيل: لما أبرأ الأكمه والأبرص وأحيا الموتى قالوا: هذا سحر، فأنبئنا عما في بيوتنا،

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r28.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r28.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r28.claim: Qatadah connects the disclosure to the heavenly table: people were told not to store food or betray the command, but did, and Jesus informed them.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r28.anchor: وأمر القوم ألا يدخروا بعد ابتلاء ولا يخونوا، فخانوا وادخروا، فكان عيسى يخبرهم بذلك، عن قتادة،

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r29.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r29.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r29.claim: Another report says the people were transformed into pigs when they opposed Jesus.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r29.anchor: وقيل: لما خالفوه مسخوا خنازير على اختلاف في الرواية

JISHUMI:v2p1173/r30.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r30.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r30.claim: These acts are proof if the people believe and accept them.
JISHUMI:v2p1173/r30.anchor: إن في ذلك أي فيما ذكرت لكم لآية أي لحجة وعلامة إن كنتم مؤمنين فاقبلوها

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r1.claim: Jesus knew Torah, Gospel, and knowledge of prophethood, namely wisdom.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r1.anchor: تدل الآية على أن عيسى (عليه السلام) علم التوراة والإنجيل والعلم الذي يتعلق بالنبوة وهو الحكمة.

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r2.claim: Jesus followed Moses's law except where abrogated; the author infers this from Jesus being taught Torah.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r2.anchor: وتدل على أنه كان متعبدا بشريعة موسى إلا ما وقع فيه نسخ؛ لذلك علمه التوراة.

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r3.claim: Jesus was sent to all the Children of Israel, contrary to the view that he was sent only to some.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r3.anchor: وتدل على أنه كان مبعوثا إلى جميع بني إسرائيل، خلاف ما قاله بعضهم أنه بعث إلى قوم منهم.

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r4.claim: The verse establishes that Jesus performed miracles.

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r5.claim: A servant may be described as creating in a limited sense, though not absolutely; God alone is Creator without qualification.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r5.anchor: وتدل على جواز وصف العبد بأنه يخلق، وإن كان لا يطلق عليه ذلك، بل الخالق على الإطلاق هو الله تعالى.

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r6.claim: Servants originate and perform acts; creating adds something beyond origination, refuting the Mujabbira.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن العبد يحدث ويفعل؛ لأن في الخلق زيادة على الإحداث، فيبطل في ذلك قول المجبرة في خلق الأفعال

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r7.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r7.claim: The distinction between clay likeness and living bird supports Abu Hashim's view that it is called a bird once it has flesh and blood, against Abu Ali.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r7.anchor: فقال في أحدهما: (كهيئة الطير)، ثم قال: (فيكون طيرا)؛ وذلك يصحح قول أبي هاشم: إنه اسم له إذا كان لحما ودما

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r8.claim: Blowing is attributed to Jesus, while revival is God's act qualified by God's permission.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r8.anchor: وتدل على الفصل بين فعله تعالى وفعل عيسى؛ لأن عند النفخ، وهو فعله أطلق، وعند الإحياء وهو فعل الله قال: (بإذن الله)

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r9.claim: The soul is a subtle body, as indicated by its description through blowing.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r9.anchor: وتدل على أن الروح جسم رقيق؛ لذلك وصف بالنفخ.

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r10.claim: Blowing is an act of the servant because the verse attributes it to him.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r10.anchor: وتدل على أن النفخ فعل العبد؛ لأنه أضافه إليه.

JISHUMI:v2p1175/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r11.claim: Knowledge of the unseen is a miracle reserved for prophets; Jesus's disclosure of food and stores demonstrates it.
JISHUMI:v2p1175/r11.anchor: وتدل على أن علم الغيب من المعجزات، يختص بها الأنبياء؛ لذلك قال: وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r1.claim: The difficult syntax can be resolved by supplying أرسلت with an understood saying, yielding “I was sent as a messenger that I have come to you and confirming what preceded me.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r1.anchor: قلت هو من المضائق وفيه وجهان احدهما ان يضمر له ( وأرسلت ) على إرادة القول تقديره ونعلمه الكتاب والحكمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r2.claim: A second analysis treats رسول and مصدقا as implying speech: the messenger speaks both of his coming and of confirming what came before him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r2.anchor: والثاني أن الرسول والمصدق فيهما معنى النطق فكأنه قيل وناطقا بأني قد جئتكم وناطقا بأني أصدق ما بين يدي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r3.speaker: اليزيدي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r3.claim: Al-Yazidi reads ورسول in the nominative, coordinating it with كلمة.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ اليزيدي ورسول عطفا على كلمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r4.claim: أني أخلق can be a substitute for أني قد جئتكم, a genitive substitute for آية, or a nominative clause understood as هي أني أخلق.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r4.anchor: أو جر بدل من آية أو رفع على هي أني اخلق لكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r5.claim: A kasra reading, إني, starts a new sentence and means “I can fashion for you something resembling a bird.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p391#2/r5.anchor: وقرىء ( إني ) بالكسر على الاستئناف أي أقدر لكم شيئا مثل صورة الطير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r1.claim: It becomes a living, flying bird like the other birds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r1.anchor: فيصير طيرا كسائر الطيور حيا طيارا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r2.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r2.claim: Abd Allah reads فأنفخها; the accompanying verse has ينفخ as an example of the form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( فأنفخها ) قال ( كالهبرقي تنحى ينفخ الفحما )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r3.claim: One report says that Jesus created no bird other than the bat.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r4.claim: The akmah is someone born blind; another view says the word means one whose eyes were erased.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r4.anchor: الذي ولد أعمى وقيل هو الممسوح العين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r5.claim: It is said that Qatada ibn Diama al-Sadusi, the Qur'an exegete, was the only akmah in this community.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r5.anchor: ويقال لم يكن في هذه الأمة أكمه غير قتادة بن دعامة السدوسي صاحب التفسير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r6.claim: A report says up to 50,000 sick people gathered around Jesus; he went to those unable to come, and healed only through prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r6.anchor: وروي انه ربما اجتمع عليه خمسون ألفا من المرضى من اطاق منهم اتاه ومن لم يطق اتاه عيسى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r7.claim: Repeating “by God's permission” prevents readers from imagining that Jesus possesses divinity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r7.anchor: دفعا لوهم من توهم فيه اللاهوتية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r8.claim: A report says Jesus revived Sam son of Noah before the onlookers; when they called it magic and requested a sign, he told people what they had eaten and hidden at home.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r8.anchor: وروي أنه أحيا سام بن نوح وهم ينظرون فقالوا هذا سحر فأرنا آية فقال يا فلان أكلت كذا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r9.claim: A reading has تذخرون with ذال and reduced consonant doubling.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r10.claim: ولأحل answers the earlier phrase بآية من ربكم: Jesus came with a sign from his Lord and to make lawful for them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p392/r10.anchor: أي جئتكم بآية من ربكم ولأحل لكم

MUJAHID:v1p127#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p127#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p127#3/r1.claim: Jesus tells the Israelites what they have hidden away in their homes.
MUJAHID:v1p127#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون ﴾ يعني ما خبأتم منه عيسى يقوله

MUJAHID:v1p127#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p127#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p127#3/r2.claim: Al-akmah is someone who can see during the day but not at night.
MUJAHID:v1p127#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال ﴿ الأكمه ﴾ الذي يبصر بالنهار ولا يبصر بالليل

MUQATIL:3:49/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:49/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:49/r1.claim: Jesus is a messenger to the Children of Israel, and the sign means a proof from God.
MUQATIL:3:49/r1.anchor: ويجعله { ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم } ، يعنى بعلامة، ثم بين الآية،

MUQATIL:3:49/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:49/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:49/r2.claim: Jesus fashioned a bat from clay; Muqatil describes it as an exceptionally formidable creature, only flesh yet flying without feathers, and says it flew by God's permission.
MUQATIL:3:49/r2.anchor: { أنى أخلق لكم } ، يعنى أجعل لكم { من الطين كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا } ، فخلق الخفاش { بإذن الله }

MUQATIL:3:49/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:49/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:49/r3.claim: Al-akmah is someone born blind who has never seen daylight; God restores that person's sight. Jesus also cures lepers and raises the dead by God's leave.
MUQATIL:3:49/r3.anchor: { وأبرىء الأكمه } الذى ولدته أمه أعمى، الذى لم ير النور قط، فيرد الله بصره، { و } أبرئ { والأبرص }

MUQATIL:3:49/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:49/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:49/r4.claim: Jesus raised Sam, son of Noah, son of Lamak, from the dead by God's permission; people called it magic and demanded a sign proving his truthfulness.
MUQATIL:3:49/r4.anchor: فأحيا سام بن نوح بن لمك من الموت بإذن الله، فقالوا: له: إن هذا سحر، فأرنا آية نعلم أنك صادق.

MUQATIL:3:49/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:49/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:49/r5.claim: What people store means what they save for the next day; Muqatil notes fronting in the phrase about what they eat and store.
MUQATIL:3:49/r5.anchor: قال عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم: أرأيتم إن أنا أخبرتكم { وأنبئكم بما تأكلون } فى بيوتكم من الطعام، فيها تقديم { وما تدخرون في بيوتكم } ، يعنى وما ترفعون فى غد،

MUQATIL:3:49/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:49/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:49/r6.claim: Jesus named what people had eaten and drunk; some believed and some disbelieved. This was a sign that he was God's messenger, for those who affirmed him as a messenger.
MUQATIL:3:49/r6.anchor: قال عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم: فلان أكلت كذا وكذا. وشربت كذا وكذا، وأنت يا فلان أكلت كذا وكذا،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r1.claim: ورسولا may be joined to وجيها, supplied by omitted نجعله رسولا, or read as a circumstantial accusative describing Jesus as honored in both worlds.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ ورسولا ﴾ أى ونجعله رسولا أو يكون فى موضع الحال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r2.claim: أنى introduces the content as that I have come to you with a sign.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم ﴾ بدلالة تدل على صدقي

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r3.claim: The sign is proof that Jesus’ claim to prophethood is true.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r3.anchor: بدلالة تدل على صدقي فيما أدعيه من النبوة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r4.claim: أنّي أخلق may be accusative as substitute for أني قد جئتكم, genitive as substitute for آية, or nominative after omitted هي.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r4.anchor: نصب بدل من أنى قد جئتكم أو جر بدل من آية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r5.speaker: نافع
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r5.claim: The segment notes Nafiʿ’s resumptive reading.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r5.anchor: أو رفع على هى أنى أخلق لم أنى نافع على الاستئناف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r6.claim: Jesus shapes from clay an object resembling a bird.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r6.anchor: أى اقدر لكم شيئا مثل صورة الطير

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r7.claim: The pronoun in فيه refers to the kāf of كهيئة: Jesus breathes into the thing resembling a bird.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ فأنفخ فيه ﴾ الضمير للكاف أى فى ذلك الشئ

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r8.speaker: مدني
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r8.claim: The Medinan reading adds طائرا, describing the resulting bird as flying like other birds.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r8.anchor: ﴿ فيكون طيرا ﴾ فيصير طيرا كسائر الطيور طائرا مدنى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r9.claim: By God’s permission means by His command; the author also reports that Jesus created no creature except the bat.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r9.anchor: ﴿ بإذن الله ﴾ بأمره قيل لم يخلق شيئا غير الخفاش

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r10.claim: The akmah is someone born blind.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r11.claim: Repeating by God’s permission prevents anyone from imagining Jesus possessed divinity.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r11.anchor: كرر بإذن الله دفعا لوهم من يتوهم فيه اللاهوتية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r12.claim: A report says Jesus raised Shem, Noah’s son, before onlookers; when they called it magic and asked for a sign, he told them what they had eaten and stored.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r12.anchor: فقالوا هذا سحر مبين فأرنا آية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r13.claim: In both clauses, ما may be a relative pronoun or a verbal noun.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r13.anchor: وما فيهما بمعنى الذى أو مصدرية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p155#2/r14.claim: All the preceding signs are evidence for the Israelites if they believe.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r6.claim: Here أخلق means to shape or fashion, or to estimate, for the Israelites.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r7.speaker: الأعرج وأبو جعفر
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r7.claim: Al-Aʿraj and Abū Jaʿfar read كهيئة as كهية with doubled yāʾ; other readers use the hamza.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r8.claim: The word الطير may be masculine or feminine.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r9.claim: The pronoun فيه may refer to the single bird, the birds, or the clay, which becomes a flying creature; طائر and طير compare to تاجر and تجر.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r9.anchor: أي في الواحد منه أو منها أو في الطين

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r10.speaker: وهب
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r10.claim: Wahb says the bird flew while people watched but fell dead when out of sight, distinguishing God's creative act from Jesus's.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r10.anchor: قال وهب: كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r11.claim: One account says Jesus made only the bat, whose complete and unusual animal-like features made it a striking sign of power; challengers asked him to animate one, and it flew after his breath.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r11.anchor: وقيل: لم يخلق غير الخفاش لأنه أكمل الطير خلقا ليكون أبلغ في القدرة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r12.claim: The bat is flesh and blood yet flies without feathers, gives live birth and has a milk-producing udder, teeth, ears, menstruation, and unusual vision; it is said to laugh like a human too.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r12.anchor: ومن عجائبه أنه لحم ودم يطير بغير ريش ويلد كما يلد الحيوان ولا يبيض

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r13.claim: In that account, Jesus shaped the clay and breathed, but God created the creature, as Gabriel's breath also precedes God's creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49/r13.anchor: وكان تسوية الطين والنفخ من عيسى والخلق من الله

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r1.speaker: رؤبة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r1.claim: Ruʾba's line uses الأكمه for one blind from birth.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r1.anchor: فارتد ارتداد الأكمه وقال ابن فارس:

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris says الكمه is blindness from birth, though it can occur later, and cites Suwayd's poem as evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن فارس: الكمه العمى يولد به الإنسان وقد يعرض

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the akmah sees during the day but not at night.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r3.anchor: مجاهد: هو الذي يبصر بالنهار ولا يبصر بالليل.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r4.claim: ʿIkrima calls him weak-sighted, but says linguistically the word means blindness, as in the cited verb forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r4.anchor: عكرمة: هو الأعمش، ولكنه في اللغة العمى

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r5.claim: Baras is the familiar white skin affliction; al-abrass al-qamar and sāmm abras are named creatures, and its plural is الأبارص.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r5.anchor: والبرص معروف وهو بياض يعتري الجلد

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r6.claim: These two diseases are singled out because they were incurable; since medicine predominated in Jesus's era, God gave him a miracle in that field.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r7.claim: An account the author leaves uncertain says Jesus revived four people: al-ʿĀdhir, a widow's son, a tax collector's daughter, and Noah's son Sam.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r7.anchor: قيل: أحيا أربعة أنفس: العاذر وكان صديقا له

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r8.claim: Al-ʿĀdhir, Jesus's friend, had died days earlier; Jesus prayed and he rose with his jugular dripping, lived, and had a child.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r8.anchor: فأما العاذر فإنه كان قد توفي قبل ذلك بأيام فدعا الله فقام بإذن الله

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r9.claim: A widow's son being carried on a bier rose at Jesus's prayer, dressed, carried the bier on his neck, and returned home.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r9.anchor: وأما ابن العجوز فإنه مر به يحمل على سريره فدعا الله فقام ولبس ثيابه

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r10.claim: A tax collector's daughter, dead since the previous night, revived at Jesus's prayer and later had a child.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r10.anchor: وأما بنت العاشر فكان أتى عليها ليلة فدعا الله فعاشت بعد ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r11.claim: When people challenged Jesus to revive Noah's son Sam, Sam emerged gray-haired; he said the call made him fear the Resurrection and death's agony still gripped his throat after more than four thousand years.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r11.anchor: فخرج من قبره وقد شاب رأسه. فقال له عيسى: كيف شاب رأسك

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r12.claim: Sam's revival persuaded some to believe, while others rejected it as magic.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r12.anchor: فقال للقوم: صدقوه فإنه نبي فآمن به بعضهم وكذبه بعضهم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r13.speaker: إسمعيل ابن عياش
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r13.claim: A report transmitted by Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh says Jesus prayed two cycles, reciting Sūrat al-Mulk then al-Sajda, and invoked seven names.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r13.anchor: وروي من حديث إسمعيل ابن عياش قال: حدثني محمد بن طلحة عن رجل

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r14.speaker: البيهقي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r14.claim: Al-Bayhaqī includes the prayer report but says its chain is not strong.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r14.anchor: ذكره البيهقي وقال: ليس إسناده بالقوي.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r15.claim: أنبئكم means telling them what they ate and stored. After the resurrections they asked for another sign: what they ate at home and saved for tomorrow.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r15.anchor: أي بالذي تأكلونه وما تدخرون. وذلك أنهم لما أحيا لهم الموتى

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r16.speaker: مجاهد والزهري والسختياني
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r16.claim: Mujāhid, al-Zuhrī, and al-Sakhtiyānī read وما تذخرون with dhāl and without doubling.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r16.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد والزهري والسختياني «وما تذخرون» بالذال المعجمة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r17.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r17.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and others say Jesus told schoolchildren what they had stored, so their fathers stopped them sitting with him.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r17.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وغيره: كان يخبر الصبيان في الكتاب بما يدخرون

QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r18.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r18.claim: Qatāda says Jesus told them what they had eaten from the table and secretly stored from it.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:48-49#2/r18.anchor: قتادة: أخبرهم بما أكلوه من المائدة

QASHANI:3:47-50/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:47-50/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:47-50/r4.claim: Jesus is a messenger to spiritually prepared people among Jacob's spiritual descendants.
QASHANI:3:47-50/r4.anchor: إلى المستعدين الروحانيين من أسباط يعقوب الروح

QASHANI:3:47-50/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:47-50/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:47-50/r5.claim: Jesus' sign demonstrates that he comes from God.
QASHANI:3:47-50/r5.anchor: تدل على أني آتيكم من عنده

QASHANI:3:47-50/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:47-50/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:47-50/r6.claim: Creating from clay means educating, purifying, and training deficient prepared souls; the bird-shape is a soul yearning to fly toward holiness.
QASHANI:3:47-50/r6.anchor: بالتربية والتزكية والحكمة العملية من طين نفوس المستعدين الناقصين

QASHANI:3:47-50/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:47-50/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:47-50/r7.claim: Breathing into it imparts divine knowledge and true life through companionship and training; it becomes a living soul flying to God on longing and aspiration.
QASHANI:3:47-50/r7.anchor: من نفث العلم الإلهي ونفس الحياة الحقيقية بتأثير الصحبة والتربية

QASHANI:3:47-50/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:47-50/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:47-50/r8.claim: The blind is veiled from truth, with an unopened inner eye; the leper is afflicted by vices, false beliefs, world-love, and desire, treated by spiritual medicine.
QASHANI:3:47-50/r8.anchor: المحجوب عن نور الحق الذي لم تنفتح عين بصيرته قط ولم تبصر شمس وجه الحق

QASHANI:3:47-50/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:47-50/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:47-50/r9.claim: The leper is defective through vice, false belief, love of the world, and desire's stain.
QASHANI:3:47-50/r9.anchor: المعيوب نفسه بمرض الرذائل والعقائد الفاسدة ومحبة الدنيا

QASHANI:3:47-50/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:47-50/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:47-50/r10.claim: Raising the dead signifies reviving ignorance with the life of knowledge, by God's permission.
QASHANI:3:47-50/r10.anchor: موتى الجهل بحياة العلم { بإذن الله

QASHANI:3:47-50/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:47-50/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:47-50/r11.claim: What people eat is what they take through desire; what they store is the hidden motives and intentions within them.
QASHANI:3:47-50/r11.anchor: تتناولون من مباشرة الشهوات واللذات { وما تدخرون في بيوتكم } أي: في بيوت غيوبكم

RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r1.claim: One parse supplies “We send him”: Jesus is taught the scriptures and then sent as a messenger to Israel, saying that he has brought a sign.
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r1.anchor: تقدير الآية : ونعلمه الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل ونبعثه رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل

RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj prefers supplying “he speaks to people as a messenger”; the phrase that follows gives the content of Jesus' speech to them.
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : الاختيار عندي أن تقديره : ويكلم الناس رسولا ، وإنما أضمرنا ذلك لقوله

RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r3.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash allows the conjunction wāw to be extra, making “messenger to the Children of Israel” describe Jesus after the mention of his teachings.
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r3.anchor: قال الأخفش : إن شئت جعلت الواو زائدة ، والتقدير : ويعلمه الكتاب والحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r4.claim: Rāzī takes the verse to make Jesus a messenger to all the Children of Israel, contrary to some Jews' claim that he was sent only to a particular group.
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r4.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان رسولا إلى كل بني إسرائيل بخلاف قول بعض اليهود

RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r5.claim: “A sign” means the class of signs, not one individual sign, since the verse lists raising the dead, healing, and disclosure of unseen matters.
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r5.anchor: المراد بالآية الجنس لا الفرد لأنه تعالى عدد ههنا أنواعا من الآيات

RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r6.speaker: حمزة
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r6.claim: Ḥamza opens the hamza in innī, making the clause “I create” an apposition explaining the sign Jesus brought.
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة { إنى } بفتح الهمزة ، وقرأ نافع

RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r7.speaker: نافع
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ breaks the hamza; the clause may either begin a new sentence or explain what the sign is.
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع بكسر الهمزة فمن فتح { إنى } فقد جعلها بدلا من آية

RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r8.claim: For the broken-hamza reading, Rāzī prefers treating the clause as an explanation of the sign, parallel to explanatory clauses in 48:29 and 3:59; this matches the open reading's sense.
RAZI-FULL:v8p48#2/r8.anchor: وهذا الوجه أحسن لأنه في المعنى كقراءة من فتح { إنى } على جعله بدلا من آية

RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r1.claim: Rāzī argues that khalq here means forming and measuring: humans do not create ex nihilo, “best of creators” means best estimators, and other verses use the root for fabricating lies.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r1.anchor: الذي يدل عليه القرآن والشعر والاستشهاد ، أما القرآن فآيات أحدها

RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r2.claim: If “created” in 2:29 meant bringing into existence, it would say everything on earth had already been created in the past; Rāzī therefore takes it as prior measuring of what now exists.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r2.anchor: فإذن وجب حمل الخلق على التقدير حتى يصح الكلام

RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r3.claim: Rāzī cites two poetic lines as evidence for shaping or measuring in khalq; the excerpt names no poet.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r3.anchor: ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبع ض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r4.claim: Arabic usage supports measuring and smoothing: one shapes a sandal to size; khallāq is a measure of good, khalīq denotes a due measure, and smooth rock is called khalqāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49/r4.anchor: يقال : خلق النعل إذا قدرها وسواها بالقياس والخلاق المقدار من الخير

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله البصري
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Baṣrī denies that al-Khāliq is literally a divine name, since estimation and adjustment would mean conjecture, which is impossible for God.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله البصري : إنه لا يجوز إطلاقه على الله في الحقيقة ، لأن التقدير والتسوية عبارة عن الظن والحسبان

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r2.claim: Rāzī's theological school says al-Khāliq belongs only to God, citing “God is creator of everything” and “Is there any creator besides God who provides?”
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r2.anchor: وقال أصحابنا : الخالق ، ليس إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r3.claim: Rāzī says 35:3 alone does not prove that no one is a creator: it denies a creator other than God who has the specified role of providing from heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r3.anchor: وهذا ضعيف ، لأنه تعالى قال : { هل من خالق غير الله يرزقكم من السماء }

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r4.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r4.claim: In response to al-Baṣrī, Rāzī's school says estimation can mean knowledge; conjecture is impossible for God, but knowledge is not.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r4.anchor: وأجابوا عن كلام أبي عبد الله بأن التقدير والتسوية عبارة عن العلم والظن

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r5.claim: In this verse “I create” means “I form and measure”; hayʾa is the formed image, from the verb meaning to prepare or shape.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r5.anchor: { أنى أخلق لكم من الطين } معناه : أصور وأقدر وقوله { كهيئة الطير } فالهيئة الصورة المهيئة

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r6.claim: The pronoun in “I breathe into it” refers to the shaped clay.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r6.anchor: وقوله { فأنفخ فيه } أي في ذلك الطين المصور

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r7.speaker: نافع
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ reads the resulting bird in the singular; the other readers have the plural, as at 5:110, while ṭayr can denote one bird or many.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r7.anchor: قرأ نافع { فيكون } بالألف على الواحد ، والباقون { عليهم طيرا } على الجمع

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r8.claim: It is narrated that when Jesus claimed prophethood, challengers demanded a bat; he fashioned and breathed into clay, and it flew between heaven and earth.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r8.anchor: يروى أن عيسى عليه السلام لما ادعى النبوة ، وأظهر المعجزات أخذوا يتعنتون عليه

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r9.speaker: وهب
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r9.claim: Wahb says the bird flew while people could see it but fell dead once it disappeared from their sight.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r9.anchor: قال وهب : كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون إليه ، فإذا غاب عن أعينهم سقط ميتا

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r10.claim: Some said Jesus made only a bat, matching Nāfiʿ's reading; others said he made several kinds of bird, matching the other readers' plural.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r10.anchor: ثم اختلف الناس فقال قوم : إنه لم يخلق غير الخفاش ، وكانت قراءة نافع عليه

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r11.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r11.claim: Some theologians infer from the breath that the spirit is a subtle body like wind.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r11.anchor: قال بعض المتكلمين : الآية تدل على أن الروح جسم رقيق كالريح

RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r12.claim: Rāzī says God, not Jesus' breath, created life in the clay as a miracle: only God gives life and death, as 67:2 and Abraham's argument in 2:258 show.
RAZI-FULL:v8p49#2/r12.anchor: وهذا الثاني هو الحق لقوله تعالى : { الذي خلق الموت والحيواة }

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r1.claim: Jesus' own birth was through Gabriel's breath into Mary; since Gabriel is pure spirit, Rāzī says Jesus' breath likewise concerned life and spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r1.anchor: القرآن دل على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام إنما تولد من نفخ جبريل عليه السلام في مريم

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r2.claim: “By God's permission” means God's bringing into being, as in 3:145; Jesus adds the phrase to ward off suspicions of divinity and identify life as God's miracle through a messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r2.anchor: قوله { بإذن الله } معناه بتكوين الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r3.speaker: أكثر أهل اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r3.claim: Most lexicographers say al-akmah is someone born blind.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r3.anchor: ذهب أكثر أهل اللغة إلى أن الأكمه هو الذي ولد أعمى

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r4.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl and other authorities instead define al-akmah as someone who became blind after having sight.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r4.anchor: وقال الخليل وغيره هو الذي عمي بعد أن كان بصيرا

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r5.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r5.claim: Mujāhid says al-akmah means someone who cannot see at night.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r5.anchor: وعن مجاهد هو الذي لا يبصر بالليل

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r6.claim: Rāzī notes a claim that the only akmah in this community was Qatāda b. Diʿāma al-Sadūsī, the Qur'an commentator.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r6.anchor: ويقال : إنه لم يكن في هذه الأمة أكمه غير قتادة بن دعامة السدوسي صاحب ( التفسير )

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r7.claim: A report says fifty thousand sick people gathered around Jesus; those able came to him, while he visited those unable to come, and treated them only by prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r7.anchor: وروي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ربما اجتمع عليه خمسون ألفا من المرضى من أطاق منهم أتاه

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r8.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī says Jesus raised Lazarus with “O Living, O Self-subsisting,” called Sām b. Noah from his grave, and revived an old woman's dead son, who returned home and had a child.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r8.anchor: قال الكلبي : كان عيسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r9.claim: The repeated qualification “by God's permission” removes the suspicion that Jesus is divine.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r9.anchor: وقوله { بإذن الله } رفع لتوهم من اعتقد فيه الإلاهية

RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r10.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r10.claim: Al-Suddī reports that Jesus foretold children's deeds and hidden food while playing; parents hid the children, lied that the house held pigs, and Jesus said they would be pigs, whereupon they became so.
RAZI-FULL:v8p50/r10.anchor: روى السدي : أنه كان يلعب مع الصبيان

RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r1.claim: A second view says Jesus' disclosures began when the table descended: the people had been forbidden to store food but were hiding provisions.
RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r1.anchor: والقول الثاني : إن الإخبار عن الغيوب إنما ظهر وقت نزول المائدة

RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r2.claim: Unassisted foreknowledge without prior questions or instruments is a miracle from God; astrologers need questions and tools and still admit frequent error.
RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r2.anchor: الإخبار عن الغيوب على هذا الوجه معجزة ، وذلك لأن المنجمين الذين يدعون استخراج الخير

RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r3.claim: These five powerful signs establish the claimant's truth for anyone who accepts miracles as proof; Brahmins reject that premise, but believers have no remaining objection.
RAZI-FULL:v8p51/r3.anchor: في هذه الخمسة لمعجزة قاهرة قوية دالة على صدق المدعي لكل من آمن بدلائل المعجزة

QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r1.claim: When people reproached Mary, God made Jesus speak on his first day; he presented signs including raising the dead, healing the blind and leper, and revealing their secret deeds.
QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r1.anchor: أنطق الله عيسى عليه السلام وهو ابن يوم

QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r2.claim: Jesus confirmed earlier revealed laws while receiving a law that abrogated some earlier rulings and retained others, as the Qur'an specifies.
QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r2.anchor: وأخبر أنه مصدق لما تقدمه من الشرائع ، ومختص بشريعة تنسخ بعض ما تقدمه

QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r12.claim: The revealed account teaches Muhammad its meanings by revelation, not by requiring him to acquire them through analogy or inference.
QUSHAYRI:v1p149/r12.anchor: نعرفك معانيه بما نوحي إليك ، لا بتكلفك ما تصل إلى علمه

STUDYQURAN:3:49/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r1.claim: The miracles in this verse are discussed further at 5:110, where similar points are made.
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r1.anchor: For a discussion of the miracles mentioned in this verse, see 5:110c

STUDYQURAN:3:49/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r2.speaker: Some opinions
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r2.claim: One minority view takes the blind to mean people who can see by day but not at night.
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r2.anchor: some opinions record that the blind are those who can see during the day, but not at night

STUDYQURAN:3:49/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r3.speaker: Some opinions
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r3.claim: Another minority interpretation identifies the blind as people with bleary eyes, al-aʿmash.

STUDYQURAN:3:49/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r4.speaker: Most commentators
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r4.claim: Most commentators understand the blind to mean people born blind.
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r4.anchor: most commentators understand it to refer to those who are born blind

STUDYQURAN:3:49/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r5.claim: Leprosy was widely known in the ancient world, disfiguring people and damaging nerves; it was highly contagious and until recently medically incurable.
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r5.anchor: leprosy was widely known in the ancient world, causing severe disfigurement and nerve damage, and was highly contagious

STUDYQURAN:3:49/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r6.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r6.claim: Some relate that as a child Jesus told playmates or classmates what their parents were doing or keeping in their houses.
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r6.anchor: some relate that as a child Jesus would tell his playmates or his classmates about what their parents were doing

STUDYQURAN:3:49/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r7.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r7.claim: Others say this disclosure occurred when people were forbidden to store food in their houses.
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r7.anchor: others say that this was in relation to a time when the people were forbidden to store up food in their houses

STUDYQURAN:3:49/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r8.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r8.claim: Another account connects the disclosure to the table of food in 5:112–115: people were told not to store any feast food, did so, and were chastised.
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r8.anchor: Others say that this refers to the table onto which food descended in 5:112–15

STUDYQURAN:3:49/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r9.claim: Both Quran and Bible accept Jesus’ raising the dead, while the Quran stresses that raising the dead and animating the clay bird were miracles by God’s Leave; the clay-bird miracle is absent from the New Testament.
STUDYQURAN:3:49/r9.anchor: the Quran emphasizes the fact that both Jesus’ giving life to the clay bird (not found in the New Testament) and his raising of the dead were miracles

TAB-FULL:v5p418/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p418/r1.claim: The syntax ellipses “and We make him” before “a messenger,” supplied by the context; al-Tabari supports this omission with a line of poetry.
TAB-FULL:v5p418/r1.anchor: لدلالة الكلام عليه، كما قال الشاعر: [البحر الكامل]

TAB-FULL:v5p418/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p418/r2.claim: Jesus is made a messenger to Israel as prophet, bearer of good news and warning; his sign from God verifies his statement and proves he is God's messenger.
TAB-FULL:v5p418/r2.anchor: بمعنى: ونجعله رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل بأنه نبي وبشير ونذير؛ وحجتي عن صدقي على ذلك أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم

TAB-FULL:v5p418/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418/r3.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
TAB-FULL:v5p418/r3.claim: Ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says the sign establishes Jesus's prophethood and that he is God's messenger to them.
TAB-FULL:v5p418/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير: {ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم} [آل عمران: 49] «أي تحقق بها نبوتي

TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r1.claim: The sign is Jesus's making a bird form from clay and breathing into it; ṭayr is the plural of ṭāʾir.
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r1.anchor: فتأويل الكلام: ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل بأني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم بأن أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير، والطير جمع طائر.

TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r2.speaker: بعض أهل الحجاز
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r2.claim: Some Hijazi readers use the singular in both places: “like the form of a bird,” then “it becomes a bird.”

TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the plural in both places because it describes Jesus's repeated act, agrees with the muṣḥaf spelling, and is a sound, widely transmitted reading.
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r3.anchor: وأعجب القراءات إلي في ذلك قراءة من قرأ: {كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا} [آل عمران: 49] على الجماع فيهما جميعا؛

TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that as a boy Jesus formed clay into a bird at the scribal school, breathed into it by God's leave, and it flew; the boys spread the news, and his mother later fled with him from the Israelites.
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r4.anchor: قال: ثنا ابن إسحاق " أن عيسى، صلوات الله عليه، جلس يوما مع غلمان من الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r5.claim: The same account says Jesus asked which bird was hardest to create; he was told the bat and made one from clay.
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r5.anchor: وذكر أنه لما أراد أن يخلق الطير من الطين سألهم: أي الطير أشد خلقا؟ فقيل له الخفاش

TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that Jesus asked which bird was hardest to create; they answered the bat because it is only flesh, and he made one.
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قوله: {أني أخلق

TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r7.claim: “I breathe into it” refers to the bird, though “into it” with feminine agreement would also be valid, referring to the form; al-Tabari compares the parallel in al-Māʾida and Arabic usage.
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r7.anchor: قيل: لأن معنى الكلام: فأنفخ في الطير، ولو كان ذلك: فأنفخ فيها، كان صحيحا جائزا

TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r8.claim: Al-Tabari notes a reading without fī, “fa-anfukh-hā,” and cites Arab usage and a basīṭ-meter poem for this construction.
TAB-FULL:v5p418#2/r8.anchor: وقد تفعل العرب مثل ذلك فتقول: رب ليلة قد بتها وبت فيها

TAB-FULL:v5p421/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r1.claim: The verb abrīʾu means “I heal”: Arabic says God healed the sick person, and uses both bariʾa forms for recovery.
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r1.anchor: فهو يبرئه إبراء، وبرأ المريض فهو يبرأ برءا،

TAB-FULL:v5p421/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r2.claim: Mujahid defines al-akmah as one who sees in daylight but cannot see at night.
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وأبرئ الأكمه} [آل عمران: 49] قال: " الأكمه: الذي يبصر بالنهار، ولا يبصر بالليل

TAB-FULL:v5p421/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r3.claim: Qatada says al-akmah is someone born blind with the eyes closed.
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: «كنا نحدث أن الأكمه، الذي ولد وهو أعمى مضموم العينين»

TAB-FULL:v5p421/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas also defines al-akmah as one born blind.
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " الأكمه: الذي يولد

TAB-FULL:v5p421/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r5.speaker: السدي، ابن عباس، قتادة، الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r5.claim: Al-Suddi, Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Hasan report the gloss “the blind,” without the narrower specification of birth with closed eyes.

TAB-FULL:v5p421/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v5p421/r6.claim: Other interpreters say al-akmah means al-aʿmash, one with weak or dim eyesight.

TAB-FULL:v5p423/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r1.claim: Ikrima defines al-akmah as al-aʿmash, one with dim or weak eyesight.
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {وأبرئ الأكمه} [آل عمران: 49] قال: «الأعمش»

TAB-FULL:v5p423/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r2.claim: Al-Tabari says the established Arabic sense is blindness; he supports this with Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil's word kamihat and Ruʾba's word al-akmah.
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r2.anchor: والمعروف عند العرب من معنى الكمه: العمى، يقال منه: كمهت عينه، فهي تكمه كمها

TAB-FULL:v5p423/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r3.speaker: سويد بن أبي كاهل
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r3.claim: Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil's cited line uses kamihat of eyes becoming white, serving as poetic evidence for the blindness sense.
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r3.anchor: كما قال سويد بن أبي كاهل: [البحر الرمل] كمهت عيناه حتى ابيضتا … فهو يلحى نفسه لما نزع

TAB-FULL:v5p423/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r4.speaker: رؤبة
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r4.claim: Ruʾba's cited line uses al-akmah, also attesting the Arabic association with blindness.
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r4.anchor: ومنه قول رؤبة: [البحر الرجز] هرجت فارتد ارتداد الأكمه … في غائلات الحائر المتهته

TAB-FULL:v5p423/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r5.claim: Jesus cites healing the blind and leprous as proof of prophethood: these conditions have no medical cure, so their healing is a miracle granted by God.
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r5.anchor: أن الكمه والبرص لا علاج لهما،

TAB-FULL:v5p423/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r6.claim: Al-Tabari rejects Ikrima's dim-sightedness and Mujahid's night-blindness readings: ordinary treatment could cure those conditions, so they would not be an unanswerable sign.
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r6.anchor: فأما ما قال عكرمة، من أن الكمه العمش،

TAB-FULL:v5p423/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r7.claim: He concludes al-akmah is one blind both day and night, most like Qatada's person born so; human beings cannot claim to treat such blindness, as with leprosy.
TAB-FULL:v5p423/r7.anchor: وهو بما قال قتادة: من أنه المولود كذلك أشبه؛ لأن علاج مثل ذلك لا يدعيه أحد من البشر

TAB-FULL:v5p424/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p424/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v5p424/r1.claim: Wahb reports Jesus returned from Egypt at twelve, lived in Syria until thirty, prophesied three years, then was raised; crowds of up to fifty thousand sick gathered, and he healed them by prayer, going to those unable to reach him.
TAB-FULL:v5p424/r1.anchor: قال: ثني عبد الصمد بن معقل أنه سمع وهب بن منبه، يقول: «لما صار عيسى ابن اثنتي عشرة سنة

TAB-FULL:v5p424/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p424/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p424/r2.claim: Jesus says he can tell them what they eat without having witnessed it and what they hide rather than consume; this hidden knowledge is another proof of his prophethood.
TAB-FULL:v5p424/r2.anchor: وأما قوله: {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون} [آل عمران: 49] فإنه يعني: وأخبركم بما تأكلونه مما لم أعاينه وأشاهده معكم في وقت أكلكموه

TAB-FULL:v5p424/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p424/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p424/r3.claim: Unlike astrologers and soothsayers, whose occasional correct disclosures come through inferential methods or spirit helpers, Jesus and the prophets receive unseen knowledge directly from God without prior means or trickery.
TAB-FULL:v5p424/r3.anchor: وإنما كان عيسى يخبر به عن غير استخراج ولا طلب لمعرفته باحتيال، ولكن ابتداء بإعلام الله إياه من غير أصل تقدم ذلك

TAB-FULL:v5p427/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says that when Jesus was nine or ten, his mother sent him to school; the teacher found the boy already knew each lesson before it was taught.
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r1.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " لما بلغ عيسى تسع سنين أو عشرا أو نحو ذلك، أدخلته أمه الكتاب فيما يزعمون

TAB-FULL:v5p427/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Jesus learned Torah and, while playing with the village boys, told them what their fathers were doing.
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r2.anchor: عن السدي: «لما كبر عيسى أسلمته أمه يتعلم التوراة، فكان يلعب مع الغلمان غلمان القرية

TAB-FULL:v5p427/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Jesus told boys at school what their families had eaten or stored; he could tell a boy what food his family had hidden and ask him to share it.
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم} [آل عمران: 49] قال: «كان عيسى ابن مريم إذ كان في الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v5p427/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r4.claim: Prophetic proofs may concern matters people can in principle reach through some stratagem, but prophets disclose them in a way no human can reach by stratagem apart from God.
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r4.anchor: فهكذا فعل الأنبياء وحججها إنما تأتي بما أتت به من الحجيج بما قد يوصل إليه ببعض الحيل، على غير الوجه الذي يأتي به غيرها

TAB-FULL:v5p427/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses the disclosure as what people ate the previous night and what they hid from it; Jesus is the speaker.
TAB-FULL:v5p427/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم} [آل عمران: 49] قال: «بما أكلتم البارحة

TAB-FULL:v5p428/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r1.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ says Jesus disclosed the food and other things people secretly stored in their houses, knowledge God had given him.
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال عطاء بن أبي رباح يعني قوله: {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم}

TAB-FULL:v5p428/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ glosses the phrase as what people ate the night before and what food they had hidden.
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r2.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم} [آل عمران: 49] قال: " ما تأكلون: ما أكلتم البارحة

TAB-FULL:v5p428/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r3.claim: Al-Suddi reports that Jesus exposed what boys' families ate and stored; when parents called him a sorcerer and hid their sons in a room, he said they would become pigs, and they were pigs when the room opened.
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " كان - يعني عيسى ابن مريم - يحدث الغلمان

TAB-FULL:v5p428/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the stored things are what people hide out of fear that the One who withholds may not replace them.
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {وما تدخرون في بيوتكم} [آل عمران: 49] قال: «ما تخبئون مخافة الذي يمسك أن لا يخلفه شيء»

TAB-FULL:v5p428/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r5.claim: Qatada gives another setting: people asked for a heavenly table of fruit, were ordered not to hide or save any for tomorrow, and Jesus exposed those who broke the test.
TAB-FULL:v5p428/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم} [آل عمران: 49] «فكان القوم لما سألوا المائدة

TAB-FULL:v5p430/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r1.claim: Jesus raised the dead by supplicating to God for them, and God answered his prayer.
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون} [آل عمران: 49] قال

TAB-FULL:v5p430/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r2.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r2.claim: A report from Ammar says the table followers were told to eat without storing food; they stored and betrayed, so they were made swine, as warned in 5:115.
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، عن خلاس بن عمرو، عن عمار بن ياسر ذلك

TAB-FULL:v5p430/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r3.claim: Yaddakhirūn derives from the iftiʿāl form of dhakhara; adjacent dhāl and tāʾ assimilate into a doubled dāl because pronouncing both is difficult.
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r3.anchor: وأصل يدخرون من الفعل يفتعلون، من قول القائل: ذخرت الشيء بالذال، فأنا أذخره

TAB-FULL:v5p430/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r4.claim: The transmitted reading assimilates dhāl into tāʾ, yielding doubled dāl; some Arabs instead assimilate tāʾ into dhāl, but the widely transmitted reading is the only admissible one.
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r4.anchor: وإبدالهما دالا مشددة لا يجوز القراءة بغيرها لتظاهر النقل من القراء بها

TAB-FULL:v5p430/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r5.speaker: زهير
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r5.claim: Zuhayr's line is reported with either ẓāʾ or ṭāʾ in yظلم, illustrating alternate forms of iftiʿāl from ظلم.
TAB-FULL:v5p430/r5.anchor: يروى بالظاء، يريد: فيفتعل من الظلم، ويروى بالطاء أيضا

SULAMI:v1p100#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p100#3/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p100#3/r1.claim: The gloss speaks of one encompassed by lordly attributes and effaced from personal attributes, living by himself and giving life through Him; its wording is unclear in the source.
SULAMI:v1p100#3/r1.anchor: قيل : من اشتملت عليه صفات الربوبية وغاب عن أوصاف لا يجدن حيي بنفسه وأحيي به كل شيء

SULAMI:v1p100#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p100#3/r2.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p100#3/r2.claim: The verse refutes claims that someone manifests a miracle independently of God's permission: God can manifest miracles at any time and through whomever He wills, while bodies and forms are only their instrument.
SULAMI:v1p100#3/r2.anchor: وأبطل بهذه الآية دعاوى من ادعى إظهار معجزة عليه به دون إذن ربه ، فالله قادر على الإعجاز في جميع الأوقات

TABRISI:3:48-49/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r3.speaker: نافع
TABRISI:3:48-49/r3.claim: Nafiʿ reads innī akhluqu with kasra on the hamza; other readers use fatḥa.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r3.anchor: قرأ نافع إني أخلق بكسر الألف والباقون أني بالفتح

TABRISI:3:48-49/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r4.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب وأبو جعفر
TABRISI:3:48-49/r4.claim: Medina and Yaʿqub read ṭāʾiran; Abu Jaʿfar reads ka-hayʾat al-ṭāʾir in both places; other readers have ṭayran without alif.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r4.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب طائرا ومثله في المائدة وأبو جعفر كهيئة الطائر فيهما

TABRISI:3:48-49/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r6.claim: With fatḥa, annī is appositional to āya; with kasra it may begin a new clause or explain the sign, the latter being better because it has the same sense as apposition.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r6.anchor: ومن كسر أحتمل وجهين أحدهما: الاستئناف وقطع الكلام مما قبله

TABRISI:3:48-49/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r7.claim: The singular ṭāʾiran can describe each thing shaped and breathed into as a bird, as “flog them eighty lashes” means eighty lashes for each person.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ طائرا أراد فيكون ما أنفخ فيه أو ما أخلقه طائرا

TABRISI:3:48-49/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r9.claim: The source notes ordinary ṭīn, using clay to seal a letter and coating a house with clay as examples of the related verb ṭayyana.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r9.anchor: والطين معروف وطنت الكتاب جعلت عليه طينا لأختمه به

TABRISI:3:48-49/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r10.claim: Hayʾa means the visible state or form of something.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r10.anchor: والهيئة الحال الظاهرة هاء فلان يهاء هيئة

TABRISI:3:48-49/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r11.claim: Nafkh means blowing, and naffākha can refer to a bubble of water.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r11.anchor: والنفخ معروف نفخ ينفخ نفخا والنفاخة للماء

TABRISI:3:48-49/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r12.claim: Al-akmah means the blind; Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil’s poem depicts eyes becoming white.

TABRISI:3:48-49/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r13.claim: Iddikhār is an iftiʿāl verbal noun from d-kh-r; grammarians also permit tadhkharūn with dhāl.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r13.anchor: والادخار الافتعال من الدخر وجوز النحويون تذخرون بالذال

TABRISI:3:48-49/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r15.claim: Rasūlan is accusative after an omitted “and We make him,” or as a circumstantial phrase for his future mission; al-Zajjaj paraphrases it as speaking to them as a messenger.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r15.anchor: ورسولا نصب على تقدير ونجعله رسولا فحذف لدلالة البشارة عليه

TABRISI:3:48-49/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r16.claim: Annī akhluqu can be genitive as apposition to āya or nominative; al-Zajjaj says the kasra reading means “I say: I have come to you.”
TABRISI:3:48-49/r16.anchor: وموضع أني أخلق لكم يحتمل أن يكون خفضا ورفعا فالخفض على البدل من آية

TABRISI:3:48-49/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49/r17.claim: Mā can be a relative pronoun (“what you eat and store”) or a verbal noun (“your eating and storing”); the relative reading is better.
TABRISI:3:48-49/r17.anchor: وبما تأكلون جائز أن يكون ما هنا بمعنى الذي أي بما تأكلونه وتدخرونه

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r7.claim: The account of Mary and Jesus’s birth is interrupted here; the rest of Mary’s story comes in Surat Maryam, and the commentary now begins Jesus’s story.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r7.anchor: وقطع ها هنا قصة مريم وولادتها ويأتي تمام قصتها في سورة مريم

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r8.claim: Jesus addressed the Children of Israel when he was sent to them, saying he had come to them.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r8.anchor: أي قال لهم وكلمهم لما بعث إليهم بأني قد جئتكم

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r9.claim: The sign is evidence and proof pointing to Jesus’s prophethood.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r9.anchor: أي بدلالة وحجة { من ربكم } دالة على نبوتي

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r10.claim: Here create means to shape and form from clay an image resembling a bird.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r10.anchor: معناه وهذه الآية أني أقدر لكم وأصور لكم من الطين مثل صورة الطير

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r11.claim: The pronoun in فيه refers to the bird-shaped form made from clay; elsewhere the feminine pronoun refers to the fashioned shape.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r11.anchor: أي في الطير المقدر من الطين وقال في موضع آخر فيها

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r12.claim: Permission means God’s power or command: shaping clay and blowing are within human ability, but making it living flesh and blood is God’s act alone.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r12.anchor: لأن تصور الطين على هيئة الطير والنفخ فيه مما يدخل تحت مقدور العباد

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r13.claim: The exegetical account says Jesus made a bat-shaped figure from clay, blew into it, and it became a bird.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r13.anchor: وفي التفسير أنه صنع من الطين كهيئة الخفاش ونفخ فيه فصار طائرا

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r14.claim: Al-akmah is a person born blind.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r14.anchor: أي الذي ولد أعمى عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r15.speaker: الحسن والسدي
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r15.claim: Another reported definition of al-akmah is simply a blind person.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r15.anchor: وقيل هو الأعمى عن الحسن والسدي

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r16.claim: The leper is one afflicted with whiteness of the skin.

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r17.speaker: وهب
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r17.claim: Wahb says as many as fifty thousand sick people could gather for Jesus in a day; he went to those unable to reach him and treated them by prayer conditional on faith.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r17.anchor: وقال وهب وربما اجتمع على عيسى من المرض في اليوم خمسون ألفا

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r18.claim: Jesus’s reviving the dead is attribution by metaphor and extension: God revived them in response to Jesus’s prayer.
