TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r18.anchor: إنما أضاف الإحياء إلى نفسه على وجه المجاز والتوسع ولأن الله تعالى كان يحيي الموتى

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r19.claim: The account says Jesus revived Lazarus, a friend dead three days; Lazarus emerged from his grave and later lived and had a child.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r19.anchor: وقيل أنه أحيى أربعة أنفس عازر وكان صديقا له وكان قد مات منذ ثلاثة أيام

TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r20.claim: The same account says Jesus revived the son of an old woman and the tax collector’s daughter; both lived and had children.
TABRISI:3:48-49#2/r20.anchor: وابن العجوز مر به ميتا على سيره فدعا الله عيسى ع فجلس على سريره

TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r1.claim: Jesus revived Sam son of Noah by invoking God’s greatest name; Sam, whose hair turned half gray, asked whether the Resurrection had begun and requested protection from death’s agonies.
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r1.anchor: وسام بن نوح دعا عليه باسم الله الأعظم فخرج من قبره وقد شاب نصف رأسه

TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says Jesus revived the dead by calling, O Living One, O Sustainer.
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كان يحيي الأموات بيا حي يا قوم

TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r3.claim: God matched Jesus’s signs to medicine, Moses’s to magic, and Muhammad’s Quran to his age’s eloquence, so each people faced a miracle in its own field that they could not match.
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r3.anchor: لأن الغالب كان في زمانه الطب فأراهم الله الآيات من جنس ما هم عليه

TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r4.claim: Jesus told people what they had eaten and stored for later, such as their midday meal and what they saved until evening.
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r4.anchor: أي أخبركم بالذي تأكلون وتدخرونه كأن يقول للرجل تغديت بكذا وكذا

TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r5.claim: The things Jesus described are a proof, miracle, and sign for his audience.
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r5.anchor: أي فيما ذكرت لكم { لآية } أي حجة ومعجزة ودلالة

TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r6.claim: The sign benefits believers in God, since knowledge of the sender must precede knowledge of the messenger for the miracle’s implication to be known.
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r6.anchor: لأن العلم بالمرسل لا بد أن يكون قبل العلم بالرسول

TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r7.claim: The verse indicates that Jesus was sent to all the Children of Israel.
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r7.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن عيسى ع كان مبعوثا إلى جميع بني إسرائيل

TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r8.claim: The wording I create shows that a human servant originates, acts, and creates, against the Mujbira; God remains the absolute Creator.
TABRISI:3:48-49#3/r8.anchor: يدل على أن العبد يحدث ويفعل ويخلق خلافا لقول المجبرة لكن الخالق على الإطلاق هو الله تعالى

FARRA:v1p215/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p215/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p215/r1.claim: For تدخرون from ذخرت, a light reading on the تفعَل pattern is also reported alongside the doubled form.
FARRA:v1p215/r1.anchor: وقوله: (وما تدخرون) هي تفتعلون من ذخرت، وتقرأ

FARRA:v1p215/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p215/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p215/r2.claim: Some Arabs alternate د and ذ in iftiʿāl forms; examples include مظلم/مطلم and مذكر/مدكر.
FARRA:v1p215/r2.anchor: وبعض العرب يقول: تدخرون فيجعل الدال والذال يعتقبان

FARRA:v1p215/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p215/r3.speaker: بعض بني أسد
FARRA:v1p215/r3.claim: The alternation is especially common among Banū Asad: al-Farrāʾ heard one say اتغر, while other Arabs say اثغر.
FARRA:v1p215/r3.anchor: وسمعت بعض بني أسد يقول: قد اتغر

FARRA:v1p215/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p215/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p215/r4.claim: When a quiescent ت meets ذ, assimilation can obscure the iftiʿāl pattern, so speakers choose د as an intermediate consonant.
FARRA:v1p215/r4.anchor: فأما الذين يقولون: يدخر ويدكر ومدكر فإنهم وجدوا التاء إذا سكنت

FARRA:v1p215/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p215/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p215/r5.claim: Other speakers fully assimilate the ت into ذ; this follows the regular rule even though it obscures the form’s single-consonant origin.
FARRA:v1p215/r5.anchor: وأما الذين غلبوا الذال فأمضوا القياس،

FARRA:v1p215/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p215/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p215/r6.claim: Arabic also uses an intermediate consonant in ازدجر for ازتجر; some instead say مزجر, letting ز dominate.
FARRA:v1p215/r6.anchor: فقد قالوا: ازدجر ومعناها: ازتجر، فجعلوا الدال عدلا

FARRA:v1p215/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p215/r7.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v1p215/r7.claim: Some say مزجر, with ز dominating ت, as another example of consonant alternation.

FARRA:v1p215/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p215/r8.speaker: بعض بني عقيل
FARRA:v1p215/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ heard Banū ʿUqayl advise using the urine of gazelles as a drink, with ص in اصعطها prevailing over ت.
FARRA:v1p215/r8.anchor: وسمعت بعض بني عقيل يقول: عليك بأبوال الظباء فاصعطها

FARRA:v1p215/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p215/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p215/r9.claim: In standard speech, ت of iftiʿāl becomes ط after ص or ض, as in اضطر from الضرر and اصطبر.
FARRA:v1p215/r9.anchor: وتاء الافتعال تصير مع الصاد والضاد طاء، كذلك الفصيح

THALABI:v3p71/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r1.speaker: الكسائي
THALABI:v3p71/r1.claim: Al-Kisa'i says the opening vowel follows because the message is attached to the sending, while another explanation supplies بأني or لأني.
THALABI:v3p71/r1.anchor: قال الكسائي: وإنما فتح لأنه أوقع الرسالة عليه وقيل: بأني أو لأني

THALABI:v3p71/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r2.speaker: الخليل والفراء
THALABI:v3p71/r2.claim: Al-Khalil and al-Farra say the form originally had a doubled yā; the difficult doubling was lightened because the preceding vowel was open.
THALABI:v3p71/r2.anchor: قال الخليل والفراء: أصلها بآية بتشديد الياء فثقل عليهم التشديد فأبدلوا لانفتاح ما قبل التشديد

THALABI:v3p71/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r3.speaker: الكسائي
THALABI:v3p71/r3.claim: Al-Kisa'i gives another derivation for the word, comparing its original form to Fatima and explaining that one of the two yā letters was omitted.
THALABI:v3p71/r3.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هي في الأصل أبيه مثل فاطمة فحذفت أحدى الياءين

THALABI:v3p71/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r4.speaker: نافع والباقون
THALABI:v3p71/r4.claim: Nafi reads إني with kasra as a new sentence with an implied verb of saying; the other readers use fatḥa, meaning بأني.
THALABI:v3p71/r4.anchor: قول نافع بكسر الألف على الاستئناف وإضمار القول. وقرأ الباقون بالفتح على معنى بأني

THALABI:v3p71/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p71/r5.claim: The sign from God confirms Jesus' claim and establishes his message.
THALABI:v3p71/r5.anchor: قد جئتكم بآية: والآية من ربكم: يصدق قولي ويحقق رسالتي

THALABI:v3p71/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p71/r6.claim: Here أخلق means to form and determine.

THALABI:v3p71/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r7.speaker: الزهري وأبو جعفر
THALABI:v3p71/r7.claim: Al-Zuhri and Abu Jaafar read كهية with a doubled yā; the other readers use كهيئة with hamza.
THALABI:v3p71/r7.anchor: قرأ الزهري وأبو جعفر: كهية بتشديد الياء. والآخرون بالهمزة

THALABI:v3p71/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p71/r8.claim: Hay'a is a prepared image or form, from the verb meaning to prepare and set something right.
THALABI:v3p71/r8.anchor: والهيئة الصورة المهيأة، وهي من قولهم هيأت الشيء إذا قصرته وأصلحته

THALABI:v3p71/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر والباقون
THALABI:v3p71/r9.claim: Abu Jaafar reads الطائر with alif, while the remaining readers read الطير without it.
THALABI:v3p71/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر (الطائر) بالألف، والباقون بغير ألف

THALABI:v3p71/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p71/r10.claim: The pronoun in فأَنْفُخُ فيه refers to the clay.

THALABI:v3p71/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r11.speaker: أهل المدينة والعامة
THALABI:v3p71/r11.claim: Most readers use the plural طيرا because Jesus created many birds; the Medinan reading is singular طائرا, referring to one kind of bird.
THALABI:v3p71/r11.anchor: قرأه العامة على الجمع لأنه خلق طيرا كثيرا

THALABI:v3p71/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p71/r12.claim: The singular reading is explained by the claim that Jesus created only the bat, singled out as a remarkably complete bird with breasts, teeth, menstruation, and flight.
THALABI:v3p71/r12.anchor: لأنه لم يخلق غير الخفاش، وإنما خص الخفاش لأنه أكمل الطير خلقا

THALABI:v3p71/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r13.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v3p71/r13.claim: Wahb says the clay bird flew while people watched and fell dead when they looked away, distinguishing human craft from God's creation and perfection.
THALABI:v3p71/r13.anchor: وقال وهب: كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون إليه، فإذا غاب عن أعينهم سقط ميتا

THALABI:v3p71/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p71/r14.claim: وأبرئ means that Jesus heals and restores the sick to health.
THALABI:v3p71/r14.anchor: وأبرئ الأكمه والأبرص: أي أشفيهما وأصححهما

THALABI:v3p71/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r15.speaker: عكرمة والأعمش ومجاهد والضحاك
THALABI:v3p71/r15.claim: Ikrima, al-A'mash, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak define al-akmah as someone who sees by day but cannot see at night.
THALABI:v3p71/r15.anchor: فقال عكرمة والأعمش، ومجاهد والضحاك: [هو الذي] يبصر بالنهار ولا يبصر بالليل

THALABI:v3p71/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r16.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
THALABI:v3p71/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada define al-akmah as someone born blind who never saw light.
THALABI:v3p71/r16.anchor: ابن عباس وقتادة: هو الذي ولد أعمى ولم يبصر ضوء قط

THALABI:v3p71/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p71/r17.speaker: الحسن والسدي والخليل
THALABI:v3p71/r17.claim: Hasan and al-Suddi say al-akmah means blind; al-Khalil, as cited by al-Zajjaj, says it includes one born blind or one who later loses sight.
THALABI:v3p71/r17.anchor: الحسن والسدي: هو [الأعمى، وحكى الزجاج عن الخليل أن الأكمه هو الذي يولد أعمى

THALABI:v3p72/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p72/r1.speaker: سويد بن أبي كاهل
THALABI:v3p72/r1.claim: Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil's line uses the eyes turning white to illustrate the loss of sight associated with akmah.
THALABI:v3p72/r1.anchor: قال سويد بن أبي كاهل: كمهت عيناه حتى ابيضتا

THALABI:v3p72/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p72/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p72/r2.claim: Al-abrass is a person afflicted with white skin patches or discoloration.

THALABI:v3p72/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p72/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p72/r3.claim: Because medicine was prominent in Jesus' time, God gave him a miracle in that field: curing conditions for which medicine had no remedy.
THALABI:v3p72/r3.anchor: وكان [الغالب] على زمن عيسى الطب فأراهم الله المعجزة من جنس ذلك داعيا لا دواء له

THALABI:v3p72/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p72/r4.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v3p72/r4.claim: Wahb says fifty thousand sick people gathered in one day; Jesus walked to those unable to come, and healed them by supplication on condition of faith.
THALABI:v3p72/r4.anchor: وقال وهب: ثم اجتمع على عيسى من المرضى في اليوم الواحد خمسون ألفا

THALABI:v3p72/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p72/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p72/r5.claim: One account says Jesus raised his friend Lazarus after three days in the grave; Lazarus emerged with his veins dripping, lived, and had children.
THALABI:v3p72/r5.anchor: قيل: أحيا أربعة أنفس: عازر وكان صديقا فأرسل أخته إلى عيسى أن أخاك عازر يموت

THALABI:v3p72/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p72/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p72/r6.claim: Jesus raised a widow's son from a funeral bier; the young man sat up, dressed, carried the bier home, and lived to have children.
THALABI:v3p72/r6.anchor: وابن العجوز مر به ميتا على عيسى (عليه السلام) على سرير يحمل فدعا الله عيسى (عليه السلام)

THALABI:v3p72/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p72/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p72/r7.claim: Jesus revived a girl who had been dead since the previous day; she lived and bore a child.
THALABI:v3p72/r7.anchor: والبنت العاقر قيل له: أتحييها وقد ماتت أمس؟ فدعا الله فعاشت

THALABI:v3p72/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p72/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p72/r8.claim: Jesus revived Shem son of Noah by the greatest name; Shem, half his head gray, asked whether the Resurrection had come, then requested protection from death's agonies before dying again.
THALABI:v3p72/r8.anchor: وسام بن نوح دعا عيسى (عليه السلام) باسم الله الأعظم فخرج من قبره وقد شاب نصف رأسه

THALABI:v3p72/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p72/r9.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v3p72/r9.claim: Al-Kalbi says Jesus raised the dead by invoking God as Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum.
THALABI:v3p72/r9.anchor: قال الكلبي: كان عيسى (عليه السلام) يحيي الأموات ب: يا حي يا قيوم

THALABI:v3p73/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p73/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p73/r1.claim: Anabbi'ukum means inform you; what you eat is what Jesus observes, and what you store is what you put away in your homes until eating it.
THALABI:v3p73/r1.anchor: وأنبئكم: أخبركم، بما تأكلون: مما أعاينه، وما تدخرون: وما ترزمونه، في بيوتكم

THALABI:v3p73/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p73/r2.speaker: مجاهد وأيوب السختياني
THALABI:v3p73/r2.claim: Mujahid and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani read تذخرون with dhāl, its sukūn, and a fatḥa on khāʾ, from the verb ذخر.
THALABI:v3p73/r2.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وأيوب السختياني: تذخرون، بالذال المعجمة وسكونها وفتح الخاء

THALABI:v3p73/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p73/r3.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v3p73/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says that after Jesus healed and raised the dead, people called it magic and challenged him to tell what they ate and stored; he named their midday and evening meals.
THALABI:v3p73/r3.anchor: قال الكلبي: فلما أبرأ عيسى الأكمه والأبرص وأحيى الموتى قالوا: هذا سحر، ولكن أخبرنا بما نأكل

THALABI:v3p73/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p73/r4.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v3p73/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says Jesus told schoolboys what their families had eaten and stored; when they repeated it, their parents hid them, called Jesus a sorcerer, and denied the boys were there.
THALABI:v3p73/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: كان عيسى (عليه السلام) إذا كان في الكتاب يحدث الغلمان بما يصنع أبوهم

THALABI:v3p73/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p73/r5.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v3p73/r5.claim: In al-Suddi's account, Jesus declared the hidden boys would become pigs; they did, provoking Israelite hostility, and Mary fled with him to Egypt.
THALABI:v3p73/r5.anchor: قال عيسى: كذلك يكونون. ففتحوا عليهم، فإذا هم خنازير

THALABI:v3p73/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p73/r6.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v3p73/r6.claim: Qatada says the event concerned the heavenly table spread with manna and quail: people were forbidden to hoard food for tomorrow, but Jesus exposed what they ate and saved, and they were transformed into pigs.
THALABI:v3p73/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: إنما هذا في المائدة وكان خوانا ينزل عليهم إنما كانوا كالمن والسلوى

THALABI:v3p73/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p73/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p73/r7.claim: In that refers to what Jesus has just described.
THALABI:v3p73/r7.anchor: إن في ذلك الذي ذكرت لكم

THALABI:v3p73/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p73/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p73/r8.claim: The participle meaning confirming is coordinated with رسولا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq gives one parse of rasūlan as coordinated with a verb meaning “make him a messenger.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬2): ينتصب على وجهين: أحدهما: (ويجعله (¬3) رسولا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers parsing rasūlan with “speaks to the people,” since the following words mean “I have come to you”; Jesus addresses them as a messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬2): ينتصب على وجهين: أحدهما: (ويجعله (¬3) رسولا). قال: والاختيار عندي: أنه (ويكلم الناس رسولا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r3.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash allows an inserted conjunction and takes rasūlan as a circumstantial accusative describing the pronoun in “we teach him the Book.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r3.anchor: وقال الأخفش (¬6): إن شئت جعلت الواو في {ورسولا} مقحمة (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r4.claim: Although the wording says one sign, Jesus brought several: forming a bird, curing the blind-born and leper, raising the dead, and telling what people ate. The author takes bird-making as the sign, then treats the cures and other miracles as a new sentence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p266/r4.anchor: وهي: خلق الطير، وإبراء الأكمه والأبرص، وإحياء الموتى، وإنباء (¬2) بما يأكلون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r1.claim: With fatḥ on annī, the clause is an appositive to āya, understood as “I came to you with my creating”; it may be genitive as an appositive or nominative with the sense “the sign is that I create.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r1.anchor: كأنه قال: (وجئتكم بأني أخلق لكم من الطين)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r2.claim: With kasr on innī, one parse starts a new sentence and breaks it from what precedes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r2.anchor: ومن كسر (¬9)، فله وجهان: أحدهما: الاستئناف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r3.claim: The other kasr parse makes “I create for you” explain the sign; the author prefers it because it matches the fatḥ reading in meaning, as in the cited explanatory clauses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p267/r3.anchor: وهذا الوجه أحسن؛ لأنه في المعنى كقراءة من فتح (أني)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r1.claim: Here create means to determine and shape; in Arabic, creation can mean estimation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r1.anchor: أخلق لكم من الطين} أي: أقدر، وأصور. والخلق، معناه: التقدير في اللغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r2.claim: Hayʾa means a formed image, from the verb “to shape or determine a thing.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r3.claim: Ṭayr may be masculine when treated as a collective noun or feminine when treated as a group noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r3.anchor: و (الطير): يجوز تذكيره، على معنى الجمع، وتأنيثه، على معنى الجماعة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r4.claim: The pronoun cannot refer to the general word clay: the breath goes into a particular piece shaped from clay, not all the clay previously mentioned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تعود (¬2) الكناية (¬3) إلى الطين؛ لأن النفخ إنما يكون في طين مخصوص

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r5.claim: One possible antecedent is the shaped object: “the form” stands for the thing possessing that form, as “the portion” can mean what is apportioned in 4:8.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تعود الكناية على ذي الهيئة. وأريد ب (الهيئة): ذو الهيئة، كما أريد ب (القسمة): المقسوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r6.claim: Abu Ali's option lets the pronoun refer to the creation implied by “I create,” with creation standing for the created thing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r6.anchor: فيكون قوله: {فأنفخ فيه}؛ أي: في الخلق، ويكون الخلق بمنزلة المخلوق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r7.claim: It can instead refer to the likeness implied by the kāf: the meaning is “I create a creation like the form of a bird,” with the kāf describing an implied verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p268/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن تعود إلى ما دل عليه الكاف من معنى المثل؛ لأن المعنى: أخلق من الطين مثل هيئة الطير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r1.speaker: نافع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r1.claim: Nafi reads ṭāʾiran; it can mean that what Jesus blows into or forms becomes a bird, or that each thing formed becomes a bird, as in the expression “eighty lashes” for each person receiving eighty.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r2.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r2.claim: Some say Nafi chose the singular because Jesus created only one kind of bird, the bat, which they regarded as the most fully formed bird.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم (¬4): ذهب نافع (¬5) إلى نوع واحد من الطير؛ لأنه لم يخلق غير الخفاش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r3.speaker: وهب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r3.claim: Wahb reports that the bird flew while people watched, then fell dead when it went out of their sight.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r3.anchor: قال وهب: كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r4.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī assigns bariʾtu to Tamim speech and baraʾtu to the people of the Hijaz.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r4.anchor: قال الأصمعي (¬2): برئت من المرض: لغة تميم، وبرأت: لغة أهل الحجاز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r5.claim: Abu Zayd reverses the regional attribution for baraʾtu and says the rest of the Arabs use bariʾtu.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r5.anchor: وقال أبو زيد (¬4): برأت من المرض: لغة أهل الحجاز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada define al-akmah as someone born blind who never saw light.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وقتادة (¬2): هو الذي ولد أعمى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p270/r7.claim: Al-abraṣ is a person afflicted with a white skin patch or discoloration.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi recounts that Jesus revived Lazarus, his friend; called Sam son of Noah from his grave; and prayed for a dead young man on a bier, who rose, returned to his family, lived, and had children.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي (¬6): كان (¬7) عيسى عليه السلام يحيي الأموات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r2.claim: In “what you eat and store,” mā means “that which”: what you eat and what you store.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r3.claim: A tafsir gloss says Jesus told them what they ate in the morning and what they kept for the rest of the day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r3.anchor: وجاء (¬3) في التفسير: بما تأكلون في غدوكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r4.claim: Taddakhirūn is on the iftaʿala pattern from dhukhr, “storing”: the original iztakhara changes tāʾ to voiced dāl after voiced dhāl, then assimilates dhāl into dāl. The author gives similar consonant adjustments in izdajara, iḍṭarra, and iṣṭabara.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r5.speaker: الخليل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r5.claim: Al-Khalil defines a voiced consonant as one articulated with firm contact that blocks breath, and a voiceless consonant as one with weaker contact through which breath flows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p273/r5.anchor: قال الخليل (¬1): الحرف (¬2) المجهور: الذي أشبع (¬3) الاعتماد (¬4) عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r1.claim: The phrase means that Jesus is also made a messenger to the Children of Israel.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r1.anchor: أي: ويجعله رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r2.claim: The word annī here means that he came to them with a sign from his Lord.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r2.anchor: أني } أي: بأني { قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r3.claim: Creating the bird-like form means measuring and shaping it into the bird’s likeness.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r5.claim: Al-abraṣ is someone with al-ḍaḥ, a white skin patch.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r5.anchor: والأبرص } أي: الذي به وضح [أي: بياض]

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r6.claim: He tells them what they eat in the morning.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r6.anchor: في غدوكم { وما } كم { تدخرون } لباقي يومكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:49-50/r7.claim: He tells them what they store for the remainder of the day.

ELMALILI:3:47-51/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r5.claim: Repeatedly qualifying Jesus's miracles as occurring by God's permission strongly directs them to the Creator's divinity, against Christian claims of Jesus's divinity.
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r5.anchor: Mucizelerde بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ kayıdlarının tekrarı bunların Nasârâ’nın iddiası vechile Îsâ’nın ulûhiyetine değil, hâlıkının ulûhiyetine delâlet edeceklerini kuvvetle beyan içindir.

ELMALILI:3:47-51/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r6.claim: Jesus was a divinely appointed Word and a sign of God through his nature, character, knowledge, wisdom, scripture, writing, actions, and speech; he came as a messenger to Israel.

ELMALILI:3:47-51/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r7.claim: Jesus's four miracles challenged supposedly unchangeable custom: shaping a bird from clay, healing the blind and lepers, raising the dead, and reporting what people ate and stored.
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r7.anchor: Benî İsrâil’e bir resul olarak gelecek, değişmez zannedilen âdetler hilâfına dört mucize gösterip imana davet edecek

ELMALILI:3:47-51/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r9.claim: All Jesus's miracles and his entire mission served one message: fear and obey God, his and their Lord, worship Him alone, and follow the straight path.
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r9.anchor: bütün mucizelerinin gayesi tek bir âyete vukuftan ibaret olduğunu söyleyecekti ki bu âyet de şu idi: Allah’tan korkunuz ve bana itaat ediniz

ELMALILI:3:47-51/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r10.claim: Whether the annunciation and divine promise were fulfilled needs no separate inquiry: God does not break His promise, the angels are truthful, and Mary received the answer directly.
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r10.anchor: meleklerin yalan söylemeyecekleri müsellem olmakla beraber

ELMALILI:3:47-51/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r11.claim: The qualification minhu, the angels' announcement, and Be, and it is establish that the Word's realization was certain.
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r11.anchor: kelimenin hayâl olmadığını anlatmak için مِنْهُ ile mukayyed olması, melâike ile gelmesi, tahakkukuna delil olduğu gibi كُن فَيَكُونُ’daki فَيَكُونُ da bu babda şüpheye mahal bırakmamış

ELMALILI:3:47-51/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r13.claim: Jesus actually came with the described identity, qualities, religion, and call, and his whole life and mission expressed this single message.
ELMALILI:3:47-51/r13.anchor: Îsâ bu hüviyet, bu ahvâl ve evsâf ve bu dîn ü davetle bir resul olarak وَجِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ

MAJAZ:v1p93/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p93/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p93/r1.claim: Al-akmah is someone born blind; Ruʾba’s poem uses akmah for blindness and its return.
MAJAZ:v1p93/r1.anchor: الأكمه» (49) : الذي يولد من أمه أعمى، قال رؤبة: وكيد مطال وخصم منده ... هرجت فارتد ارتداد الأكمه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r1.speaker: bazı yahudiler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r1.claim: Some Jews claimed Jesus was sent only to a particular Israelite community rather than to all Israelites.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r2.claim: The verse shows that Jesus was sent to all Israelites, not one particular community; Razi is cited, with 2:40 referenced for background on Israel.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r2.anchor: İsrâiloğulları’ndan muayyen bir topluma değil onların tamamına gönderildiğini göstermektedir (Râzî, VIII, 54

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r3.claim: The miracles mattered to Jesus’s contemporaries, but later Christian conclusions about them became dangerous; the verse and 5:110 repeatedly stress that they depended on God’s permission.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r3.anchor: bunların yüce Allah’ın iznine bağlı olduğuna sık sık dikkat çekilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r4.claim: Because a prophet is human and God supplies the extraordinary signs that support his claim to bring revelation, overlooking this dependence empties faith in the prophet of value and leads to misguidance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r4.anchor: peygamberin bir beşer olduğu ve gösterdiği bütün olağan üstü hallerin Allah’tan mesaj getirdiği iddiasını desteklemek için yine O’nun tarafından sağlandığı göz ardı edilirse

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r5.claim: Christians wrongly deified Jesus instead of attributing the miracles to the absolute power of God, thereby building religious life on a corrupt foundation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r5.anchor: hıristiyanlar bu olağan üstü durumları bütün evrenin yaratıcısı olan yüce Allah’ın mutlak kudretine bağlamak yerine, Hz. Îsâ’yı tanrılaştırma yoluna girmişler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r6.claim: The dialogue in 5:110–118 makes clear that Jesus could not have told people to make him and his mother gods.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r6.anchor: Mâide sûresinin 110-118. âyetlerinde karşılıklı konuşma üslûbu içinde Hz. Îsâ’nın insanlara “Beni ve annemi tanrı edinin” demiş olamayacağı ortaya konur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r7.claim: The reminder is addressed especially to the Najran delegation and generally to advocates of beliefs containing association with God: Jesus’s message rested on tawhid.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r7.anchor: özelde Necran heyetine, genelde Allah’a ortak koşma unsuru içeren bütün inançların savunucularına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r8.claim: The authors render abras as “leper,” identifying it as a type of skin disease.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r8.anchor: “Cüzzamlı” şeklinde tercüme ettiğimiz abras kelimesi, bir tür cilt hastalığını ifade eder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r9.claim: The common dictionary sense also allows “mottled” or “afflicted with alaca,” though the authors prefer leprosy or its onset based on dictionary material and historical evidence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r9.anchor: Yaygın sözlük anlamı esas alınarak bu kelimeyi “alacalı, alaca hastalığına tutulmuş” şeklinde çevirmek mümkündür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r10.claim: Dictionary material cited from Butrus al-Bustani and historical evidence support the interpretation as leprosy or an incipient form of it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r10.anchor: Fakat bazı sözlüklerdeki bilgiler (Butrus el-Büstânî, Muhîtü’l-muhît, “brs” md.) ve tarihî veriler burada cüzzam veya cüzzam başlangıcı bir hastalığın kastedildiği görüşünü destekleyici niteliktedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r11.claim: Leprosy caused great anxiety and received detailed attention in the Torah, making Jesus’s healing of such patients a particularly significant miracle.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:49/r11.anchor: o dönemde toplumda büyük tedirginlik yaratan, Tevrat’ın da ayrıntılı hükümler getirerek özel bir biçimde ilgilendiği bir hastalık türü olduğundan

BAQILLANI:v1p59/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p59/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p59/r1.claim: The objection that rhymed prose may freely vary its cadence fails: a mismatched span makes the composition disordered, which cannot characterize Qur'anic eloquence.
BAQILLANI:v1p59/r1.anchor: وقد علم أن فصاحة القرآن غير مذمومة في الأصل فلا يجوز أن يقع فيها نحو هذا الوجه من الاضطراب

BAQILLANI:v1p59/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p59/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p59/r2.claim: Metered poetry and Qur'anic phrases such as 3:49 can resemble sajʿ without being sajʿ; familiar sajʿ would not have baffled its hearers.
BAQILLANI:v1p59/r2.anchor: وقد يتفق في الشعر كلام متزن على منهاج السجع

BAQILLANI:v1p59/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p59/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p59/r3.claim: Because sajʿ was a familiar convention, it cannot explain the Qur'an's challenge; the hearers' bewilderment and calling it magic show its form exceeded their customary styles.
BAQILLANI:v1p59/r3.anchor: وليس القوم بعاجزين عن تلك الأساليب المعتادة عندهم المألوفة لديهم

BURHAN:v4p190/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p190/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p190/r1.claim: The suddenness particle fa-idhā may be a noun functioning as a place adverb or a particle with an omitted predicate; because a time adverb cannot predicate of a person here, the noun must denote place.
BURHAN:v4p190/r1.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون في هذه الحالة ظرف زمان لامتناع وقوع الزمان خبرا عن الجثة وإذا امتنع إن تكون للزمان تعين إن تكون مكانا

NAHHAS:v1p378/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p378/r3.speaker: قول أول
NAHHAS:v1p378/r3.claim: One analysis estimates yajʿaluhu rasūlan: “and He makes him a messenger.”
NAHHAS:v1p378/r3.anchor: في نصبه قولان أحدهما أن التقدير ويجعله رسولا

NAHHAS:v1p378/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p378/r4.speaker: قول ثان
NAHHAS:v1p378/r4.claim: A second analysis estimates yukallimuhum rasūlan: “and he speaks to them as a messenger.”
NAHHAS:v1p378/r4.anchor: والآخر ويكلمهم رسولا ( أني قد جئتكم ) أي بأني فأن في موضع نصب

NAHHAS:v1p378/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p378/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p378/r5.claim: Anni qad jiʾtukum means “that I have come to you”; anna is in the accusative after an implied bi.
NAHHAS:v1p378/r5.anchor: أي بأني فأن في موضع نصب ( أني أخلق لكم من الطين

NAHHAS:v1p378/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p378/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p378/r6.claim: The clause anni akhluqu is appositional to the preceding anna; it can be genitive as an apposition to āya, or nominative after an implied huwa, “it is that I create.”
NAHHAS:v1p378/r6.anchor: بدل منها ويجوز أن يكون في موضع خفض على البدل من آية ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع

NAHHAS:v1p378/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p378/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p378/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans read hayʾat al-ṭayr … ṭayran; Yazīd reads hayʾat al-ṭāʾir … ṭāʾiran, and Nāfiʿ combines ṭayr with ṭāʾiran. The first two readings are clearer; ṭayr can be masculine or feminine, with singular ṭāʾir or ṭayr.
NAHHAS:v1p378/r7.anchor: هذه قراءة أبي عمرو وأهل الكوفة وقرأ يزيد بن القعقاع ( كهيئة الطائر فأنفخ فيه فيكون طائرا )

NAHHAS:v1p378/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p378/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p378/r8.claim: Mā in bimā taʾkulūna can be a relative pronoun (“what you eat”) or a verbal noun with its verb.
NAHHAS:v1p378/r8.anchor: أي بالذي تأكلونه ويجوز أن يكون ما والفعل مصدرا ( وما تدخرون )

NAHHAS:v1p378/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p378/r9.speaker: مجاهد والزهري وأيوب السختياني
NAHHAS:v1p378/r9.claim: Mujāhid, al-Zuhrī, and Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī read tadhkharūna with ḏāl, lightly pronounced.
NAHHAS:v1p378/r9.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد والزهري وأيوب السختياني ( وما تذخرون ) بالذال معجمة مخففا

NAHHAS:v1p378/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p378/r10.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p378/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ derives the form from tadhkhartum and says the difficult t-dh cluster prompted substitution and assimilation; al-Naḥḥās rejects this, since assimilation should make the first consonant yield to the second.
NAHHAS:v1p378/r10.anchor: قال الفراء أصلها الذال يعني تذخرون من ذخرت فالأصل تذتخرون فثقل على اللسان

NAHHAS:v1p378/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p378/r11.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p378/r11.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh explain the standard form by replacing the breathy t with voiced d beside voiced ḏ, producing tḏdakhkharūna and then taddakharūna; reversing the assimilation to tadhkharūna is possible but not preferred.
NAHHAS:v1p378/r11.anchor: والصواب في هذا مذهب الخليل وسيبويه أن الذال حرف مجهور يمنع النفس أن يجري والتاء حرف مهموس

ITQAN:v2p489/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p489/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p489/r1.claim: The letter ك can function as a noun meaning “likeness,” occupy a grammatical case, and take a pronoun referring back to it.
ITQAN:v2p489/r1.anchor: ترد الكاف إسما بمعنى مثل فتكون في محل إعراب ويعود عليها الضمير

ITQAN:v2p489/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p489/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v2p489/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says فيه refers to the noun-like ك in كهيئة: Jesus blows into the modeled object, which then becomes an ordinary bird.
ITQAN:v2p489/r2.anchor: أي فأنفخ في ذلك الشيء المماثل فيصير كسائر الطيور

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r3.claim: A second sense is restoring the dead after their souls have departed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحياة في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

TABATABAI:3:42-60#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#4/r5.claim: Although Jesus' special message was to Israel, this does not limit his prophethood to Israel: prophethood conveys religion, while messengership is a particular mission whose acceptance brings salvation and rejection brings judgment.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#4/r5.anchor: النبوة هي منصب البعث والتبليغ والرسالة هي السفارة الخاصة التي تستتبع الحكم والقضاء بالحق بين الناس

TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r1.claim: Moses and Jesus could address peoples beyond Israel: Moses was sent to Pharaoh, whose magicians and people were not Israelites, and non-Israelite peoples also accepted Jesus.

TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r2.claim: Jesus was accepted by Romans and other western peoples, and eastern groups such as Najran, though they were not Israelites; the Qur'an discusses Christians generally rather than only Israelite Christians.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r2.anchor: آمن به عليه السلام قبل بعثة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الروم وأمم عظيمة من الغربيين

TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r3.claim: Creation here means assembling the parts of a thing, and the wording permits the term creator to be used of someone other than God, as in the Qur'an's phrase best of creators.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r3.anchor: الخلق جمع أجزاء الشيء وفيه نسبة الخلق إلى غيره تعالى كما يشعر به أيضا قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r4.claim: Al-akmah is someone born blind, and can also mean one who later loses sight; al-Raghib gives this sense and a cited poetic line witnesses the latter usage.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r4.anchor: والأكمه هو الذي يولد مطموس العين وقد يقال لمن تذهب عينه

TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r5.claim: Al-abras is a person with baras, a known skin disease.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r5.anchor: والأبرص من كان به برص وهو مرض جلدي معروف

TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r6.claim: The plural wording for the dead at least suggests that Jesus raised multiple people.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r6.anchor: حيث علق الإحياء بالموتى وهو جمع دلالة ولا أقل من الإشعار بالكثرة والتعدد

TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r7.claim: By God's permission stresses that Jesus' miracles came from God and that he was not independent in them; the repeated qualification guards against people inferring that he was divine.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r7.anchor: لما كان من المترقب أن يضل فيه الناس فيعتقدوا بألوهيته استدلالا بالآيات المعجزة الصادرة عنه

TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r8.claim: The wording indicates Jesus actually performed these signs, rather than merely mentioning them as hypothetical proof; a mere challenge would have been qualified with a condition such as if you asked.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#5/r8.anchor: أن هذه الآيات كانت تصدر عنه صدورا خارجيا لا أن الكلام مسوق لمجرد الاحتجاج والتحدي

TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r1.claim: Some say the verse proves only that Jesus could perform the signs if asked, not that any occurred; al-Tabataba'i rejects this limitation.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r1.anchor: فساد ما ذكره بعضهم أن قصارى ما تدل عليه الآية أن الله سبحانه جعل في عيسى ابن مريم هذا السر

TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r2.claim: Jesus's report of what people ate and stored was a further, explicit and verifiable disclosure of unseen knowledge, which belongs to God and those messengers He informs.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r2.anchor: وهذا إخبار بالغيب المختص بالله تعالى ومن خصه من رسله بالوحي وهو آية أخرى

TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r3.claim: The permission formula is omitted for this announcement because it is speech performed by Jesus, whereas creating and reviving are truly God's acts attributed to others only by His permission.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r3.anchor: عبر عنها بالإنباء وهو كلام قائم بعيسى عليه السلام يعد فعلا له فلا يليق أن يسند إلى ساحة القدس

TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r4.claim: Creating birds and reviving the dead could mislead simple listeners into deifying Jesus, while people may treat hidden knowledge as attainable by ascetics or soothsayers; hence those signs require the permission qualifier.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r4.anchor: فإن القلوب الساذجة تقبل ألوهية خالق الطير ومحيي الموتى بأدنى وسوسة ومغلطة

TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r5.claim: For healing, simply identifying it as God's sign suffices; Jesus addresses people who claim belief and challenges them to be sincere in that claim.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#6/r5.anchor: أي إن كنتم صادقين في دعواكم الإيمان

TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r3.claim: He omits the many reports about Mary’s annunciation and Jesus’s birth, mission, and miracles because the Qur’anic narrative already supplies what matters for exegesis, except for reports worth noting.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r3.anchor: واعلم أن هناك روايات كثيرة في بشارة مريم وولادة عيسى عليه السلام ودعوته ومعجزاته لكن ما وقع في الآيات الشريفة من جمل قصصه كاف فيما هو المهم من البحث التفسيري ولذلك تركنا ذكرها إلا ما يهم ذكره منها

TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r4.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r4.claim: Al-Bāqir reports that Jesus offered to disclose what Israelites had eaten before leaving home and stored overnight; some accepted his truthful sign and believed, while others disbelieved.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r4.anchor: فكان يقول أنت أكلت كذا وكذا وشربت كذا وكذا ورفعت كذا وكذا فمنهم من يقبل منه فيؤمن ومنهم من يكفر

TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r1.claim: The change in how Jesus’s signs are narrated, at the beginning and end of the passage, supports the report about his disclosure of what people ate and stored.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r1.anchor: أقول وتغيير سياق الآية في حكاية ما ذكره عليه السلام من الآيات أولا وآخرا يؤيد هذه الرواية

TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r6.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r6.claim: Al-Riḍā presents the popular explanation that the disciples were called ḥawāriyyūn because they laundered and whitened clothes, with the term linked to al-ḥiwār bread.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r6.anchor: أما عند الناس فإنهم سموا حواريين لأنهم كانوا قصارين يخلصون الثياب من الوسخ بالغسل وهو اسم مشتق من الخبز الحوار

TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r7.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r7.claim: Al-Riḍā gives the interpretation favored among the Imams: the disciples were sincere themselves and purified others from sin through exhortation and reminders.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r7.anchor: وأما عندنا فسمي الحواريون الحواريين لأنهم كانوا مخلصين في أنفسهم ومخلصين غيرهم من أوساخ الذنوب بالوعظ والتذكير

TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r8.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r8.claim: A report from al-Riḍā says the disciples numbered twelve and that Luke was the best and most knowledgeable among them.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r8.anchor: وفي التوحيد عنه عليه السلام إنهم كانوا اثنا عشر رجلا وكان أفضلهم وأعلمهم لوقا

TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r9.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r9.claim: Al-Ṣādiq reports that Jesus was entrusted with prophetic light and knowledge, sent to Jerusalem to call Israel to God’s book and wisdom, faced widespread rejection, and preached there for 33 years.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r9.anchor: وفي الإكمال عن الصادق عليه السلام في حديث بعث الله عيسى بن مريم واستودعه النور والعلم والحكم وجميع علوم الأنبياء قبله وزاده الإنجيل وبعثه إلى بيت المقدس إلى بني إسرائيل

TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r10.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r10.claim: The same report says the Jews claimed they tortured, buried, killed, and crucified Jesus, while insisting that God gave them no power over him and that it only appeared so.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#21/r10.anchor: وادعت أنها عذبته ودفنته في الأرض حيا وادعى بعضهم أنهم قتلوه وصلبوه وما كان الله ليجعل لهم سلطانا عليه وإنما شبه لهم

TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r1.claim: In the preceding report, Jesus’s transformation of people into devils means that a group of the wicked among them was transformed.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r1.anchor: أقول قوله عليه السلام فمسخ منهم شياطين أي مسخ جمعا من شرارهم

TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r2.claim: The stated 33 years may refer to Jesus’s lifespan, since he spoke to people from the cradle until maturity and was a prophet from childhood.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r2.anchor: لعله إشارة إلى مدة عمره على ما هو المشهور فإنه عليه السلام كان يكلمهم من المهد إلى الكهولة وكان نبيا من صباه

TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r3.claim: The account of Jesus speaking from the cradle points to the Qur’anic passage where he declares in infancy that God gave him scripture and made him a prophet.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#22/r3.anchor: فأشارت إليه قالوا كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا * قال إني عبد الله آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا

TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r1.speaker: أبو بصير
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r1.claim: Abū Baṣīr reports an Imam’s explanation that ʿAlī and Salmān were muhaddathūn: an angel comes to them and inscribes or taps something in the heart.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r1.anchor: عن أبي بصير عنه عليه السلام قال كان علي محدثا وكان سلمان محدثا

TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r2.speaker: حمران بن أعين
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r2.claim: Ḥumrān b. Aʿyan reports Abū Jaʿfar saying ʿAlī was muhaddath and that an angel spoke to him, without making him a prophet or messenger; the analogy is with the companions of Moses and Solomon and with Dhū al-Qarnayn.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r2.anchor: عن حمران بن أعين قال أخبرني أبو جعفر عليهما السلام أن عليا كان محدثا

TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says reports defining the muhaddath are numerous in Imāmī collections and also occur in Sunni sources.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r3.anchor: والروايات في معنى المحدث عن أئمة أهل البيت ع كثيرة جدا رواها في البصائر والكافي والكنز والاختصاص وغيرها ويوجد في روايات أهل السنة أيضا

TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r4.claim: Divine speech to a servant yields certain knowledge in itself, without inferential proof, like immediate knowledge that needs no syllogism.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r4.anchor: وأن الوحي بمعنى تكليم الله سبحانه لعبده فهو يوجب العلم اليقيني بنفس ذاته من غير حاجة إلى حجة فمثله في الإلقاءات الإلهية مثل العلوم البديهية

TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r5.claim: In these reports, prophetic “dreaming” is not an ordinary sleep dream but a swoon-like state in which the senses quiet, the prophet perceives as in waking, and God confirms the perception’s divine source.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r5.anchor: وأما المنام فالروايات كما ترى تفسره بمعنى غير المعنى المعهود منه أعني الرؤيا يراها الإنسان في النوم العادي العارض له في يومه وليلته بل هو حال يشبه الإغماء تسكن فيه حواس الإنسان النبي فيشاهد عند ذلك نظير ما نشاهده في اليقظة ثم يسدده الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r6.claim: Taḥdīth means hearing an angel’s voice with the heart’s hearing, not ordinary sensory hearing or a merely figurative mental impression; the muhaddath understands it as heard speech, though others cannot hear it.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r6.anchor: وأما التحديث فهو سماع صوت الملك غير أنه بسمع القلب دون سمع الحس وليس من قبيل الخطور الذهني الذي لا يسمى سمع صوت إلا بنحو من المجاز البعيد

TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r7.claim: God’s reassurance lets the muhaddath distinguish angelic speech from Satanic suggestion: falsehood is exposed by divine light, while satanic whispers unsettle the heart.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#23/r7.anchor: فذلك بتأييد من الله سبحانه وتسديده كما يشير إليه ما في رواية محمد بن مسلم المتقدمة أنه يعطى السكينة والوقار حتى يعلم أنه ملك وذلك أن النزغة الشيطانية إما باطل في صورته الباطلة عند الإنسان المؤمن

TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r1.claim: The believer’s God-given light exposes a Satanic suggestion even when it appears truthful; the source connects this light with being made alive after spiritual death.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r1.anchor: أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشى به في الناس

TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r2.claim: Satanic prompting brings inner agitation, while remembrance of God brings calm; the resulting tranquility or distress helps identify whether an inward message is divine or satanic.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r2.anchor: والنزغة والوسوسة مع ذلك كله لا تخلو عن اضطراب في النفس وتزلزل في القلب

TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r3.claim: Reports that a muhaddath hears an angel without seeing one mean that sight is not required; seeing an angel in a particular instance does not follow from being muhaddath.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r3.anchor: وأما ما في الروايات من أن المحدث يسمع الصوت ولا يعاين الملك فمحمول على الجهة دون التمانع بين المعنيين بمعنى أن الملاك في كون الإنسان محدثا أن يسمع الصوت من غير لزوم الرؤية

TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r4.claim: The Qur’an depicts Mary seeing the angel in human form while he announces Jesus’s birth, so angelic appearance can accompany divine communication.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r4.anchor: كقوله تعالى في مريم فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r5.claim: The Qur’an also depicts Abraham and his wife seeing the angels who bring the annunciation of Isaac and Jacob.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r5.anchor: ولقد جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا سلاما قال سلام

TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r6.claim: One proposed reconciliation is that the denied vision is seeing an angel’s actual essence, rather than seeing the form in which it appears; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes that the verses establish only the appearance.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r6.anchor: وها هنا وجه آخر وهو أن يكون المراد بالمعاينة المنفية معاينة حقيقة الملك في نفسه دون مثاله الذي يتمثل به فإن الآيات لا تثبت أزيد من معاينة المثال

TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r7.claim: A further proposal limits the denied vision to legislative revelation, preserving the lawgiving role of prophets and messengers; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī considers this explanation somewhat remote.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#24/r7.anchor: وها هنا وجه آخر ثالث احتمله بعضهم وهو أن المنفي من المعاينة الوحي التشريعي بأن يظهر للمحدث فيلقي إليه حكما شرعيا وذلك صون من الله لمقام المشرعين من أنبيائه ورسله ولا يخلو عن بعد

THALABI:v3p76/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p76/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p76/r1.claim: In the cloth story, Jesus produces garments in the requested colors; a disciple recognizes the miracle as from God, believes, and joins his companions as a disciple.
THALABI:v3p76/r1.anchor: فأخرج عيسى ثوبا أحمر وثوبا أصفر وثوبا أخضر إلى أن أخرجها على الألوان التي أرادها

THALABI:v3p76/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p76/r8.speaker: ابن عون
THALABI:v3p76/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAwn recounts that a king's serving bowl never diminished while Jesus ate; the king followed Jesus, along with his people, and they became disciples.
THALABI:v3p76/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عون: صنع ملك من الملوك طعاما.

BURHAN:v3p376/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p376/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p376/r7.claim: When reminding the Israelites of the bird formed from clay, God uses clay to magnify the favor and the miracle's importance to them.
BURHAN:v3p376/r7.anchor: ولما اراد سبحانه الامتنان على بني إسرائيل أخبرهم أن يخلق لهم من الطين كهيئة الطير تعظيما لأمر ما يخلقه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1030/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1030/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1030/r1.claim: In context, Moses was given signs to confront Pharaoh, not yet-revealed scripture: his tablets came after leaving Egypt, so his challenge used miracles such as the staff and hand; Jesus likewise challenged through signs, and these are the two cases described this way.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1030/r1.anchor: الأمر كان يتعلق بالإيتاء وليس بالإنزال بالنسبة لموسى يتعلق بالمعجزة كالعصا واليد في تسع آيات

NASHR:v2p240/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p240/r3.speaker: المدنيان
NASHR:v2p240/r3.claim: The two Medinans read أَنِّي with kasra on the hamza; the others read it with fatḥa. Ibn Mihran's attribution of kasra to Nafi alone is called erroneous.
NASHR:v2p240/r3.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان بكسر الهمزة، وقرأ الباقون بفتحها

NASHR:v2p240/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p240/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p240/r4.claim: Abu Jafar reads الطائر and فيكون طائرا with alif and hamza at both sites; Nafi and Yaqub join him on طائرا, while the rest read the unhamzated collective طيرا. One Hanbali route eases the hamza between two sounds in all four forms.
NASHR:v2p240/r4.anchor: (الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا) فقرأ أبو جعفر (الطائر)

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r12.claim: Ṭīn means clay; ṭānahu or ṭāmahu means God formed or created someone with a given nature, with n/m interchange.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r12.anchor: الطين: معروف، ويقال طانه الله على كذا، وطامه بإبدال النون ميما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r13.claim: Muṭīn is the nickname of a well-known hadith transmitter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r13.anchor: جبله وخلقه على كذا، ومطين لقب لمحدث معروف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r1.claim: One view takes rasūlan in its apparent sense, “a messenger”; another takes it as a verbal noun meaning “a message,” with al-Ḥūfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowing that gloss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r1.anchor: فقيل: هو وصف بمعنى المرسل على ظاهر ما يفهم منه. وقيل: هو مصدر بمعنى رسالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r2.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r2.claim: On the verbal-noun reading, al-Ḥūfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ connect rasūlan to al-kitāb, so God's teaching includes a message to the Children of Israel; Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows a circumstantial parse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r2.anchor: وممن جوز ذلك فيه هنا الحوفي، وأبو البقاء، وقالا: هو معطوف على الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r3.claim: One parse supplies an omitted verb, “and makes him a messenger,” since rasūlan cannot share the earlier governing verb; a cited poem similarly supplies “holding” for a second object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r3.anchor: أن يكون منصوبا بإضمار فعل تقديره: ويجعله رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r4.claim: Another parse coordinates rasūlan with ويعلمه as a circumstantial accusative, meaning that He teaches him Scripture while making him a messenger; this depends on the debated parsing of ويعلمه.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r4.anchor: أن يكون معطوفا على: ويعلمه، فيكون: حالا، إذ التقدير: ومعلما الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya also makes rasūlan a circumstantial accusative coordinated with “as a child and adult,” but Abū Ḥayyān calls the long separation very remote.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r5.anchor: أن يكون منصوبا على الحال من الضمير المستكن في: ويكلم، فيكون معطوفا على قوله: وكهلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r6.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash treats the wāw as extra and rasūlan as a circumstantial accusative from the pronoun in ويعلمه; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this as unsupported extra wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r6.anchor: أن تكون الواو زائدة، ويكون حالا من ضمير: ويعلمه، قاله الأخفش، وهو ضعيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r7.claim: A final parse supplies “I sent” in Jesus's speech, governing rasūlan; al-Zamakhsharī calls it difficult because it requires omitted speech and verb, and Abū Ḥayyān finds that omission needless.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p160/r7.anchor: أن يكون منصوبا على إضمار فعل من لفظ رسول، ويكون ذلك الفعل معمولا لقول من عيسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r1.claim: Of five parses for ورسولا, Abu Hayyan prefers an omitted verb indicated by the sense: and He makes him a messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r1.anchor: فهذه خمسة أوجه في إعراب: ورسولا، أولاها الأول، إذ ليس فيه إلا إضمار فعل يدل عليه المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r2.claim: On the public reading, أني قد جئتكم is governed by رسول; with the anomalous kasra, it depends on an omitted verb of saying.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r2.anchor: ويكون قوله أني قد جئتكم معمولا لرسول، أي ناطقا بأني قد جئتكم، على قراءة الجمهور، ومعمولا لقول محذوف على قراءة من كسر الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r3.claim: The Kufan analysis allows ورسولا to introduce quoted speech because it carries the sense of saying.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون محكيا بقوله: ورسولا، لأنه في معنى القول، وذلك على مذهب الكوفيين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r4.speaker: اليزيدي والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r4.claim: Al-Yazīdī reads ورسول in the genitive; al-Zamakhshari links it to بكلمة منه, though Abu Hayyan calls this weak by analogy due to the long separation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r4.anchor: وقرأ اليزيدي: ورسول، بالجر، وخرجه الزمخشري على أنه معطوف على: بكلمة منه، وهي قراءة شاذة في القياس لطول البعد بين المعطوف عليه والمعطوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r6.claim: An unattributed historical account says Jesus's mother fled with him to Egypt after his people isolated him; when he said the hidden children would become pigs, they were transformed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r6.anchor: وكان عيسى قد هربت به أمه من قومها إلى مصر حين عزلوا أولادهم، ونهوهم عن مخالطته، وحبسوهم في بيت، فجاء عيسى يطلبهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r7.claim: The account says God directed Mary to return to Syria when Jesus was twelve; revelation came at thirty, his prophethood lasted three years, and God raised him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r7.anchor: فلما بلغ اثنتي عشرة سنة أوحى الله إليها: أن انطلقي إلى الشام، ففعلت حتى إذا بلغ ثلاثين سنة جاءه الوحي على رأس الثلاثين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r8.claim: The source names Joseph as the first Israelite prophet, with Moses also proposed, and Jesus as the last.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r8.anchor: وكان أول أنبياء بني إسرائيل: يوسف، وقيل: موسى، وآخرهم عيسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the sign clause through مستقيم as governed by ورسولا and included in the earlier speech addressed to Mary, announcing Jesus's teaching, mission, and miracles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p161/r9.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: أني قد جئتكم بآية إلى قوله مستقيم متعلق بقوله ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل ومعمول له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r2.claim: Another parse ends the sentence at رسولًا إلى بني إسرائيل; the sign statement is not part of the preceding speech, and an arrival clause is understood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r2.anchor: وقيل: يحتمل أن يكون الكلام تم عند قوله ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل ولا يكون أني قد جئتكم متعلقا بما قبله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r3.speaker: الجمهور وعبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r3.claim: The majority reading has the singular آية in both places; ʿAbd Allah's codex has the plural بآيات in both.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بأنه، على الإفراد، وكذلك في وجئتكم بآية من ربكم وفي مصحف عبد الله: بآيات، على الجمع في الموضعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r4.claim: من ربكم may modify آية as an adjective through an omitted phrase or attach to جئتكم, meaning I came from your Lord with a sign.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون: من ربكم، في موضع الصفة، لأنه يتعلق بمحذوف، ويجوز أن يتعلق: بجئتكم، أي: جئتكم من ربكم بآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r5.claim: The public fatḥa on أني permits parses as an apposition to آية or to أني قد جئتكم, or as predicate of an omitted هي.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r5.anchor: قرأ الجمهور: أني أخلق، بفتح الهمزة على أن يكون بدلا من: آية، فيكون في موضع جر، أو بدلا من قوله: أني قد جئتكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r6.speaker: نافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r6.claim: Nāfiʿ reads the hamza in أني with kasra, taking it as a new sentence, an implicit quotation, or an explanation of the sign.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r6.anchor: وقرأ نافع بالكسر على الاستئناف، أو على إضمار القول، أو على التفسير للآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r7.claim: خلق may mean create and bring an entity from absolute nonexistence, which belongs only to God, or estimate and shape, as in a craft.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r7.anchor: ومعنى: أخلق: أقدر وأهيء، والخلق يكون بمعنى الإنشاء وإبراز العين من العدم الصرف إلى الوجود. وهذا لا يكون إلا لله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r8.claim: The source cites Qur'anic uses where خلق means shaping or estimating, including making falsehood and God as best estimators.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r8.anchor: وتخلقون إفكا ومما جاء الخلق فيه بمعنى التقدير قوله تعالى: فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r9.claim: A poet's line uses خلق for what one fashions or estimates, distinguishing a maker who finishes his work from one who does not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p162/r9.anchor: وقال الشاعر: ولأنت تفري ما خلقت ... وبعض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r1.claim: The lām in لكم expresses purpose; من الطين limits the source material, showing that Jesus shapes a form rather than creates from nothing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r1.anchor: واللام في: لكم، معناها التعليل، و: من الطين، تقييد بأنه لا يوجد من العدم الصرف، بل ذكر المادة التي يشكل منها صورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r2.speaker: الزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads كهيئة as كهية, with a kasra on hāʾ and doubled open yāʾ before the feminine ending.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r2.anchor: وقرأ الزهري: كهية، بكسر الهاء وياء مشددة مفتوحة بعدها تاء التأنيث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r3.claim: Abu al-Hasan treats the kāf as a noun and object of أخلق; most grammarians make it an adjective of an omitted object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r3.anchor: و: الكاف، من: كهيئة، اسم على مذهب أبي الحسن، فهي مفعولة: بأخلق، وعلى قول الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر بن القعقاع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ reads الطائر instead of الطير, using the singular for the species.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: الطير، وقرأ أبو جعفر بن القعقاع: كهيئة الطائر، والمراد به الجنس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r5.claim: The pronoun in فيه can return to the kāf or, under the alternative parsing, to the omitted object it describes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r5.anchor: الضمير في: فيه، يعود على: الكاف، أو على موصوفها على القولين المذكورين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r6.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r6.claim: A noncanonical reading has فأنفخها; its feminine pronoun refers to omitted هيئة or semantically to the kāf, and Abu Hayyan notes a deleted preposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r6.anchor: وقرأ بعض القراء: فأنفخها، أعاد الضمير على الهيئة المحذوفة، إذ يكون التقدير: هيئة كهيئة الطير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r7.claim: Al-Nābigha's verse shows نفخ taking a direct object; the construction may omit a preposition or use تضمين, with يكون read as complete or as become.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r7.anchor: وقال النابغة: كالهبرقي تنحى ينفخ الفحما فعدى: نفخ، لمنصوب، فيمكن أن يكون على إسقاط حرف الجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r8.speaker: نافع ويعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read طائرا here and in 5:110; the others read طيرا. طائر is the predicate of يكون, while making يكون complete and طائرا circumstantial is judged far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r8.anchor: وقرأ نافع ويعقوب هنا وفي المائدة: طائرا، وقرأ الباقون: طيرا، وانتصابه على أنه خبر: يكون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r9.claim: بإذن الله may attach to يكون or طائرا; permission means God's enabling and knowing that Jesus performs the act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r9.anchor: وتعلق بإذن الله، قيل: بيكون. وقيل: بطائر، ومعنى: بإذن الله، أي بتمكينه وعلمه بأني أفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r10.claim: Jesus's modeling and blowing display his connection to the miracle, but God alone creates life in the clay form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r10.anchor: وتعاطي عيسى التصوير بيده والنفخ في تلك الصورة تبيين لتلبسه بالمعجزة، وتوضيح أنها من قبله، وأما خلق الحياة في تلك الصورة الطينية فمن الله وحده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r11.claim: The bird miracle apparently was not a response to a demand; another report says the Israelites demanded a bat to test him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r11.anchor: وظاهر الآية يدل على أن خلقه لذلك لم يكن باقتراح منهم، بل هذه الخوارق جاءت تفسيرا لقوله: أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم وقيل: كان ذلك باقتراح منهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r12.claim: The proposed bat was said to be unusually complete, with breasts, teeth, ears, an udder, restricted twilight vision, laughter, featherless flight, menstruation, and birth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p163/r12.anchor: وخصوا الخفاش لأنه عجيب الخلق، وهو أكمل الطير خلقا، له: ثدي، وأسنان، وآذان، وضرع، يخرج منه اللبن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r1.claim: A report from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says Jesus asked what the people wanted; they requested a bat, called the hardest bird to make because it flies without feathers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r1.anchor: روي عن أبي سعيد الخدري: أنه قال لهم: ماذا تريدون؟ قالوا: الخفاش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r2.claim: Some said Jesus first made the bat while studying with his teacher; exegetes report that it flew while watched, then died when unseen, yet Israelites called Jesus a sorcerer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r2.anchor: ويقال: فعل ذلك أولا وهو مع معلمه في الكتاب، وتواطأ النقل عن المفسرين أن الطائر الذي خلقه عيسى كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r3.claim: Mujāhid explains الأكمه as a person with night blindness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r4.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r4.claim: ʿIkrima explains الأكمه as someone with weak eyesight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الأكمه هو الأعشى. وقال عكرمة: هو الأعمش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains الأكمه as one born blind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هو الذي ولد أعمى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r6.claim: Another view identifies the person as one whose eye was erased; it adds that the only such person in this community was Qatāda ibn Diʿāma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو الممسوح العين، ولم يكن في هذه الأمة أكمه غير قتادة بن دعامة السدوسي صاحب التفسير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Hasan, and al-Suddī take الأكمه to mean a blind person generally.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والحسن، والسدي: هو الأعمى على الإطلاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r8.speaker: النقاش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r8.claim: Al-Naqqāsh reports a figurative explanation: الأكمه is mute, unable to understand or be understood, with a dead heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r8.anchor: وحكى النقاش: أن الأكمه هو الأبكم الذي لا يفهم ولا يفهم، الميت الفؤاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda define الأكمه as one born blind with closed eyes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا، وقتادة: هو الذي يولد أعمى مضموم العينين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r10.claim: Jesus healed by supplication and touch, but only cures beyond physicians' ability establish prophethood as extraordinary; curing weak sight is ordinary, while restoring an erased eye is more striking.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r10.anchor: قيل: وقد كان عيسى يبرىء بدعائه، والمسح بيده، كل علة. ولكن لا يقوم الحجة على بني إسرائيل في معنى النبوة إلا بالإبراء من العلل التي يعجز عن إبرائها الأطباء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r11.claim: A report says as many as fifty thousand sick people gathered around Jesus; those able came to him, and he went to those unable to come, healing by prayer alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r11.anchor: روي أنه ربما اجتمع عليه خمسون ألفا من المرضى، من أطاق منهم أتاه، ومن لم يطق أتاه عيسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r12.claim: Blindness and leprosy are named because they resist ordinary cure; since medicine prevailed in Jesus's age, his sign met that expertise, as Moses met magic and Arabs eloquence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p164/r12.anchor: وخص بالذكر الكمه والبرص لأنهما داآن معضلان لا يقدر على الإبراء منهما، إلا الله تعالى، وكان الغالب على زمان عيسى الطب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p169/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p169/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p169/r12.claim: The source notes repetition in جئتكم بآية, أني أخلق لكم, الطير, بإذن الله, ربي وربكم, and بما تأكلون وما.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p169/r12.anchor: والتكرار: في: جئتكم بآية. وفي: أني أخلق لكم. وفي: الطير، وفي: بإذن الله، وفي: ربي وربكم، وفي: ما، في قوله: بما تأكلون وما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p169/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p169/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p169/r13.claim: The singular is used to express a collective in الآية, الأكمه والأبرص, and إذا قضى أمرا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p169/r13.anchor: والتعبير عن الجمع بالمفرد في: الآية، وفي: الأكمه والأبرص، وفي: إذا قضى أمرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p171/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p171/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p171/r1.claim: The passage uses antithesis between reviving and the dead, and between permitting and prohibiting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p171/r1.anchor: والطباق في: وأحيي الموتى، وفي: لأحل وحرم

DAMGHANI:v1p150/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r5.claim: Jesus’ raising the dead by God’s permission was a sign for the Children of Israel before the Resurrection, without lasting worldly life or sustenance.
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r5.anchor: الخامس : الإحياء للعبرة قبل يوم القيامة من غير رزق ولا أثر في الدنيا قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

DAMGHANI:v1p150/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r6.claim: Dāmghānī says Jesus raised Sam son of Noah, who spoke to the people and then died again as before.
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r6.anchor: فأحيا سام بن نوح وكلم الناس ووقع ميتا فكان كما كان
